manifest.title: Tree algebras and bisimulation-invariant MSO on finite graphs

inputs.abstract:
This submission formalizes Theorem 2 of the revised manuscript of
13 November 2026: over a finite proposition alphabet, the bisimulation-invariant
fragment of monadic second-order logic on finite reachable transition systems
is exactly the modal $\mu$-calculus. Both implications and their supporting
proof network are proved. The algebraic construction uses finite ranked
systems, yield-syntactic set-algebras, and unfold-automata.

The submission also provides a total executable MSO-to-$\mu$ translation
with correctness under the finite bisimulation-invariance promise.
Explicit algebra, profile, word-automaton and finite-model bounds justify
its exhaustive finite search.

concepts.title: Acceptance through resolution values
concepts.description:
For a language recognized by an unfolding-invariant algebra, universal yield
acceptance is exactly containment of both initial and root observation values
in the accepting set of the algebra.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PresentationObservations
import Lax369799.FiniteAcceptance

/-!
---
title: Acceptance through resolution values
type: theorem
---
For a language recognized by an unfolding-invariant algebra, universal yield
acceptance is exactly containment of both initial and root observation values
in the accepting set of the algebra.
-/
namespace Lax369799.AcceptanceObservations
open RankedSystems Algebras PresentationObservations

axiom accepting_iff_values {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (hE : UnfoldInvariant E)
    (η : RankedMap A B) (F : Set (B 0)) (L : Language A) (hL : Recognizes E η F L)
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : Presentation A 0 V) :
    SyntacticOrder.Accepting L (trim G) ↔
      values E η G ⊆ F ∧ values E η (RootExpansion.startAtRoots G) ⊆ F

end Lax369799.AcceptanceObservations

statements.signature:
accepting_iff_values : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B),
  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariant E →
    ∀ (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B) (F : Set (B 0)) (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A),
      Lax369799.Algebras.Recognizes E η F L →
        ∀ {V : Type} [inst : Fintype V] (G : Lax369799.RankedSystems.Presentation A 0 V),
          Iff (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L (Lax369799.RankedSystems.trim G))
            (And (Set.instLE.le (Lax369799.PresentationObservations.values E η G) F)
              (Set.instLE.le (Lax369799.PresentationObservations.values E η (Lax369799.RootExpansion.startAtRoots G))
                F))

concepts.title: Acceptance and the syntactic preorder
concepts.description:
Acceptance is invariant under unfolding. On deterministic systems it
agrees with membership in the original unfold-invariant language. The
syntactic preorder reverses morphisms and preserves acceptance on closed
systems, so acceptance descends to the syntactic quotient.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SyntacticOrder

/-!
---
title: Acceptance and the syntactic preorder
type: theorem
---
Acceptance is invariant under unfolding. On deterministic systems it
agrees with membership in the original unfold-invariant language. The
syntactic preorder reverses morphisms and preserves acceptance on closed
systems, so acceptance descends to the syntactic quotient.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AcceptanceTheorems
open RankedSystems Morphisms Algebras SyntacticOrder

axiom yield_sum {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T U : SetSystem A n) :
    Yield (sum S T) U ↔ Yield S U ∨ Yield T U

axiom accepting_sum {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A) (S T : SetSystem A 0) :
    Accepting L (sum S T) ↔ Accepting L S ∧ Accepting L T

axiom accepting_system {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A)
    (hL : UnfoldInvariantLanguage L) (S : System A 0) :
    Accepting L S.val ↔ S ∈ L

axiom accepting_unfold {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A)
    (S T : SetSystem A 0) (h : UnfoldEquivalent S T) :
    Accepting L S ↔ Accepting L T

axiom syntactic_morphism {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A) {n : ℕ}
    {S T : SetSystem A n} (f : Morphism S T) : SyntacticBelow L T S

axiom syntactic_acceptance {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A)
    {S T : SetSystem A 0} (h : SyntacticBelow L S T) :
    Accepting L S → Accepting L T

axiom accepting_plant {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A) (S : SetSystem A 0) :
    Accepting L (plant S) ↔ Accepting L S

end Lax369799.AcceptanceTheorems

statements.signature:
accepting_plant : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A)
  (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A 0),
  Iff (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L (Lax369799.RankedSystems.plant S)) (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L S)

accepting_sum : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A)
  (S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A 0),
  Iff (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L (Lax369799.RankedSystems.sum S T))
    (And (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L S) (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L T))

accepting_system : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A),
  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariantLanguage L →
    ∀ (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A 0),
      Iff (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L S.val) (Set.instMembership.mem L S)

accepting_unfold : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A)
  (S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A 0),
  Lax369799.Morphisms.UnfoldEquivalent S T →
    Iff (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L S) (Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L T)

syntactic_acceptance : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A)
  {S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A 0},
  Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.SyntacticBelow L S T →
    Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L S → Lax369799.SyntacticOrder.Accepting L T

yield_sum : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat} (S T U : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A n),
  Iff (Lax369799.Morphisms.Yield (Lax369799.RankedSystems.sum S T) U)
    (Or (Lax369799.Morphisms.Yield S U) (Lax369799.Morphisms.Yield T U))

concepts.title: A common condition for finite and infinite algebraic branch words
concepts.description:
The word condition of Section 6.3 combines terminating-word evaluation
with the linked-pair condition on infinite words. Both conditions are
realized by one finite deterministic parity word automaton with final
states for terminating words.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords
import Lax369799.CombinedWordCondition

/-!
---
title: A common condition for finite and infinite algebraic branch words
type: theorem
---
The word condition of Section 6.3 combines terminating-word evaluation
with the linked-pair condition on infinite words. Both conditions are
realized by one finite deterministic parity word automaton with final
states for terminating words.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AlgebraicBranchCondition
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FiniteSyntacticAlgebra UnfoldAutomata

axiom exists_condition {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0))
    [Fintype (A 1)] [Fintype (A 0)] :
    ∃ D : WordCondition (Fintype.card (A 1)) (Fintype.card (A 0)),
      (∀ w a, D.AcceptsFinite w a ↔
        FiniteBranchWords.value E (w.map (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm)
          ((Fintype.equivFin (A 0)).symm a) ∈ F) ∧
      (∀ w, D.AcceptsInfinite w ↔
        AlgebraicOmegaWords.Accepts E F (fun n => (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (w n)))

end Lax369799.AlgebraicBranchCondition

statements.signature:
exists_condition : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0))
  [inst : Fintype (A 1)] [inst_1 : Fintype (A 0)],
  Exists fun D =>
    And
      (∀ (w : List (Fin (Fintype.card (A 1)))) (a : Fin (Fintype.card (A 0))),
        Iff (D.AcceptsFinite w a)
          (Set.instMembership.mem F
            (Lax369799.FiniteBranchWords.value E (List.map (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm) w)
              (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe (Fintype.equivFin (A 0)).symm a))))
      (∀ (w : Nat → Fin (Fintype.card (A 1))),
        Iff (D.AcceptsInfinite w)
          (Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords.Accepts E F fun n =>
            EquivLike.toFunLike.coe (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (w n)))

concepts.title: Algebraic decomposition with boundary data
concepts.description:
Remove the hole symbol from each unary piece and evaluate its reachable
part. The resulting unary values, together with the planted hole mark
and its self-loop directions, give the planted normal context used in
the extremal construction. Its evaluation agrees with the planted
original context for every atomic argument.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ContextDecomposition
import Lax369799.ExtremalContexts

/-!
---
title: Algebraic decomposition with boundary data
type: theorem
---
Remove the hole symbol from each unary piece and evaluate its reachable
part. The resulting unary values, together with the planted hole mark
and its self-loop directions, give the planted normal context used in
the extremal construction. Its evaluation agrees with the planted
original context for every atomic argument.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AlgebraicDecomposition
open RankedSystems Flattening SetAlgebras ContextDecomposition

/-- The label of a non-hole vertex is an ordinary letter of the same rank. -/
noncomputable def ordinaryLetter {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0)
    (v : BodyVertex C) :
    {a : A (C.system.graph.label v.val).1 // (C.system.graph.label v.val).2 = Sum.inl a} := by
  cases h : (C.system.graph.label v.val).2 with
  | inl a => exact ⟨a, rfl⟩
  | inr hkr =>
    have hv : IsHole (C.system.graph.label v.val) := ⟨hkr, h⟩
    exact False.elim (v.property ((Classical.choose_spec C.one_hole).2 v.val hv))

noncomputable def ordinaryPiece {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0)
    (i : Fin (k + 1)) : Presentation A 1 (BodyVertex C) where
  label := fun v => ⟨(C.system.graph.label v.val).1, (ordinaryLetter C v).val⟩
  initial := (piece C i).initial
  root := (piece C i).root
  edge := (piece C i).edge
  direction_valid := (piece C i).direction_valid

noncomputable def pieceValue {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) {k : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k 0) (i : Fin (k + 1)) : A 1 := by
  classical
  exact E.eval 1 (trim (ordinaryPiece C i))

noncomputable def plantedBoundary {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) :
    ExtremalContexts.Boundary k where
  root := (boundary C).initial ∨ (boundary C).root
  loops := (boundary C).loops

axiom algebraic_decomposition {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) {k : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k 0) (a : A k) :
    E.eval 0 (plug (ExtremalContexts.normalContext (plantedBoundary C) (pieceValue E C)) (atomic a)) =
      E.eval 0 (plant (plug C (atomic a)))

end Lax369799.AlgebraicDecomposition

statements.signature:
algebraic_decomposition : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.SetAlgebras.SetAlgebra A) {k : Nat}
  (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A k 0) (a : A k),
  Eq
    (E.eval 0
      (Lax369799.Flattening.plug
        (Lax369799.ExtremalContexts.normalContext (Lax369799.AlgebraicDecomposition.plantedBoundary C)
          (Lax369799.AlgebraicDecomposition.pieceValue E C))
        (Lax369799.RankedSystems.atomic a)))
    (E.eval 0 (Lax369799.RankedSystems.plant (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C (Lax369799.RankedSystems.atomic a))))

concepts.title: The algebraic condition on infinite branch words
concepts.description:
Section 6.3 accepts an infinite unary word when it belongs to V_a(V_e)^ω
for a linked pair (a,e) whose lasso evaluates to an accepting nullary
value. For a finite unary sort this language is recognized by a finite
deterministic parity word automaton.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.UnaryFactorization
import Lax369799.OmegaProducts

/-!
---
title: The algebraic condition on infinite branch words
type: theorem
---
Section 6.3 accepts an infinite unary word when it belongs to V_a(V_e)^ω
for a linked pair (a,e) whose lasso evaluates to an accepting nullary
value. For a finite unary sort this language is recognized by a finite
deterministic parity word automaton.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FiniteSyntacticAlgebra UnaryComposition UnaryFactorization UnfoldAutomata

def Accepts {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0)) (w : ℕ → A 1) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a e : A 1) (cut : ℕ → ℕ), E.eval 0 (lasso a e) ∈ F ∧
    product E e e = e ∧ product E a e = a ∧ StrictMono cut ∧ 0 < cut 0 ∧
    block E w 0 (cut 0) = a ∧ ∀ i, block E w (cut i) (cut (i + 1)) = e

axiom regular {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0)) [Fintype (A 1)] {z : ℕ} :
    ∃ D : WordCondition (Fintype.card (A 1)) z, ∀ w, D.AcceptsInfinite w ↔
      Accepts E F (fun n => (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (w n))

axiom recurrent_factorization {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0))
    {V : Type} [Finite V] (w : ℕ → A 1) (v : ℕ → V) (h : Accepts E F w) :
    ∃ (a e : A 1) (c : ℕ → ℕ) (r : V), E.eval 0 (lasso a e) ∈ F ∧
      product E e e = e ∧ product E a e = a ∧ StrictMono c ∧ 0 < c 0 ∧
      (∀ i, v (c i) = r) ∧ (∀ i, block E w 0 (c i) = a) ∧
      (∀ i j, i < j → block E w (c i) (c j) = e)

end Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords

statements.signature:
recurrent_factorization : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0)) {V : Type}
  [Finite V] (w : Nat → A 1) (v : Nat → V),
  Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords.Accepts E F w →
    Exists fun a =>
      Exists fun e =>
        Exists fun c =>
          Exists fun r =>
            And (Set.instMembership.mem F (E.eval 0 (Lax369799.UnaryFactorization.lasso a e)))
              (And (Eq (Lax369799.UnaryComposition.product E e e) e)
                (And (Eq (Lax369799.UnaryComposition.product E a e) a)
                  (And (StrictMono c)
                    (And (instLTNat.lt 0 (c 0))
                      (And (∀ (i : Nat), Eq (v (c i)) r)
                        (And (∀ (i : Nat), Eq (Lax369799.UnaryFactorization.block E w 0 (c i)) a)
                          (∀ (i j : Nat),
                            instLTNat.lt i j → Eq (Lax369799.UnaryFactorization.block E w (c i) (c j)) e)))))))

regular : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0))
  [inst : Fintype (A 1)] {z : Nat},
  Exists fun D =>
    ∀ (w : Nat → Fin (Fintype.card (A 1))),
      Iff (D.AcceptsInfinite w)
        (Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords.Accepts E F fun n => EquivLike.toFunLike.coe (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (w n))

concepts.title: Algebraic transition tables for unfold-automata
concepts.description:
Unary and nullary algebra elements serve as edge and leaf types. A
positive-arity transition is allowed precisely when the parallel unary
value lies below the letter value. The automaton property and unary
normal form give an allowed transition preserving acceptance in each
accepting context. The word condition is supplied separately.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.DeterministicElements
import Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata

/-!
---
title: Algebraic transition tables for unfold-automata
type: theorem
---
Unary and nullary algebra elements serve as edge and leaf types. A
positive-arity transition is allowed precisely when the parallel unary
value lies below the letter value. The automaton property and unary
normal form give an allowed transition preserving acceptance in each
accepting context. The word condition is supplied separately.
-/
namespace Lax369799.AlgebraicTransitions
open RankedSystems SetAlgebras AutomatonProperty UnfoldAutomata

noncomputable def decodeTypes {B : RankedSet} [Fintype (B 1)] {n : ℕ}
    (b : Fin n → Fin (Fintype.card (B 1))) : Fin n → B 1 :=
  fun i => (Fintype.equivFin (B 1)).symm (b i)

noncomputable def automaton {A B : RankedSet} [Fintype (B 1)] [Fintype (B 0)]
    (E : SetAlgebra B) (η : RankedMap A B)
    (D : WordCondition (Fintype.card (B 1)) (Fintype.card (B 0))) : UnfoldAutomaton A where
  unary := Fintype.card (B 1)
  nullary := Fintype.card (B 0)
  transition := fun n a => {b | Below E
    (E.eval (n + 1) (DeterministicElements.parallel (decodeTypes b))) (η (n + 1) a)}
  leafTransition := fun a => {(Fintype.equivFin (B 0)) (η 0 a)}
  condition := D

axiom accepting_transition {A B : RankedSet} [Fintype (B 1)] [Fintype (B 0)]
    (E : SetAlgebra B) (f : B 0) (hE : HasAutomatonProperty E f) (η : RankedMap A B)
    (D : WordCondition (Fintype.card (B 1)) (Fintype.card (B 0)))
    (n : ℕ) (a : A (n + 1)) (C : Flattening.SetContext B (n + 1) 0)
    (h : Below E f (E.eval 0 (Flattening.plug C (atomic (η (n + 1) a))))) :
    ∃ b ∈ (automaton E η D).transition n a,
      Below E f (E.eval 0 (Flattening.plug C
        (atomic (E.eval (n + 1) (DeterministicElements.parallel (decodeTypes b))))))

end Lax369799.AlgebraicTransitions

statements.signature:
accepting_transition : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} [inst : Fintype (B 1)] [inst_1 : Fintype (B 0)]
  (E : Lax369799.SetAlgebras.SetAlgebra B) (f : B 0),
  Lax369799.AutomatonProperty.HasAutomatonProperty E f →
    ∀ (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B)
      (D : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition (Fintype.card (B 1)) (Fintype.card (B 0))) (n : Nat)
      (a : A (instHAdd.hAdd n 1)) (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext B (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) 0),
      Lax369799.SetAlgebras.Below E f
          (E.eval 0 (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C (Lax369799.RankedSystems.atomic (η (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) a)))) →
        Exists fun b =>
          And (Set.instMembership.mem ((Lax369799.AlgebraicTransitions.automaton E η D).transition n a) b)
            (Lax369799.SetAlgebras.Below E f
              (E.eval 0
                (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C
                  (Lax369799.RankedSystems.atomic
                    (E.eval (instHAdd.hAdd n 1)
                      (Lax369799.DeterministicElements.parallel (Lax369799.AlgebraicTransitions.decodeTypes b)))))))

concepts.title: Algebras and recognition
concepts.description:
An algebra evaluates systems over its own ranked carrier. Evaluation is
invariant under isomorphism, evaluates atomic systems as their labels, and
commutes with flattening. The explicit isomorphism clause accounts for our
enumeration of finite vertex sets. A regular-tree algebra also identifies
unfold-equivalent systems. A recognising map assigns an algebra element to
each letter; a set of elements of sort zero specifies acceptance.
See Section 3.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.Morphisms
import Lax369799.Flattening

/-!
---
title: Algebras and recognition
type: definition
---
An algebra evaluates systems over its own ranked carrier. Evaluation is
invariant under isomorphism, evaluates atomic systems as their labels, and
commutes with flattening. The explicit isomorphism clause accounts for our
enumeration of finite vertex sets. A regular-tree algebra also identifies
unfold-equivalent systems. A recognising map assigns an algebra element to
each letter; a set of elements of sort zero specifies acceptance.
See Section 3.
-/

namespace Lax369799.Algebras
open RankedSystems Morphisms Flattening

structure Algebra (A : RankedSet) where
  eval : ∀ n, System A n → A n
  isomorphic : ∀ n (S T : System A n), Isomorphic S.val T.val → eval n S = eval n T
  unit : ∀ n (a : A n), eval n (atomicSystem a) = a
  associative : ∀ n (S : System (System A) n) (T : System A n),
    SystemFlattening S T → eval n (relabelSystem eval S) = eval n T

def UnfoldInvariant {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (S T : System A n), UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val → E.eval n S = E.eval n T

abbrev Language (A : RankedSet) := Set (System A 0)

def UnfoldInvariantLanguage {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A) : Prop :=
  ∀ S T, UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val → (S ∈ L ↔ T ∈ L)

def Recognizes {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (η : RankedMap A B)
    (F : Set (B 0)) (L : Language A) : Prop :=
  ∀ T, T ∈ L ↔ E.eval 0 (relabelSystem η T) ∈ F

def Recognizable {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A) : Prop :=
  ∃ (B : RankedSet) (E : Algebra B) (η : RankedMap A B) (F : Set (B 0)),
    RankwiseFinite B ∧ Recognizes E η F L

def RegularTreeRecognizable {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A) : Prop :=
  ∃ (B : RankedSet) (E : Algebra B) (η : RankedMap A B) (F : Set (B 0)),
    RankwiseFinite B ∧ UnfoldInvariant E ∧ Recognizes E η F L

structure AlgebraMorphism {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (F : Algebra B) where
  map : RankedMap A B
  commutes : ∀ n (S : System A n), F.eval n (relabelSystem map S) = map n (E.eval n S)

end Lax369799.Algebras

concepts.title: Rankwise-finite recognition implies automaton recognition
concepts.description:
An unfold-invariant language of systems recognised by a rankwise-finite
algebra is recognised by an unfold-automaton. This is `thm:alg2aut` in
Section 6.3. The recognising algebra in the hypothesis is not assumed to
be unfold-invariant; unfold-invariance is a property of the language.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SupportedAlgebras
import Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata

/-!
---
title: Rankwise-finite recognition implies automaton recognition
type: theorem
---
An unfold-invariant language of systems recognised by a rankwise-finite
algebra is recognised by an unfold-automaton. This is `thm:alg2aut` in
Section 6.3. The recognising algebra in the hypothesis is not assumed to
be unfold-invariant; unfold-invariance is a property of the language.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AlgebraToAutomaton
open RankedSystems Algebras UnfoldAutomata

axiom algebra_to_automaton {A : RankedSet} (L : Language A)
    (hL : UnfoldInvariantLanguage L) (hA : SupportedAlgebras.Recognizable L) :
    ∃ M : UnfoldAutomaton A, UnfoldAutomata.Recognizes M L

end Lax369799.AlgebraToAutomaton

statements.signature:
algebra_to_automaton : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A),
  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariantLanguage L →
    Lax369799.SupportedAlgebras.Recognizable L → Exists fun M => Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.Recognizes M L

concepts.title: Bisimulation-invariant algebraic recognition implies mu-calculus definability
concepts.description:
A bisimulation-invariant language over the transition alphabet recognised
by a rankwise-finite algebra is definable by a modal mu-calculus sentence
on its decoded transition systems. This is `thm:alg2mu` in Section 6.4.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SupportedAlgebras
import Lax369799.Algebras
import Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus
import Lax369799.TransitionEncoding

/-!
---
title: Bisimulation-invariant algebraic recognition implies mu-calculus definability
type: theorem
---
A bisimulation-invariant language over the transition alphabet recognised
by a rankwise-finite algebra is definable by a modal mu-calculus sentence
on its decoded transition systems. This is `thm:alg2mu` in Section 6.4.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AlgebraToMuCalculus
open RankedSystems Algebras TransitionEncoding

axiom algebra_to_mu {P : Type} [Finite P] (L : Language (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (hL : ∀ S T, RankedBisimilar S T → (S ∈ L ↔ T ∈ L))
    (hA : SupportedAlgebras.Recognizable L) :

concepts.title: Deterministic elements and the earlier replacement property
concepts.description:
An element is deterministic if it is the value of a set-system using only
letters of ranks zero and one. Given a rank-zero element f, the automaton
property says that an element in an accepting context can be replaced by
a deterministic element below it while preserving acceptance above f.
This is the earlier replacement interface. The revised manuscript's
Definition 90 requires canonical direction decomposition and regular-branch
acceptance as well; its syntactic instance is in ExtremalPaths.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SyntacticOrder

/-!
---
title: Deterministic elements and the earlier replacement property
type: definition
---
An element is deterministic if it is the value of a set-system using only
letters of ranks zero and one. Given a rank-zero element f, the automaton
property says that an element in an accepting context can be replaced by
a deterministic element below it while preserving acceptance above f.
This is the earlier replacement interface. The revised manuscript's
Definition 90 requires canonical direction decomposition and regular-branch
acceptance as well; its syntactic instance is in ExtremalPaths.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AutomatonProperty
open RankedSystems Flattening SetAlgebras

def Deterministic {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) {n : ℕ} (a : A n) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : SetSystem A n, (∀ v, (S.graph.label v).1 ≤ 1) ∧ E.eval n S = a

def HasAutomatonProperty {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) (f : A 0) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (C : SetContext A n 0) (a : A n), Below E f (E.eval 0 (plug C (atomic a))) →
    ∃ δ : A n, Deterministic E δ ∧ Below E δ a ∧
      Below E f (E.eval 0 (plug C (atomic δ)))

def PlantInvariant {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) (f : A 0) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : SetSystem A 0, Below E f (E.eval 0 S) ↔ Below E f (E.eval 0 (plant S))

def OrderSeparating {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) (f : A 0) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (a b : A n),
    (∀ C : SetContext A n 0,
      Below E f (E.eval 0 (plug C (atomic a))) →
      Below E f (E.eval 0 (plug C (atomic b)))) → Below E a b

end Lax369799.AutomatonProperty

concepts.title: Accepting runs and modal game plays
concepts.description:
Every accepting run supplies winning modal choices. Finite branches use
the final-state test, while infinite branches use the parity condition.
Inserting zero-priority marking positions between word positions does
not alter the acceptance condition.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame

/-!
---
title: Accepting runs and modal game plays
type: theorem
---
Every accepting run supplies winning modal choices. Finite branches use
the final-state test, while infinite branches use the parity condition.
Inserting zero-priority marking positions between word positions does
not alter the acceptance condition.
-/

namespace Lax369799.AutomatonRunGame
open TransitionEncoding TransitionSystems UnfoldAutomata ModalAcceptanceGame

axiom parity_interleave {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (S : TransitionSystem P) (w : ℕ → Fin M.unary) (p : ℕ → Vertex M S)
    (he : ∀ n, (game M S).priority (p (2*n)) =
      ceiling M.condition - M.condition.priority (M.condition.run w n))
    (ho : ∀ n, (game M S).priority (p (2*n+1)) = 0) :
    M.condition.AcceptsInfinite w ↔ (game M S).EveWins p

axiom run_winning {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    {S : RankedSystems.System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0} (r : Run M S) (hr : r.Accepting) :
    ParityWinningRegions.Winning (game M (decode S)) true
      (position M.condition.initial (decode S).initial)

end Lax369799.AutomatonRunGame

  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (w : Nat → Fin M.unary)
  (p : Nat → Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.Vertex M S),
  (∀ (n : Nat),
      Eq ((Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S).priority (p (instHMul.hMul 2 n)))
        (instHSub.hSub (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.ceiling M.condition)
          (M.condition.priority (M.condition.run w n)))) →
    (∀ (n : Nat), Eq ((Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S).priority (p (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 2 n) 1))) 0) →
      Iff (M.condition.AcceptsInfinite w) ((Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S).EveWins p)

  (r : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.Run M S),
  r.Accepting →
    Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning

      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.decode S).initial)

concepts.title: Clone-automata
concepts.description:
An unfold-automaton over the transition alphabet is a clone-automaton when
its transitions are closed under uniformly duplicating every component a
positive number of times. Thus a transition of arity n with types
(b₁,…,bₙ) entails a transition of arity nm with m consecutive copies of
each bᵢ. Nullary transitions are unchanged. This is the duplication
condition of Section 6.4; it is distinct from invariance of the recognised
language.
The identifier IsBisimAutomaton is retained from the earlier development;
it expresses the clone condition of the revised Section 6.4.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata
import Lax369799.TransitionEncoding
import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Basic

/-!
---
title: Clone-automata
type: definition
---
An unfold-automaton over the transition alphabet is a clone-automaton when
its transitions are closed under uniformly duplicating every component a
positive number of times. Thus a transition of arity n with types
(b₁,…,bₙ) entails a transition of arity nm with m consecutive copies of
each bᵢ. Nullary transitions are unchanged. This is the duplication
condition of Section 6.4; it is distinct from invariance of the recognised
language.
The identifier IsBisimAutomaton is retained from the earlier development;
it expresses the clone condition of the revised Section 6.4.
-/

namespace Lax369799.BisimAutomata
open RankedSystems Algebras UnfoldAutomata TransitionEncoding

def Duplicate {H : Type} {n m : ℕ} (b : Fin n → H) : Fin (n * m) → H :=
  fun i => b i.divNat

def IsBisimAutomaton {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ν : Set P) (n : ℕ) (b : Fin (n + 1) → Fin M.unary),
    b ∈ M.transition n ν → ∀ m, 0 < m →
      ∃ (k : ℕ) (h : (n + 1) * m = k + 1),
        (fun i => Duplicate b (Fin.cast h.symm i)) ∈ M.transition k ν

end Lax369799.BisimAutomata

concepts.title: Clone-automaton normal form and modal translation
concepts.description:
A bisimulation-invariant language recognised by a rankwise-finite algebra
has a recognising clone-automaton (Lemma 108, Section 6.4).
The modal translation identifies the acceptance of such an automaton with
a mu-calculus sentence when its recognised language is bisimulation-invariant.
The latter hypothesis is explicit: the duplication condition alone does
not assert language invariance.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SupportedAlgebras
import Lax369799.BisimAutomata
import Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus

/-!
---
title: Clone-automaton normal form and modal translation
type: theorem
---
A bisimulation-invariant language recognised by a rankwise-finite algebra
has a recognising clone-automaton (Lemma 108, Section 6.4).
The modal translation identifies the acceptance of such an automaton with
a mu-calculus sentence when its recognised language is bisimulation-invariant.
The latter hypothesis is explicit: the duplication condition alone does
not assert language invariance.
-/

namespace Lax369799.BisimAutomatonTheorem
open RankedSystems Algebras UnfoldAutomata TransitionEncoding BisimAutomata

axiom bisim_automaton_exists {P : Type} [Finite P]
    (L : Language (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (hL : ∀ S T, RankedBisimilar S T → (S ∈ L ↔ T ∈ L))
    (hA : SupportedAlgebras.Recognizable L) :
    ∃ M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P),
      IsBisimAutomaton M ∧ UnfoldAutomata.Recognizes M L

/-- The clone automaton admits an accepting run on each accepted presentation. -/
axiom bisim_automaton_runs {P : Type} [Finite P]
    (L : Language (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (hL : ∀ S T, RankedBisimilar S T → (S ∈ L ↔ T ∈ L))
    (hA : SupportedAlgebras.Recognizable L) :
    ∃ M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P),
      IsBisimAutomaton M ∧ UnfoldAutomata.Recognizes M L ∧
        ∀ S ∈ L, ∃ r : Run M S, r.Accepting

axiom bisim_automaton_to_mu {P : Type} [Finite P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (hM : IsBisimAutomaton M)
    (hL : ∀ S T, RankedBisimilar S T → (Accepts M S ↔ Accepts M T)) :
    ∃ φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P, ∀ S,
      Accepts M S ↔ ModalMuCalculus.Models (decode S) φ

end Lax369799.BisimAutomatonTheorem

concepts.title: Quotients of graphs by vertex bisimilarity
concepts.description:
Vertex bisimilarity compares labeled graphs without selecting an initial
vertex. On one graph it is an equivalence relation. The quotient graph
has a functional bisimulation from the original graph, with successor
lifting. These quotients support the converse ranked encoding theorem.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.TransitionSystems

/-!
---
title: Quotients of graphs by vertex bisimilarity
type: theorem
---
Vertex bisimilarity compares labeled graphs without selecting an initial
vertex. On one graph it is an equivalence relation. The quotient graph
has a functional bisimulation from the original graph, with successor
lifting. These quotients support the converse ranked encoding theorem.
-/
namespace Lax369799.BisimulationQuotient

structure Graph (P V : Type) where
  edge : V → V → Prop
  valuation : V → Set P

structure BisimulationMap {P V W : Type} (G : Graph P V) (H : Graph P W) where
  toFun : V → W
  valuation : ∀ v, G.valuation v = H.valuation (toFun v)
  forward : ∀ v w, G.edge v w → H.edge (toFun v) (toFun w)
  backward : ∀ v w, H.edge (toFun v) w → ∃ v', G.edge v v' ∧ toFun v' = w

def IsBisimulation {P V W : Type} (G : Graph P V) (H : Graph P W)
    (R : V → W → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ v w, R v w → G.valuation v = H.valuation w ∧
    (∀ v', G.edge v v' → ∃ w', H.edge w w' ∧ R v' w') ∧
    (∀ w', H.edge w w' → ∃ v', G.edge v v' ∧ R v' w')

def Related {P V W : Type} (G : Graph P V) (H : Graph P W) (v : V) (w : W) : Prop :=
  ∃ R, IsBisimulation G H R ∧ R v w

abbrev Carrier {P V : Type} (G : Graph P V) := Quot (Related G G)

def quotient {P V : Type} (G : Graph P V) : Graph P (Carrier G) where
  valuation := Quot.lift G.valuation (by
    rintro v w ⟨R, hR, h⟩
    exact (hR v w h).1)
  edge := fun q r => ∃ v w, Quot.mk (Related G G) v = q ∧
    Quot.mk (Related G G) w = r ∧ G.edge v w

axiom related_equivalence {P V : Type} (G : Graph P V) : Equivalence (Related G G)

axiom quotient_projection {P V : Type} (G : Graph P V) :
    ∃ f : BisimulationMap G (quotient G), f.toFun = Quot.mk (Related G G)

def ofSystem {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) : Graph P S.Vertex :=
  ⟨S.edge, S.valuation⟩

structure SystemMap {P : Type} (S T : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P)
    extends BisimulationMap (ofSystem S) (ofSystem T) where
  initial : toFun S.initial = T.initial

axiom common_quotient {P : Type} (S T : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P)
    (h : TransitionSystems.Bisimilar S T) :
    ∃ U : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P, Nonempty (SystemMap S U) ∧ Nonempty (SystemMap T U)

end Lax369799.BisimulationQuotient

concepts.description:
Initial and root profiles with variable-map fibres bounded by one more than
the size of the unary observing sort determine every closed contextual
acceptance test. Consequently the contextual quotient of finite presentations
is rankwise finite for every regular-tree recognizable language.

/-!
---
title: Bounded profiles refine finite contextual equivalence
type: theorem
---
Initial and root profiles with variable-map fibres bounded by one more than
the size of the unary observing sort determine every closed contextual

is rankwise finite for every regular-tree recognizable language.

concepts.title: Monotonicity of algebraic branch conditions
concepts.description:
Unary application and finite branch evaluation are monotone. For a finite
unary sort, increasing every letter of an accepted infinite word also
preserves acceptance. A common subsequence of factorization cuts compares
the accepting linked pairs. These comparisons underlie the rerouting
construction of Lemma 108.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras
import Lax369799.AlgebraicOmegaWords

/-!
---
title: Monotonicity of algebraic branch conditions
type: theorem
---
Unary application and finite branch evaluation are monotone. For a finite
unary sort, increasing every letter of an accepted infinite word also
preserves acceptance. A common subsequence of factorization cuts compares
the accepting linked pairs. These comparisons underlie the rerouting
construction of Lemma 108.
-/
namespace Lax369799.BranchMonotonicity
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FinitePresentations SetSystemAlgebras UnaryComposition UnaryFactorization

def ConditionMonotone {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    [Fintype (A 1)] [Fintype (A 0)]
    (D : UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition (Fintype.card (A 1)) (Fintype.card (A 0))) : Prop :=
  (∀ w v a b, List.Forall₂ (fun x y => Below E
      ((Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm x) ((Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm y)) w v →
    Below E ((Fintype.equivFin (A 0)).symm a) ((Fintype.equivFin (A 0)).symm b) →
    D.AcceptsFinite w a → D.AcceptsFinite v b) ∧
  (∀ w v, (∀ i, Below E ((Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (w i))
      ((Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (v i))) →
    D.AcceptsInfinite w → D.AcceptsInfinite v)

axiom condition {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) [Fintype (A 1)] [Fintype (A 0)]
    (F : Set (A 0)) (hF : ∀ a b, a ∈ F → Below E a b → b ∈ F)
    (D : UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition (Fintype.card (A 1)) (Fintype.card (A 0)))
    (hD : (∀ w a, D.AcceptsFinite w a ↔
      FiniteBranchWords.value E.toAlgebra (w.map (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm)
        ((Fintype.equivFin (A 0)).symm a) ∈ F) ∧
      (∀ w, D.AcceptsInfinite w ↔ AlgebraicOmegaWords.Accepts E.toAlgebra F
        (fun n => (Fintype.equivFin (A 1)).symm (w n)))) : ConditionMonotone E D

axiom act_mono {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) {n : ℕ}
    {a a' : A 1} {b b' : A n} (ha : Below E a a') (hb : Below E b b') :
    Below E (act E.toAlgebra a b) (act E.toAlgebra a' b')

axiom product_mono {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    {a a' b b' : A 1} (ha : Below E a a') (hb : Below E b b') :
    Below E (product E.toAlgebra a b) (product E.toAlgebra a' b')

axiom block_mono {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    (w v : ℕ → A 1) (h : ∀ i, Below E (w i) (v i)) (i j : ℕ) :
    Below E (block E.toAlgebra w i j) (block E.toAlgebra v i j)

axiom finite_mono {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    {w v : List (A 1)} (h : List.Forall₂ (Below E) w v)
    {a b : A 0} (hab : Below E a b) :
    Below E (FiniteBranchWords.value E.toAlgebra w a)
      (FiniteBranchWords.value E.toAlgebra v b)

axiom block_append {A : RankedSet} (E : FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.Algebra A)
    (w : ℕ → A 1) {i j k : ℕ} (hij : i < j) (hjk : j < k) :
    block E w i k = product E (block E w i j) (block E w j k)

axiom lasso_mono {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A)

concepts.title: Unary types preserving explicit choices
concepts.description:
Selected unary types must preserve the binary choice operation on closed
continuations. This is a necessary restriction for exposing choices as
separate branch tests. It is not asserted of all unary algebra elements.
Finite words of such types preserve choices, and finite expressions built
from them can be tested path by path. Existence of suitable selected types
and extension to cyclic presentations are separate obligations.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.FiniteBranchWords

/-!
---
title: Unary types preserving explicit choices
type: theorem
---
Selected unary types must preserve the binary choice operation on closed
continuations. This is a necessary restriction for exposing choices as
separate branch tests. It is not asserted of all unary algebra elements.
Finite words of such types preserve choices, and finite expressions built
from them can be tested path by path. Existence of suitable selected types
and extension to cyclic presentations are separate obligations.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ChoicePreservingUnary
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FiniteSyntacticAlgebra FiniteBranchWords

def PreservesChoices {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (b : A 1) : Prop :=
  ∀ c d : A 0, act E b (sumValue E c d) = sumValue E (act E b c) (act E b d)

/-- The eligible unary types, retaining their proof of choice preservation. -/
def TypeSet {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) := {b : A 1 // PreservesChoices E b}

inductive Expression (A : RankedSet) where
  | leaf : A 0 → Expression A
  | step : A 1 → Expression A → Expression A
  | choice : Expression A → Expression A → Expression A

def Expression.eval {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) : Expression A → A 0
  | .leaf a => a
  | .step b t => act E b (t.eval E)
  | .choice s t => sumValue E (s.eval E) (t.eval E)

def Expression.Eligible {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) : Expression A → Prop
  | .leaf _ => True
  | .step b t => PreservesChoices E b ∧ t.Eligible E
  | .choice s t => s.Eligible E ∧ t.Eligible E

def Expression.paths {A : RankedSet} : Expression A → List (List (A 1) × A 0)
  | .leaf a => [([], a)]
  | .step b t => t.paths.map (fun p => (b :: p.1, p.2))
  | .choice s t => s.paths ++ t.paths

axiom word_preserves_choices {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A)
    (w : List (A 1)) (hw : ∀ b ∈ w, PreservesChoices E b) (c d : A 0) :
    value E w (sumValue E c d) = sumValue E (value E w c) (value E w d)

axiom finite_branch_test {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (F : Set (A 0))
    (hF : ∀ c d, sumValue E c d ∈ F ↔ c ∈ F ∧ d ∈ F)
    (t : Expression A) (ht : t.Eligible E) :
    t.eval E ∈ F ↔ ∀ p ∈ t.paths, value E p.1 p.2 ∈ F

axiom finite_types {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) [Finite (A 1)] : Finite (TypeSet E)

end Lax369799.ChoicePreservingUnary

  (∀ (c d : A 0),
      Iff (Set.instMembership.mem F (Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.sumValue E c d))
        (And (Set.instMembership.mem F c) (Set.instMembership.mem F d))) →
    ∀ (t : Lax369799.ChoicePreservingUnary.Expression A),
      Lax369799.ChoicePreservingUnary.Expression.Eligible E t →
        Iff (Set.instMembership.mem F (Lax369799.ChoicePreservingUnary.Expression.eval E t))
          (∀ (p : Prod (List (A 1)) (A 0)),
            List.instMembership.mem t.paths p →

    ∀ (c d : A 0),
      Eq (Lax369799.FiniteBranchWords.value E w (Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.sumValue E c d))

concepts.title: Realizing winning clone-automaton strategies
concepts.description:
Duplicate transition components to cover every permitted successor of a
winning marking. The reachable part of this finite strategy construction
is bisimilar to the input system and carries an accepting automaton run.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.AutomatonRunGame

/-!
---
title: Realizing winning clone-automaton strategies
type: theorem
---
Duplicate transition components to cover every permitted successor of a
winning marking. The reachable part of this finite strategy construction
is bisimilar to the input system and carries an accepting automaton run.
-/

namespace Lax369799.CloneGameRun
open TransitionEncoding TransitionSystems UnfoldAutomata ModalAcceptanceGame

axiom winning_run {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (hM : BisimAutomata.IsBisimAutomaton M) (S : TransitionSystem P)
    (hwin : ParityWinningRegions.Winning (game M S) true
      (position M.condition.initial S.initial)) :
    ∃ U : RankedSystems.System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0,
      Bisimilar (decode U) S ∧ ∃ r : Run M U, r.Accepting

end Lax369799.CloneGameRun

  Lax369799.BisimAutomata.IsBisimAutomaton M →
    ∀ (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P),
      Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
          (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial S.initial) →
        Exists fun U =>
          And (Lax369799.TransitionSystems.Bisimilar (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.decode U) S)
            (Exists fun r => r.Accepting)

concepts.title: Refining runs of the clone table
concepts.description:
An accepting run of the recurrent clone table lifts to an accepting run
of the original transition table on a system with isomorphic decoding.
The direction map is surjective, labels increase along every branch,
and the algebraic word condition is monotone.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.CloneTransitions
import Lax369799.BranchMonotonicity

/-!
---
title: Refining runs of the clone table
type: theorem
---
An accepting run of the recurrent clone table lifts to an accepting run
of the original transition table on a system with isomorphic decoding.
The direction map is surjective, labels increase along every branch,
and the algebraic word condition is monotone.
-/
namespace Lax369799.CloneRunRefinement
open RankedSystems (RankedSet System)
open TransitionEncoding UnfoldAutomata SetSystemAlgebras

noncomputable def fromTable {P : Type} {Y : RankedSet} [Fintype (Y 1)] [Fintype (Y 0)]
    (T : Set P → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → Y 1))
    (leaves : Set P → Set (Fin (Fintype.card (Y 0))))
    (D : WordCondition (Fintype.card (Y 1)) (Fintype.card (Y 0))) :
    UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P) where
  unary := Fintype.card (Y 1)
  nullary := Fintype.card (Y 0)
  transition := fun n ν => {b | (fun i => (Fintype.equivFin (Y 1)).symm (b i)) ∈ T ν n}
  leafTransition := leaves
  condition := D

variable {P : Type} {Y : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra Y)
    [Fintype (Y 1)] [Fintype (Y 0)]
    (T : Set P → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → Y 1))
    (leaves : Set P → Set (Fin (Fintype.card (Y 0))))
    (D : WordCondition (Fintype.card (Y 1)) (Fintype.card (Y 0)))
    (S : System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0)
    (r : Run (CloneTransitions.automaton (CloneTransitions.beta E T) leaves D) S)

axiom run_refinement
    (hD : Lax369799.BranchMonotonicity.ConditionMonotone E D) (hr : r.Accepting) :
    ∃ U : System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0, Isomorphic (decode U) (decode S) ∧
      ∃ s : Run (fromTable T leaves D) U, s.Accepting

end Lax369799.CloneRunRefinement

run_refinement : ∀ {P : Type} {Y : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.SetAlgebra Y)
  [inst : Fintype (Y 1)] [inst_1 : Fintype (Y 0)] (T : Set P → (n : Nat) → Set (Fin (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) → Y 1))
  (leaves : Set P → Set (Fin (Fintype.card (Y 0))))
  (D : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition (Fintype.card (Y 1)) (Fintype.card (Y 0)))
  (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P) 0)
  (r :
    Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.Run (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.automaton (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.beta E T) leaves D)
      S),
  Lax369799.BranchMonotonicity.ConditionMonotone E D →
    r.Accepting →
      Exists fun U =>
        And
          (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.Isomorphic (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.decode U)
            (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.decode S))
          (Exists fun s => s.Accepting)

concepts.title: Compressed transitions and their clone closure
concepts.description:
Lemma 108 compresses each block of directions by taking the meet of its
unary labels, retains the compressed tuples occurring infinitely often,
and closes them under uniform duplication. The closure is a clone table,
and one threshold controls all compressed transition families appearing
in a finite input system.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.BisimAutomata
import Lax369799.FiniteRecurrence
import Lax369799.FiniteAlgebraMeets
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Basic

/-!
---
title: Compressed transitions and their clone closure
type: theorem
---
Lemma 108 compresses each block of directions by taking the meet of its
unary labels, retains the compressed tuples occurring infinitely often,
and closes them under uniform duplication. The closure is a clone table,
and one threshold controls all compressed transition families appearing
in a finite input system.
-/

namespace Lax369799.CloneTransitions
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open SetSystemAlgebras BisimAutomata UnfoldAutomata TransitionEncoding

def Closure {H : Type} (B : ∀ n, Set (Fin n → H)) (n : ℕ) : Set (Fin n → H) :=
  {b | ∃ p m, 0 < p ∧ 0 < m ∧ ∃ h : p * m = n,
    ∃ c ∈ B p, b = fun i => Duplicate c (Fin.cast h.symm i)}

def compress {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) {n k : ℕ}
    (b : Fin (n * k) → A 1) : Fin n → A 1 :=
  fun i => FiniteAlgebraMeets.value E (fun j : Fin k => b (finProdFinEquiv (i, j)))

def alpha {A : RankedSet} {V : Type} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    (T : V → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → A 1)) (ν : V) (n k : ℕ) : Set (Fin n → A 1) :=
  {c | ∃ (l : ℕ) (h : n * k = l + 1) (b : Fin (l + 1) → A 1),
    b ∈ T ν l ∧ compress E (fun i => b (Fin.cast h i)) = c}

def beta {A : RankedSet} {V : Type} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    (T : V → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → A 1)) (ν : V) (n : ℕ) : Set (Fin n → A 1) :=
  FiniteRecurrence.Recurrent (alpha E T ν n)

noncomputable def automaton {P H : Type} [Fintype H] {z : ℕ}
    (B : Set P → ∀ n, Set (Fin n → H)) (leaves : Set P → Set (Fin z))
    (D : WordCondition (Fintype.card H) z) : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P) where
  unary := Fintype.card H
  nullary := z
  transition := fun n ν => {b | (fun i => (Fintype.equivFin H).symm (b i)) ∈ Closure (B ν) (n + 1)}
  leafTransition := leaves
  condition := D

axiom closure_closed {H : Type} (B : ∀ n, Set (Fin n → H)) {n m : ℕ}
    (b : Fin n → H) (hb : b ∈ Closure B n) (hm : 0 < m) : Duplicate b ∈ Closure B (n * m)

axiom component {A : RankedSet} (E : SetAlgebra A) {n k : ℕ}
    (b : Fin (n * k) → A 1) (i : Fin n) (j : Fin k) :
    Below E (compress E b i) (b (finProdFinEquiv (i, j)))

axiom stabilizes {A : RankedSet} {V : Type} (E : SetAlgebra A) [Finite (A 1)]
    (T : V → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → A 1)) (ν : V) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ N, ∀ k, N ≤ k → alpha E T ν n k ⊆ beta E T ν n

axiom uniform_stabilization {A : RankedSet} {V I : Type} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    [Finite (A 1)] [Finite I] (T : V → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → A 1))
    (ν : I → V) (arity : I → ℕ) :
    ∃ N, ∀ i k, N ≤ k → alpha E T (ν i) (arity i) k ⊆ beta E T (ν i) (arity i)

axiom clone_automaton {P H : Type} [Fintype H] {z : ℕ}
    (B : Set P → ∀ n, Set (Fin n → H)) (leaves : Set P → Set (Fin z))
    (D : WordCondition (Fintype.card H) z) : IsBisimAutomaton (automaton B leaves D)

axiom refinement {A : RankedSet} {V : Type} (E : SetAlgebra A)
    (T : V → ∀ n, Set (Fin (n + 1) → A 1)) (ν : V) {n : ℕ}
    (b : Fin n → A 1) (hb : b ∈ Closure (beta E T ν) n) :
    ∃ (l : ℕ) (c : Fin (l + 1) → A 1), c ∈ T ν l ∧
      ∃ σ : Fin (l + 1) → Fin n, Function.Surjective σ ∧
        ∀ i, Below E (b (σ i)) (c i)

end Lax369799.CloneTransitions

  (D : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition (Fintype.card H) z),
  Lax369799.BisimAutomata.IsBisimAutomaton (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.automaton B leaves D)

closure_closed : ∀ {H : Type} (B : (n : Nat) → Set (Fin n → H)) {n m : Nat} (b : Fin n → H),
  Set.instMembership.mem (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.Closure B n) b →
    instLTNat.lt 0 m →
      Set.instMembership.mem (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.Closure B (instHMul.hMul n m))
        (Lax369799.BisimAutomata.Duplicate b)

component : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.SetAlgebra A) {n k : Nat}
  (b : Fin (instHMul.hMul n k) → A 1) (i : Fin n) (j : Fin k),
  Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.Below E (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.compress E b i)
    (b (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe finProdFinEquiv { fst := i, snd := j }))

refinement : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {V : Type} (E : Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.SetAlgebra A)
  (T : V → (n : Nat) → Set (Fin (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) → A 1)) (ν : V) {n : Nat} (b : Fin n → A 1),
  Set.instMembership.mem (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.Closure (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.beta E T ν) n) b →
    Exists fun l =>
      Exists fun c =>
        And (Set.instMembership.mem (T ν l) c)
          (Exists fun σ =>
            And (Function.Surjective σ)
              (∀ (i : Fin (instHAdd.hAdd l 1)), Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.Below E (b (σ i)) (c i)))

stabilizes : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {V : Type} (E : Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.SetAlgebra A) [Finite (A 1)]
  (T : V → (n : Nat) → Set (Fin (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) → A 1)) (ν : V) (n : Nat),
  Exists fun N =>
    ∀ (k : Nat),
      instLENat.le N k →
        Set.instLE.le (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.alpha E T ν n k) (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.beta E T ν n)

uniform_stabilization : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {V I : Type} (E : Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.SetAlgebra A) [Finite (A 1)]
  [Finite I] (T : V → (n : Nat) → Set (Fin (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) → A 1)) (ν : I → V) (arity : I → Nat),
  Exists fun N =>
    ∀ (i : I) (k : Nat),
      instLENat.le N k →
        Set.instLE.le (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.alpha E T (ν i) (arity i) k)
          (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.beta E T (ν i) (arity i))

concepts.title: The closed extremal witness
concepts.description:
The rank-zero case of Lemma 91 retains the hole and its incoming unary
piece, makes the hole initial, and retains the former initial vertices
as roots. No direction copy or output edge is needed. Testing this closed
witness forces every component of an accepting context above the original
extremal datum. Minimality then identifies its value with the hole value.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ExtremalSituations

/-!
---
title: The closed extremal witness
type: theorem
---
The rank-zero case of Lemma 91 retains the hole and its incoming unary
piece, makes the hole initial, and retains the former initial vertices
as roots. No direction copy or output edge is needed. Testing this closed
witness forces every component of an accepting context above the original
extremal datum. Minimality then identifies its value with the hole value.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ClosedExtremal
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FinitePresentations FiniteContextualOrder FiniteSyntacticAlgebra
open FiniteAcceptance ExpandedSyntacticAlgebra
open ExtremalContexts (Data)
open FiniteExtremal (Accepts value DataBelow)

def witness {A : RankedSet} (x : Data A 0) (a : A 0) : FiniteSystem A 0 where
  size := 2
  graph := {
    label := Fin.cases ⟨0, a⟩ (fun i => ⟨1, x.2 i⟩)
    initial := {0}
    root := fun v => v = 1 ∨ (v = 0 ∧ x.1.root)
    edge := fun v d t => v = 1 ∧ d = 0 ∧ t = .inl 0
    direction_valid := by
      rintro v d t ⟨rfl, rfl, _⟩
      exact Nat.zero_lt_one }

axiom comparison {A : RankedSet} (L : Algebras.Language A)
    (E : SyntacticAlgebra L) (x y : Data (Carrier (Accepting L)) 0)
    (a : Carrier (Accepting L) 0)
    (hx : Lax369799.FiniteExtremal.IsExtremal (Accepting L) E.algebra a x)

concepts.title: Closed values as unary pieces
concepts.description:
A nullary value can occur in a unary piece with an unused output variable.
Its vertex can be initial or unmarked. Both operations preserve binary
sums; unmarked vertices are retained during substitution.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra

/-!
---
title: Closed values as unary pieces
type: theorem
---
A nullary value can occur in a unary piece with an unused output variable.
Its vertex can be initial or unmarked. Both operations preserve binary
sums; unmarked vertices are retained during substitution.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ClosedUnaryLift
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FinitePresentations FiniteSyntacticAlgebra

def system {A : RankedSet} (initial : Bool) (c : A 0) : FiniteSystem A 1 where
  size := 1
  graph := {
    label := fun _ => ⟨0, c⟩
    initial := fun _ => initial = true
    root := ∅
    edge := fun _ _ _ => False
    direction_valid := fun _ _ _ h => False.elim h }

def value {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (initial : Bool) (c : A 0) : A 1 :=
  E.eval 1 (system initial c)

axiom preserves_sum {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (initial : Bool) (c d : A 0) :
    value E initial (sumValue E c d) = sumValue E (value E initial c) (value E initial d)

end Lax369799.ClosedUnaryLift

  Eq (Lax369799.ClosedUnaryLift.value E initial (Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.sumValue E c d))
    (Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.sumValue E (Lax369799.ClosedUnaryLift.value E initial c)

concepts.title: Combining finite and infinite branch conditions
concepts.description:
The finite-word evaluator can be combined with any parity condition on
infinite words. The product reads both components in parallel, uses the
parity component's priorities, and tests the evaluator's final state on
terminating words.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.FiniteBranchWords
import Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod

/-!
---
title: Combining finite and infinite branch conditions
type: theorem
---
The finite-word evaluator can be combined with any parity condition on
infinite words. The product reads both components in parallel, uses the
parity component's priorities, and tests the evaluator's final state on
terminating words.
-/
namespace Lax369799.CombinedWordCondition
open UnfoldAutomata FiniteBranchWords

noncomputable def combine {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z)
    (f : Fin u → Fin z → Fin z) (F : Set (Fin z)) : WordCondition u z := by
  classical
  let Q := Fin D.states × State (Fin z)
  let e := Fintype.equivFin Q
  exact {
    states := Fintype.card Q
    initial := e (D.initial, (machine f F).start)
    step := fun q a => e (D.step (e.symm q).1 a, (machine f F).step (e.symm q).2 a)
    priority := fun q => D.priority (e.symm q).1
    final := {q | (e.symm q).2 ∈ (machine f F).accept} }

axiom finite_iff {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z)
    (f : Fin u → Fin z → Fin z) (F : Set (Fin z))
    (w : List (Fin u)) (a : Fin z) :
    (combine D f F).AcceptsFinite w a ↔ w.foldr f a ∈ F

axiom infinite_iff {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z)
    (f : Fin u → Fin z → Fin z) (F : Set (Fin z))
    (w : ℕ → Fin u) :
    (combine D f F).AcceptsInfinite w ↔ D.AcceptsInfinite w

end Lax369799.CombinedWordCondition

  (w : List (Fin u)) (a : Fin z),
  Iff ((Lax369799.CombinedWordCondition.combine D f F).AcceptsFinite w a) (Set.instMembership.mem F (List.foldr f a w))

  (w : Nat → Fin u), Iff ((Lax369799.CombinedWordCondition.combine D f F).AcceptsInfinite w) (D.AcceptsInfinite w)

concepts.title: Splitting outgoing choices in cyclic unary contexts
concepts.description:
Restrict the outgoing edges of the hole to a set of target vertices.
For a selected unary value, acceptance for a union of targets is
equivalent to acceptance for both restrictions. The context may contain
feedback, roots, and a self-loop at the hole; every vertex is retained.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ExtremalUnaryTypes
import Lax369799.FiniteMarkUnion

/-!
---
title: Splitting outgoing choices in cyclic unary contexts
type: theorem
---
Restrict the outgoing edges of the hole to a set of target vertices.
For a selected unary value, acceptance for a union of targets is
equivalent to acceptance for both restrictions. The context may contain
feedback, roots, and a self-loop at the hole; every vertex is retained.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ContextChoices
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FinitePresentations FiniteContexts FiniteContextualOrder FiniteAcceptance
open FiniteDecomposition FiniteSyntacticAlgebra ExpandedSyntacticAlgebra

noncomputable def restrict {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : Context A k 0)
    (p : Set C.system.Vertex) : Context A k 0 where
  system := {
    size := C.system.size
    graph := { C.system.graph with
      edge := fun v d t => C.system.graph.edge v d t ∧
        (v = holeVertex C → match t with | .inl w => p w | .inr _ => False)
      direction_valid := fun v d t h => C.system.graph.direction_valid v d t h.1 } }
  one_hole := C.one_hole

axiom accepting_union {A : RankedSet} (L : Algebras.Language A)
    (E : SyntacticAlgebra L) (b : Carrier (Accepting L) 1)
    (hb : ExtremalUnaryTypes.Selected L E b)
    (C : Context (Carrier (Accepting L)) 1 0) (p q : Set C.system.Vertex) :
    AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug (restrict C (p ∪ q)) (atomic b))) ↔
      AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug (restrict C p) (atomic b))) ∧
      AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug (restrict C q) (atomic b)))

axiom accepting_finite {A : RankedSet} (L : Algebras.Language A)
    (E : SyntacticAlgebra L) (b : Carrier (Accepting L) 1)
    (hb : ExtremalUnaryTypes.Selected L E b)
    (C : Context (Carrier (Accepting L)) 1 0) (s : Finset C.system.Vertex) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug (restrict C (↑s)) (atomic b))) ↔
      ∀ v ∈ s, AcceptingClass (Accepting L)
        (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug (restrict C {v}) (atomic b)))

axiom accepting_all_choices {A : RankedSet} (L : Algebras.Language A)
    (E : SyntacticAlgebra L) (b : Carrier (Accepting L) 1)
    (hb : ExtremalUnaryTypes.Selected L E b)
    (C : Context (Carrier (Accepting L)) 1 0) :
    AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug C (atomic b))) ↔
      ∀ v : C.system.Vertex, AcceptingClass (Accepting L)
        (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug (restrict C {v}) (atomic b)))

end Lax369799.ContextChoices

concepts.title: Context decomposition with hole boundary data
concepts.description:
A hole is an ordinary vertex: it may be initial, a root, and the target of
its own outgoing edges. Cutting a closed context into unary pieces must
retain these three kinds of boundary information. The entry piece starts
at the original non-hole initial vertices; piece i+1 starts at non-hole
successors in direction i. All pieces retain the non-hole roots, and
edges into the hole become edges to the sole variable.

Recomposition takes a separate copy of every piece, redirects variable
edges to a fresh hole, restores its initial and root marks, and restores
its self-loops. Unreachable vertices are removed after recomposition.
The resulting set-system covers the original context and is therefore
unfold-equivalent to it.

This records explicitly the boundary information omitted by the literal
construction preceding `lemma:context-decomposition` in Section 2.8 of
arXiv:2407.12677v6. The pieces are presented over the extended alphabet,
but no piece contains a vertex labelled by the hole. Presentations retain
unreachable vertices until the final restriction.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.Flattening
import Lax369799.PresentationCovers
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Option
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod

/-!
---
title: Context decomposition with hole boundary data
type: theorem
---
A hole is an ordinary vertex: it may be initial, a root, and the target of
its own outgoing edges. Cutting a closed context into unary pieces must
retain these three kinds of boundary information. The entry piece starts
at the original non-hole initial vertices; piece i+1 starts at non-hole
successors in direction i. All pieces retain the non-hole roots, and
edges into the hole become edges to the sole variable.

Recomposition takes a separate copy of every piece, redirects variable
edges to a fresh hole, restores its initial and root marks, and restores
its self-loops. Unreachable vertices are removed after recomposition.
The resulting set-system covers the original context and is therefore
unfold-equivalent to it.

This records explicitly the boundary information omitted by the literal
construction preceding `lemma:context-decomposition` in Section 2.8 of
arXiv:2407.12677v6. The pieces are presented over the extended alphabet,
but no piece contains a vertex labelled by the hole. Presentations retain
unreachable vertices until the final restriction.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ContextDecomposition
open RankedSystems Morphisms Flattening

noncomputable def holeVertex {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) :
    C.system.Vertex := Classical.choose C.one_hole

abbrev BodyVertex {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) :=
  {v : C.system.Vertex // v ≠ holeVertex C}

structure Boundary (k : ℕ) where
  initial : Prop
  root : Prop
  loops : Set (Fin k)

noncomputable def boundary {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) : Boundary k where
  initial := holeVertex C ∈ C.system.graph.initial
  root := holeVertex C ∈ C.system.graph.root
  loops := {d | C.system.graph.edge (holeVertex C) d.val (.inl (holeVertex C))}

noncomputable def piece {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0)
    (i : Fin (k + 1)) : Presentation (WithHole A k) 1 (BodyVertex C) where
  label := fun v => C.system.graph.label v.val
  initial := fun v => (i = 0 ∧ v.val ∈ C.system.graph.initial) ∨
    ∃ d : Fin k, i = d.succ ∧ C.system.graph.edge (holeVertex C) d.val (.inl v.val)
  root := fun v => v.val ∈ C.system.graph.root
  edge := fun v d t => match t with
    | .inl w => C.system.graph.edge v.val d (.inl w.val)
    | .inr _ => C.system.graph.edge v.val d (.inl (holeVertex C))
  direction_valid := by
    intro v d t ht
    cases t with
    | inl w => exact C.system.graph.direction_valid v.val d _ ht
    | inr i => exact C.system.graph.direction_valid v.val d _ ht

abbrev CopyVertex (k : ℕ) (V : Type) := Option (Fin (k + 1) × V)

/-- `none` is the new hole; `some (i,v)` is vertex v in piece i. -/
def recomposePresentation {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} {V : Type}
    (B : Boundary k) (P : Fin (k + 1) → Presentation (WithHole A k) 1 V) :
    Presentation (WithHole A k) 0 (CopyVertex k V) where
  label := fun v => match v with
    | none => ⟨k, Sum.inr ⟨rfl⟩⟩
    | some (i, v) => (P i).label v
  initial := fun v => match v with
    | none => B.initial
    | some (i, v) => i = 0 ∧ v ∈ (P i).initial
  root := fun v => match v with
    | none => B.root
    | some (i, v) => v ∈ (P i).root
  edge := fun v d t => match t with
    | .inr j => Fin.elim0 j
    | .inl w => match v, w with
      | none, none => ∃ i : Fin k, d = i.val ∧ i ∈ B.loops
      | none, some (j, w) => ∃ i : Fin k, d = i.val ∧ j = i.succ ∧ w ∈ (P j).initial
      | some (i, v), none => (P i).edge v d (.inr 0)
      | some (i, v), some (j, w) => i = j ∧ (P i).edge v d (.inl w)
  direction_valid := by
    intro v d t ht
    cases t with
    | inr j => exact Fin.elim0 j
    | inl w =>
      cases v with
      | none =>
        cases w with
        | none => obtain ⟨i, rfl, _⟩ := ht; exact i.isLt
        | some w => obtain ⟨i, rfl, _, _⟩ := ht; exact i.isLt
      | some v =>
        cases w with
        | none => exact (P v.1).direction_valid v.2 d _ ht
        | some w => exact (P v.1).direction_valid v.2 d _ ht.2

noncomputable def recompose {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) :
    SetSystem (WithHole A k) 0 := by
  classical
  exact trim (recomposePresentation (boundary C) (piece C))

axiom piece_has_no_hole {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0)
    (i : Fin (k + 1)) (v : BodyVertex C) : ¬ IsHole ((piece C i).label v)

axiom decomposition_cover {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) :
  UnfoldsTo C.system (recompose C)

axiom decomposition_equivalence {A : RankedSet} {k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k 0) :
  UnfoldEquivalent C.system (recompose C)

end Lax369799.ContextDecomposition

  Not (Lax369799.Flattening.IsHole ((Lax369799.ContextDecomposition.piece C i).label v))

concepts.title: Restricting and resizing the directions of a context
concepts.description:
Select the hole's successors using a map from new directions to old
ones, change the hole rank, and restrict to reachable vertices. The
hole remains reachable because its first visit uses no outgoing hole
edge. Substitution into this context is isomorphic to renaming the
argument's outputs before insertion into the original context.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ContextRelabelling
import Lax369799.SupportPorts

/-!
---
title: Restricting and resizing the directions of a context
type: theorem
---
Select the hole's successors using a map from new directions to old
ones, change the hole rank, and restrict to reachable vertices. The
hole remains reachable because its first visit uses no outgoing hole
edge. Substitution into this context is isomorphic to renaming the
argument's outputs before insertion into the original context.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ContextPorts
open RankedSystems Flattening

/-- Change the hole's rank and retain every ordinary symbol. -/
def resizeSymbol {A : RankedSet} {m : ℕ} (k : ℕ) : Symbol (WithHole A m) → Symbol (WithHole A k)
  | ⟨r,.inl a⟩ => ⟨r,.inl a⟩
  | ⟨_,.inr _⟩ => ⟨k,.inr ⟨rfl⟩⟩

noncomputable def resizeGraph {A : RankedSet} {m k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A m 0)
    (s : Fin k → Fin m) : Presentation (WithHole A k) 0 C.system.Vertex := by
  classical
  exact {
    label := fun v => resizeSymbol k (C.system.graph.label v)
    initial := C.system.graph.initial
    root := C.system.graph.root
    edge := fun v d t => if IsHole (C.system.graph.label v) then
      ∃ i : Fin k,d = i.val ∧ C.system.graph.edge v (s i).val t
      else C.system.graph.edge v d t
    direction_valid := by
      intro v d t ht
      cases hlabel : C.system.graph.label v with
      | mk r a =>
        cases a with
        | inl a =>
          have hn : ¬IsHole (C.system.graph.label v) := by
            rw [hlabel]; rintro ⟨e,he⟩; cases he
          rw [if_neg hn] at ht
          have hd := C.system.graph.direction_valid v d t ht
          rw [hlabel] at hd
          simpa only [hlabel,resizeSymbol] using hd
        | inr e =>
          have hh : IsHole (C.system.graph.label v) := by rw [hlabel]; exact ⟨e,rfl⟩
          rw [if_pos hh] at ht
          obtain ⟨i,rfl,_⟩ := ht
          simpa only [hlabel,resizeSymbol] using i.isLt }

axiom resize_exists {A : RankedSet} {m k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A m 0)
    (hC : C.system.Deterministic) (s : Fin k → Fin m) :
    ∃ D : SetContext A k 0, D.system = trim (resizeGraph C s) ∧ D.system.Deterministic

axiom plug_resize {A : RankedSet} {m k : ℕ} (C : SetContext A m 0)
    (hC : C.system.Deterministic) (s : Fin k → Fin m) (R : System A k)
    (D : SetContext A k 0) (hD : D.system = trim (resizeGraph C s))
    (U V : System A 0) (hU : U.val = plug C (Renaming.renameSystem s R).val)
    (hV : V.val = plug D R.val) : Morphisms.Isomorphic U.val V.val

end Lax369799.ContextPorts

statements.signature:
plug_resize : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {m k : Nat} (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A m 0),
  C.system.Deterministic →
    ∀ (s : Fin k → Fin m) (R : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A k) (D : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A k 0),
      Eq D.system (Lax369799.RankedSystems.trim (Lax369799.ContextPorts.resizeGraph C s)) →
        ∀ (U V : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A 0),
          Eq U.val (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C (Lax369799.Renaming.renameSystem s R).val) →
            Eq V.val (Lax369799.Flattening.plug D R.val) → Lax369799.Morphisms.Isomorphic U.val V.val

resize_exists : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {m k : Nat} (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A m 0),
  C.system.Deterministic →
    ∀ (s : Fin k → Fin m),
      Exists fun D =>
        And (Eq D.system (Lax369799.RankedSystems.trim (Lax369799.ContextPorts.resizeGraph C s))) D.system.Deterministic

concepts.title: Relabelling and deterministic context substitution
concepts.description:
Relabelling ordinary letters preserves the unique hole. It commutes with
substitution, and plugging a deterministic system into a deterministic
context gives a deterministic system.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SystemEvaluation

/-!
---
title: Relabelling and deterministic context substitution
type: theorem
---
Relabelling ordinary letters preserves the unique hole. It commutes with
substitution, and plugging a deterministic system into a deterministic
context gives a deterministic system.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ContextRelabelling
open RankedSystems Flattening

def mapAlphabet {A B : RankedSet} (η : RankedMap A B) (k : ℕ) :
    RankedMap (WithHole A k) (WithHole B k) := fun r => Sum.map (η r) id

def mapContext {A B : RankedSet} (η : RankedMap A B) {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) : SetContext B k n where
  system := relabel (mapAlphabet η k) C.system
  one_hole := by
    have hi (v : C.system.Vertex) :
        IsHole ((relabel (mapAlphabet η k) C.system).graph.label v) ↔
          IsHole (C.system.graph.label v) := by
      change (∃ h, Sum.map (η _) id (C.system.graph.label v).2 = Sum.inr h) ↔
        ∃ h, (C.system.graph.label v).2 = Sum.inr h
      cases (C.system.graph.label v).2 <;> simp
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hu⟩ := C.one_hole
    exact ⟨v, (hi v).mpr hv, fun w hw => hu w ((hi w).mp hw)⟩

axiom relabel_plug {A B : RankedSet} (η : RankedMap A B) {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (S : SetSystem A k) :
    relabel η (plug C S) = plug (mapContext η C) (relabel η S)

axiom plug_system {A : RankedSet} {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (hC : C.system.Deterministic) (S : System A k) :
    ∃ U : System A n, U.val = plug C S.val

axiom evaluation_congruence {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebras.Algebra B)
    (η : RankedMap A B) {k n : ℕ} (C : SetContext A k n) (hC : C.system.Deterministic)
    (S T : System A k) (U V : System A n)
    (hU : U.val = plug C S.val) (hV : V.val = plug C T.val)
    (h : E.eval k (relabelSystem η S) = E.eval k (relabelSystem η T)) :
    E.eval n (relabelSystem η U) = E.eval n (relabelSystem η V)

end Lax369799.ContextRelabelling

statements.signature:
evaluation_congruence : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B)
  (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B) {k n : Nat} (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A k n),
  C.system.Deterministic →
    ∀ (S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A k) (U V : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A n),
      Eq U.val (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C S.val) →
        Eq V.val (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C T.val) →
          Eq (E.eval k (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η S))
              (E.eval k (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η T)) →
            Eq (E.eval n (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η U))
              (E.eval n (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η V))

plug_system : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {k n : Nat} (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A k n),
  C.system.Deterministic →
    ∀ (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A k), Exists fun U => Eq U.val (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C S.val)

relabel_plug : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B) {k n : Nat}
  (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A k n) (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A k),
  Eq (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabel η (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C S))
    (Lax369799.Flattening.plug (Lax369799.ContextRelabelling.mapContext η C) (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabel η S))

concepts.title: Finite resolution approximation in a context
concepts.description:
A direct resolution in a context needs only a finite family of direct
resolutions at its hole. Keeping their sum inside the context permits
independent choices at different occurrences. This is the approximation
behind Corollary 46 of arXiv v6 (Corollary 50 in the revised manuscript),
and its consequence for initial yields, using the earlier reachable interface.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.FiniteResolutionApproximation

/-!
---
title: Finite resolution approximation in a context
type: theorem
---
A direct resolution in a context needs only a finite family of direct
resolutions at its hole. Keeping their sum inside the context permits
independent choices at different occurrences. This is the approximation
behind Corollary 46 of arXiv v6 (Corollary 50 in the revised manuscript),
and its consequence for initial yields, using the earlier reachable interface.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ContextResolutionApproximation
open RankedSystems Morphisms Flattening FiniteResolutionNormalForms

axiom direct_approximation {A : RankedSet} {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (S : SetSystem A k) (R : System A n)
    (hR : DirectResolution (plug C S) R) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → Component S) (U : System A n),
      (∀ i, (c i).rooted = false) ∧
      DirectResolution (plug C (trim (family c).graph)) U ∧ UnfoldsTo R.val U.val

axiom initial_yields {A : RankedSet} {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (S : SetSystem A k) (R : System A n) :
    InitYield (plug C S) R ↔
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → Component S),
        (∀ i, (c i).rooted = false) ∧ InitYield (plug C (trim (family c).graph)) R

axiom root_yields {A : RankedSet} {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (S : SetSystem A k) (R : System A n) :
    InitYield (uproot (plug C S)) R ↔
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → Component S),
        InitYield (uproot (plug C (trim (family c).graph))) R

axiom yields {A : RankedSet} {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (S : SetSystem A k) (R : SetSystem A n) :
    Yield (plug C S) R ↔
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (c : Fin m → Component S),
        Yield (plug C (trim (family c).graph)) R

end Lax369799.ContextResolutionApproximation

  Lax369799.Morphisms.DirectResolution (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C S) R →
    Exists fun m =>

            (And

                (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C

                U)

concepts.title: Smallification preserving identity continuations
concepts.description:
Variables can be grouped by their target and their optional unary
continuation value. The grouping preserves evaluation in a closed
deterministic context and has at most |A₁|+1 representatives over each
target. The additional observation represents a direct return to the
hole, whose cut piece is empty.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.DeterministicNormalForms
import Lax369799.ContextRelabelling

/-!
---
title: Smallification preserving identity continuations
type: theorem
---
Variables can be grouped by their target and their optional unary
continuation value. The grouping preserves evaluation in a closed
deterministic context and has at most |A₁|+1 representatives over each
target. The additional observation represents a direct return to the
hole, whose cut piece is empty.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ContextSmallification
open RankedSystems Flattening Algebras Renaming

axiom context_smallification {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebra A) (hE : UnfoldInvariant E)
    [Finite (A 1)] {m n : ℕ} (C : SetContext A m 0) (hC : C.system.Deterministic)
    (S : System A m) (σ : Fin m → Fin n) :
    ∃ (m' : ℕ) (τ : Fin m → Fin m') (sectionMap : Fin m' → Fin m),
      (∀ j, τ (sectionMap j) = j) ∧
      (∀ i, σ (sectionMap (τ i)) = σ i) ∧
      (∀ j, Nat.card {i // σ (sectionMap i) = j} ≤ Nat.card (A 1) + 1) ∧
      ∃ U V : System A 0,
        U.val = plug C S.val ∧
        V.val = plug C (renameSystem (sectionMap ∘ τ) S).val ∧
        E.eval 0 U = E.eval 0 V

axiom mapped_context_smallification {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (hE : UnfoldInvariant E)
    [Finite (B 1)] (η : RankedMap A B) {m n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A m 0) (hC : C.system.Deterministic) (S : System A m) (σ : Fin m → Fin n) :
    ∃ (m' : ℕ) (τ : Fin m → Fin m') (sectionMap : Fin m' → Fin m),
      (∀ j, τ (sectionMap j) = j) ∧
      (∀ i, σ (sectionMap (τ i)) = σ i) ∧
      (∀ j, Nat.card {i // σ (sectionMap i) = j} ≤ Nat.card (B 1) + 1) ∧
      ∃ U V : System A 0,
        U.val = plug C S.val ∧
        V.val = plug C (renameSystem (sectionMap ∘ τ) S).val ∧
        E.eval 0 (relabelSystem η U) = E.eval 0 (relabelSystem η V)

end Lax369799.ContextSmallification

context_smallification : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra A),
  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariant E →
    ∀ [Finite (A 1)] {m n : Nat} (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A m 0),
      C.system.Deterministic →
        ∀ (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A m) (σ : Fin m → Fin n),
          Exists fun m' =>
            Exists fun τ =>
              Exists fun sectionMap =>
                And (∀ (j : Fin m'), Eq (τ (sectionMap j)) j)
                  (And (∀ (i : Fin m), Eq (σ (sectionMap (τ i))) (σ i))
                    (And
                      (∀ (j : Fin n),
                        instLENat.le (Nat.card (Subtype fun i => Eq (σ (sectionMap i)) j))
                          (instHAdd.hAdd (Nat.card (A 1)) 1))
                      (Exists fun U =>
                        Exists fun V =>
                          And (Eq U.val (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C S.val))
                            (And
                              (Eq V.val
                                (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C
                                  (Lax369799.Renaming.renameSystem (Function.comp sectionMap τ) S).val))
                              (Eq (E.eval 0 U) (E.eval 0 V))))))
