  instLTNat.lt 0 (instHSub.hSub (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.ceiling D) (D.priority q))

reverse_parity : ∀ {u z : Nat} (D : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition u z) (w : Nat → Fin u),
  Iff (D.AcceptsInfinite w)
    (Exists fun c =>
      And (Even c)
        (And
          (∀ (N : Nat),
            Exists fun n =>
              And (instLENat.le N n)
                (Eq (instHSub.hSub (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.ceiling D) (D.priority (D.run w n))) c))
          (∀ (b : Nat),
            instLTNat.lt c b →
              Not
                (∀ (N : Nat),
                  Exists fun n =>
                    And (instLENat.le N n)
                      (Eq (instHSub.hSub (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.ceiling D) (D.priority (D.run w n))) b)))))

terminal_winning : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (b : Bool),
  Iff
    (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.terminal b))
    (Eq b Bool.true)

winning_equation : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.Vertex),
  Iff
    (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position q v))
    (Lax369799.ModalTransitions.OneStep M q S v fun p =>
      Set.ofPred fun w =>
        Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
          (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position p w))

winning_nested : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.Vertex),
  Iff
    (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position q v))
    (Set.instMembership.mem
      (Lax369799.ParityGameEquations.solve (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S)
        (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.ceiling M.condition) 1) fun x =>
        Set.instEmptyCollection.emptyCollection)
      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position q v))

concepts.title: Modal equations on input vertices
concepts.description:
Project winning regions to word-state/input positions. Marking positions
are determined by universal successor conditions and terminals by their
outcomes. The projection and its monotone section preserve the least and
greatest solutions of each stopped priority game. The resulting nested
equations have one coordinate per word state and are evaluated on the
original input graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame
import Lax369799.FixedPointRetraction

/-!
---
title: Modal equations on input vertices
type: theorem
---
Project winning regions to word-state/input positions. Marking positions
are determined by universal successor conditions and terminals by their
outcomes. The projection and its monotone section preserve the least and
greatest solutions of each stopped priority game. The resulting nested
equations have one coordinate per word state and are evaluated on the
original input graph.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ModalGameEquations
open TransitionSystems TransitionEncoding UnfoldAutomata ModalTransitions ModalAcceptanceGame
open FiniteParityGames ParityWinningRegions ParityFixedPoints
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

def project {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (S : TransitionSystem P) :
    Set (Vertex M S) →o Marking M S where
  toFun := fun X q => {v | position q v ∈ X}
  monotone' := fun _ _ h _ _ hv => h hv

def lift {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (S : TransitionSystem P) :
    Marking M S →o Set (Vertex M S) where
  toFun := fun X t => match t with
    | .inl (q, v) => v ∈ X q
    | .inr (.inl (v, ρ)) => ∀ q w, S.edge v w → w ∈ ρ q → w ∈ X q
    | .inr (.inr b) => b = true
  monotone' := by
    intro X Y h t ht
    rcases t with ⟨q, v⟩ | (⟨v, ρ⟩ | b)
    · exact h q ht
    · exact fun q w hw hρ => h q (ht q w hw hρ)
    · exact ht

def statePriority {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (q : Fin M.condition.states) : ℕ := ceiling M.condition - M.condition.priority q

def boundary {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (S : TransitionSystem P)
    (B : Fin M.condition.states → S.Vertex → Prop) : Set (Vertex M S) :=
  {t | match t with
    | .inl (q, v) => B q v
    | _ => False}

noncomputable def stopped {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (S : TransitionSystem P) (n : ℕ) (ρ : ℕ → Marking M S) : Game (Vertex M S) :=
  stop (game M S) (boundary M S (fun q _ => n ≤ statePriority M q))
    (boundary M S (fun q v => OneStep M q S v (ρ (statePriority M q))))

noncomputable def solve {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (S : TransitionSystem P) : ℕ → (ℕ → Marking M S) → Marking M S
  | 0, ρ => fun q => {v | OneStep M q S v (ρ (statePriority M q))}
  | n + 1, ρ => if Even n then
      sSup {X : Marking M S | X ≤ solve M S n (Function.update ρ n X)}
    else sInf {X : Marking M S | solve M S n (Function.update ρ n X) ≤ X}

axiom solve_stopped {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (S : TransitionSystem P) (n : ℕ) (ρ : ℕ → Marking M S) :
    project M S (Winning (stopped M S n ρ) true) = solve M S n ρ

axiom winning {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (S : TransitionSystem P) (n : ℕ) (hn : ∀ q, statePriority M q < n)
    (ρ : ℕ → Marking M S) :
    project M S (Winning (game M S) true) = solve M S n ρ

end Lax369799.ModalGameEquations

statements.signature:
solve_stopped : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (n : Nat) (ρ : Nat → Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.Marking M S),
  Eq
    (OrderHom.instFunLike.coe (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.project M S)
      (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.stopped M S n ρ) Bool.true))
    (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.solve M S n ρ)

winning : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (n : Nat),
  (∀ (q : Fin M.condition.states), instLTNat.lt (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.statePriority M q) n) →
    ∀ (ρ : Nat → Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.Marking M S),
      Eq
        (OrderHom.instFunLike.coe (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.project M S)
          (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true))
        (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.solve M S n ρ)

concepts.title: Translating the modal acceptance game to a sentence
concepts.description:
Translate the projected priority equations into formulas by binding a
finite vector of variables at each priority. Capture-avoiding substitution
supplies the boundary parameters; finite equation elimination implements
each vector binder in the scalar mu-calculus. The resulting sentence is
independent of the input graph and defines the game's winning region.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ModalGameEquations
import Lax369799.FiniteMuEquations

/-!
---
title: Translating the modal acceptance game to a sentence
type: theorem
---
Translate the projected priority equations into formulas by binding a
finite vector of variables at each priority. Capture-avoiding substitution
supplies the boundary parameters; finite equation elimination implements
each vector binder in the scalar mu-calculus. The resulting sentence is
independent of the input graph and defines the game's winning region.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ModalGameTranslation
open TransitionSystems TransitionEncoding UnfoldAutomata ModalTransitions ModalAcceptanceGame
open ModalMuCalculus MuSubstitution
open ModalGameEquations (statePriority)
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

noncomputable def bindBoundary {P : Type}
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) {m : ℕ}
    (n : ℕ) (θ : ℕ → Fin M.condition.states → Formula P m) :
    ℕ → Fin M.condition.states → Formula P (M.condition.states + m) :=
  fun p q => if p = n then .variable (Fin.castAdd m q)
    else rename (Fin.natAdd M.condition.states) (θ p q)

noncomputable def formulas {P : Type} [Fintype P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) :
    (n : ℕ) → {m : ℕ} → (ℕ → Fin M.condition.states → Formula P m) →
      Fin M.condition.states → Formula P m
  | 0, _, θ => fun q => substitute (θ (statePriority M q)) (transitionFormula M q)
  | n + 1, _, θ => Lax369799.FiniteMuEquations.solve
      (if Even n then .greatest else .least) (formulas M n (bindBoundary M n θ))

noncomputable def sentence {P : Type} [Fintype P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (q : Fin M.condition.states) : Sentence P :=
  formulas M (ceiling M.condition + 1) (fun _ _ => .bot) q

axiom formulas_correct {P : Type} [Fintype P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (S : TransitionSystem P)
    (n : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (θ : ℕ → Fin M.condition.states → Formula P m)
    (ρ : Fin m → Set S.Vertex) :
    (fun q => (formulas M n θ q).eval S ρ) =
      Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.solve M S n (fun p q => (θ p q).eval S ρ)

axiom sentence_correct {P : Type} [Fintype P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (S : TransitionSystem P)
    (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.Vertex) :
    v ∈ (sentence M q).eval S Fin.elim0 ↔
      Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (game M S) true (position q v)

axiom game_to_mu {P : Type} [Finite P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) :
    ∃ φ : Sentence P, ∀ S,
      Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (game M S) true
        (position M.condition.initial S.initial) ↔ Models S φ

end Lax369799.ModalGameTranslation

statements.signature:
formulas_correct : ∀ {P : Type} [inst : Fintype P]
  (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (n : Nat) {m : Nat}
  (θ : Nat → Fin M.condition.states → Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula P m) (ρ : Fin m → Set S.Vertex),
  Eq (fun q => Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (Lax369799.ModalGameTranslation.formulas M n θ q) ρ)
    (Lax369799.ModalGameEquations.solve M S n fun p q => Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (θ p q) ρ)

game_to_mu : ∀ {P : Type} [Finite P]
  (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P)),
  Exists fun φ =>
    ∀ (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P),
      Iff
        (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
          (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial S.initial))
        (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ)

sentence_correct : ∀ {P : Type} [inst : Fintype P]
  (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.Vertex),
  Iff
    (Set.instMembership.mem
      (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (Lax369799.ModalGameTranslation.sentence M q) Fin.elim0) v)
    (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position q v))

concepts.title: Modal mu-calculus
concepts.description:
The modal mu-calculus is presented in negation normal form: negation is
allowed on proposition letters, and all fixed-point variables occur
positively. Formulas have conjunction, disjunction, box, diamond, and least
and greatest fixed points. A binder introduces variable zero and shifts
the previous free variables. Least fixed points are intersections of
pre-fixed points; greatest fixed points are unions of post-fixed points.
A closed formula is evaluated at the initial vertex.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.TransitionSystems
import Mathlib.Order.CompleteLattice.Basic

/-!
---
title: Modal mu-calculus
type: definition
---
The modal mu-calculus is presented in negation normal form: negation is
allowed on proposition letters, and all fixed-point variables occur
positively. Formulas have conjunction, disjunction, box, diamond, and least
and greatest fixed points. A binder introduces variable zero and shifts
the previous free variables. Least fixed points are intersections of
pre-fixed points; greatest fixed points are unions of post-fixed points.
A closed formula is evaluated at the initial vertex.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus
open TransitionSystems

inductive Formula (P : Type) : ℕ → Type
  | top {n} : Formula P n
  | bot {n} : Formula P n
  | proposition {n} : P → Formula P n
  | negProposition {n} : P → Formula P n
  | variable {n} : Fin n → Formula P n
  | conj {n} : Formula P n → Formula P n → Formula P n
  | disj {n} : Formula P n → Formula P n → Formula P n
  | diamond {n} : Formula P n → Formula P n
  | box {n} : Formula P n → Formula P n
  | mu {n} : Formula P (n + 1) → Formula P n
  | nu {n} : Formula P (n + 1) → Formula P n

def Formula.eval {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) :
    {n : ℕ} → Formula P n → (Fin n → Set S.Vertex) → Set S.Vertex
  | _, .top, _ => Set.univ
  | _, .bot, _ => ∅
  | _, .proposition p, _ => {v | p ∈ S.valuation v}
  | _, .negProposition p, _ => {v | p ∉ S.valuation v}
  | _, .variable x, ρ => ρ x
  | _, .conj φ ψ, ρ => φ.eval S ρ ∩ ψ.eval S ρ
  | _, .disj φ ψ, ρ => φ.eval S ρ ∪ ψ.eval S ρ
  | _, .diamond φ, ρ => {v | ∃ w, S.edge v w ∧ w ∈ φ.eval S ρ}
  | _, .box φ, ρ => {v | ∀ w, S.edge v w → w ∈ φ.eval S ρ}
  | _, .mu φ, ρ => sInf {X | φ.eval S (Fin.cases X ρ) ⊆ X}
  | _, .nu φ, ρ => sSup {X | X ⊆ φ.eval S (Fin.cases X ρ)}

abbrev Sentence (P : Type) := Formula P 0

def Models {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) (φ : Sentence P) : Prop :=
  S.initial ∈ φ.eval S Fin.elim0

def Definable {P : Type} (L : Set (TransitionSystem P)) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : Sentence P, ∀ S, S ∈ L ↔ Models S φ

end Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus

concepts.title: Small finite models for modal parity acceptance
concepts.description:
If a modal acceptance game wins on a finite transition system, it wins
on a finite reachable system with at most as many vertices as the word
condition has states. Alternating simulations and positional strategies
supply the bound needed for the finite-search effectivity argument.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame

/-!
---
title: Small finite models for modal parity acceptance
type: theorem
---
If a modal acceptance game wins on a finite transition system, it wins
on a finite reachable system with at most as many vertices as the word
condition has states. Alternating simulations and positional strategies
supply the bound needed for the finite-search effectivity argument.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ModalSmallModels
open TransitionEncoding TransitionSystems UnfoldAutomata ParityWinningRegions

axiom small_model {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (S : TransitionSystem P)
    (h : Winning (ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) true
      (ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial S.initial)) :
    ∃ T : TransitionSystem P,T.size ≤ M.condition.states ∧
      Winning (ModalAcceptanceGame.game M T) true
        (ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial T.initial)

end Lax369799.ModalSmallModels

statements.signature:
small_model : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P),
  Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M S) Bool.true
      (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial S.initial) →
    Exists fun T =>
      And (instLENat.le T.size M.condition.states)
        (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.game M T) Bool.true
          (Lax369799.ModalAcceptanceGame.position M.condition.initial T.initial))

concepts.title: Modal transitions obtained from type supports
concepts.description:
Section 6.4 replaces each transition tuple by its support. Each type in
the support must occur at some successor, and every successor must have
some type in the support. Nullary transitions test the final word state
and the absence of successors. These conditions are expressible by
finite positive modal formulas.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.BisimAutomata
import Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset

/-!
---
title: Modal transitions obtained from type supports
type: theorem
---
Section 6.4 replaces each transition tuple by its support. Each type in
the support must occur at some successor, and every successor must have
some type in the support. Nullary transitions test the final word state
and the absence of successors. These conditions are expressible by
finite positive modal formulas.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ModalTransitions
open TransitionEncoding TransitionSystems UnfoldAutomata ModalMuCalculus

def Realized {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (ν : Set P) (B : Set (Fin M.unary)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (b : Fin (n + 1) → Fin M.unary), b ∈ M.transition n ν ∧ Set.range b = B

def OneStep {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (q : Fin M.condition.states) (S : TransitionSystem P) (v : S.Vertex)
    (ρ : Fin M.condition.states → Set S.Vertex) : Prop :=
  ((∃ a ∈ M.leafTransition (S.valuation v), M.condition.step q (.inr a) ∈ M.condition.final) ∧
    ∀ w, ¬ S.edge v w) ∨
  ∃ B, Realized M (S.valuation v) B ∧
    (∀ b ∈ B, ∃ w, S.edge v w ∧ w ∈ ρ (M.condition.step q (.inl b))) ∧
    (∀ w, S.edge v w → ∃ b ∈ B, w ∈ ρ (M.condition.step q (.inl b)))

def conjunction {P : Type} {n : ℕ} (l : List (Formula P n)) : Formula P n :=
  l.foldr Formula.conj .top

def disjunction {P : Type} {n : ℕ} (l : List (Formula P n)) : Formula P n :=
  l.foldr Formula.disj .bot

noncomputable def valuationFormula {P : Type} [Fintype P] {n : ℕ} (ν : Set P) : Formula P n := by
  classical
  exact conjunction (Finset.univ.toList.map (fun p =>
    if p ∈ ν then .proposition p else .negProposition p))

noncomputable def supportFormula {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (q : Fin M.condition.states) (B : Set (Fin M.unary)) : Formula P M.condition.states := by
  classical
  let bs := (Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ∈ B)).toList
  exact .conj
    (conjunction (bs.map (fun b => .diamond (.variable (M.condition.step q (.inl b))))))
    (.box (disjunction (bs.map (fun b => .variable (M.condition.step q (.inl b))))))

noncomputable def transitionFormula {P : Type} [Fintype P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (q : Fin M.condition.states) :
    Formula P M.condition.states := by
  classical
  exact disjunction (Finset.univ.toList.map (fun ν : Set P =>
    Formula.conj (valuationFormula ν) (.disj
      (if ∃ a ∈ M.leafTransition ν, M.condition.step q (.inr a) ∈ M.condition.final
        then .box .bot else .bot)
      (disjunction ((Finset.univ.filter (Realized M ν)).toList.map (supportFormula M q))))))

axiom eval_transition {P : Type} [Fintype P]
    (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P)) (q : Fin M.condition.states)
    (S : TransitionSystem P) (ρ : Fin M.condition.states → Set S.Vertex) (v : S.Vertex) :
    v ∈ (transitionFormula M q).eval S ρ ↔ OneStep M q S v ρ

axiom realized_nonempty {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    (ν : Set P) (B : Set (Fin M.unary)) (h : Realized M ν B) : B.Nonempty

def marking {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    {S : RankedSystems.System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0} (r : Run M S)
    (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.val.Vertex) :
    Fin M.condition.states → Set S.val.Vertex :=
  fun p => {w | ∃ i, S.val.graph.edge v i.val (.inl w) ∧
    M.condition.step q (.inl (r.edgeType v i)) = p}

axiom run_marking {P : Type} (M : UnfoldAutomaton (TransitionAlphabet P))
    {S : RankedSystems.System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0} (r : Run M S)
    (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.val.Vertex)
    (hfinal : ∀ h : Rank S v = 0,
      M.condition.step q (.inr (r.leafType v h)) ∈ M.condition.final) :
    OneStep M q (decode S) v (marking M r q v)

end Lax369799.ModalTransitions

statements.signature:
eval_transition : ∀ {P : Type} [inst : Fintype P]
  (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (q : Fin M.condition.states) (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P)
  (ρ : Fin M.condition.states → Set S.Vertex) (v : S.Vertex),
  Iff
    (Set.instMembership.mem
      (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (Lax369799.ModalTransitions.transitionFormula M q) ρ) v)
    (Lax369799.ModalTransitions.OneStep M q S v ρ)

realized_nonempty : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  (ν : Set P) (B : Set (Fin M.unary)), Lax369799.ModalTransitions.Realized M ν B → B.Nonempty

run_marking : ∀ {P : Type} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P))
  {S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.TransitionAlphabet P) 0}
  (r : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.Run M S) (q : Fin M.condition.states) (v : S.val.Vertex),
  (∀ (h : Eq (Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.Rank S v) 0),
      Set.instMembership.mem M.condition.final (M.condition.step q (Sum.inr (r.leafType v h)))) →
    Lax369799.ModalTransitions.OneStep M q (Lax369799.TransitionEncoding.decode S) v
      (Lax369799.ModalTransitions.marking M r q v)

concepts.title: Monadic second-order logic on transition systems
concepts.description:
MSO has vertex variables, set variables, equality, the initial-vertex
predicate, proposition predicates, the edge relation, membership, Boolean
connectives, and quantification over vertices and arbitrary vertex sets.
The two natural-number indices count the free variables of each kind;
a sentence has no free variables. Semantics is given by the usual Tarski
clauses (Section 6.2).
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.TransitionSystems

/-!
---
title: Monadic second-order logic on transition systems
type: definition
---
MSO has vertex variables, set variables, equality, the initial-vertex
predicate, proposition predicates, the edge relation, membership, Boolean
connectives, and quantification over vertices and arbitrary vertex sets.
The two natural-number indices count the free variables of each kind;
a sentence has no free variables. Semantics is given by the usual Tarski
clauses (Section 6.2).
-/

namespace Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder
open TransitionSystems

inductive Formula (P : Type) : ℕ → ℕ → Type
  | equal {m n} : Fin m → Fin m → Formula P m n
  | initial {m n} : Fin m → Formula P m n
  | proposition {m n} : P → Fin m → Formula P m n
  | edge {m n} : Fin m → Fin m → Formula P m n
  | member {m n} : Fin m → Fin n → Formula P m n
  | neg {m n} : Formula P m n → Formula P m n
  | disj {m n} : Formula P m n → Formula P m n → Formula P m n
  | existsVertex {m n} : Formula P (m + 1) n → Formula P m n
  | existsSet {m n} : Formula P m (n + 1) → Formula P m n

def Formula.eval {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) :
    {m n : ℕ} → Formula P m n → (Fin m → S.Vertex) →
    (Fin n → Set S.Vertex) → Prop
  | _, _, .equal x y, ρ, _ => ρ x = ρ y
  | _, _, .initial x, ρ, _ => ρ x = S.initial
  | _, _, .proposition p x, ρ, _ => p ∈ S.valuation (ρ x)
  | _, _, .edge x y, ρ, _ => S.edge (ρ x) (ρ y)
  | _, _, .member x X, ρ, σ => ρ x ∈ σ X
  | _, _, .neg φ, ρ, σ => ¬ φ.eval S ρ σ
  | _, _, .disj φ ψ, ρ, σ => φ.eval S ρ σ ∨ ψ.eval S ρ σ
  | _, _, .existsVertex φ, ρ, σ => ∃ v, φ.eval S (Fin.cases v ρ) σ
  | _, _, .existsSet φ, ρ, σ => ∃ X, φ.eval S ρ (Fin.cases X σ)

abbrev Sentence (P : Type) := Formula P 0 0

def Models {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) (φ : Sentence P) : Prop :=
  φ.eval S Fin.elim0 Fin.elim0

def Definable {P : Type} (L : Set (TransitionSystem P)) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : Sentence P, ∀ S, S ∈ L ↔ Models S φ

end Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder

concepts.title: Morphisms, unfoldings, and yields
concepts.description:
A morphism preserves labels, initial vertices, root vertices, and edges.
Local surjectivity requires equality of the corresponding images at initial
vertices, roots, and the successors of each vertex. Unfold-equivalence means
having a common locally surjective cover. Initial yields are systems with
an unfolding that maps into the given set-system; root yields are their
planted counterparts after uprooting. See Sections 2.3–2.5.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.RankedSystems

/-!
---
title: Morphisms, unfoldings, and yields
type: definition
---
A morphism preserves labels, initial vertices, root vertices, and edges.
Local surjectivity requires equality of the corresponding images at initial
vertices, roots, and the successors of each vertex. Unfold-equivalence means
having a common locally surjective cover. Initial yields are systems with
an unfolding that maps into the given set-system; root yields are their
planted counterparts after uprooting. See Sections 2.3–2.5.
-/

namespace Lax369799.Morphisms
open RankedSystems

structure Morphism {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) where
  toFun : S.Vertex → T.Vertex
  initial : ∀ v, v ∈ S.graph.initial → toFun v ∈ T.graph.initial
  root : ∀ v, v ∈ S.graph.root → toFun v ∈ T.graph.root
  label : ∀ v, T.graph.label (toFun v) = S.graph.label v
  edge : ∀ v d t, S.graph.edge v d t → T.graph.edge (toFun v) d (Sum.map toFun id t)

def Morphism.LocallySurjective {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {S T : SetSystem A n}
    (f : Morphism S T) : Prop :=
  (∀ w ∈ T.graph.initial, ∃ v ∈ S.graph.initial, f.toFun v = w) ∧
  (∀ w ∈ T.graph.root, ∃ v ∈ S.graph.root, f.toFun v = w) ∧
  ∀ v d t, T.graph.edge (f.toFun v) d t →
    ∃ s, S.graph.edge v d s ∧ Sum.map f.toFun id s = t

def Isomorphic {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Morphism S T, Function.Bijective f.toFun ∧ f.LocallySurjective

/-- `UnfoldsTo S T` means that T is an unfolding of S. -/
def UnfoldsTo {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : Morphism T S, f.LocallySurjective

def UnfoldEquivalent {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : SetSystem A n, UnfoldsTo S U ∧ UnfoldsTo T U

def DirectResolution {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S : SetSystem A n)
    (T : System A n) : Prop := Nonempty (Morphism T.val S)

def InitYield {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S : SetSystem A n)
    (T : System A n) : Prop :=
  ∃ D : System A n, DirectResolution S D ∧ UnfoldsTo T.val D.val

def Yield {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) : Prop :=
  (∃ U : System A n, InitYield S U ∧ T = U.val) ∨
  (∃ U : System A n, InitYield (uproot S) U ∧ T = plant U.val)

def YieldBelow {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) : Prop :=
  ∀ U, Yield S U → Yield T U

def YieldEquivalent {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : SetSystem A n) : Prop :=
  ∀ U, Yield S U ↔ Yield T U

abbrev RegularTree (A : RankedSet) (n : ℕ) :=
  Quot (fun (S T : System A n) => UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val)

end Lax369799.Morphisms

concepts.title: Morphism and yield theorems
concepts.description:
The structural results of Sections 2.3–2.5: composition and pullbacks of
morphisms, stability of local surjectivity, equivalence of unfoldings,
and preservation of yields. The pullback includes its universal property
and the local-surjectivity conclusions for both projections.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.Morphisms

/-!
---
title: Morphism and yield theorems
type: theorem
---
The structural results of Sections 2.3–2.5: composition and pullbacks of
morphisms, stability of local surjectivity, equivalence of unfoldings,
and preservation of yields. The pullback includes its universal property
and the local-surjectivity conclusions for both projections.
-/

namespace Lax369799.MorphismTheorems
open RankedSystems Morphisms

axiom composition {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {S T U : SetSystem A n}
    (f : Morphism S T) (g : Morphism T U) :
    ∃ h : Morphism S U, h.toFun = g.toFun ∘ f.toFun ∧
      (f.LocallySurjective → g.LocallySurjective → h.LocallySurjective)

axiom pullback {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {S T U : SetSystem A n}
    (f : Morphism S U) (g : Morphism T U) :
    ∃ (P : SetSystem A n) (p : Morphism P S) (q : Morphism P T),
      f.toFun ∘ p.toFun = g.toFun ∘ q.toFun ∧
      (∀ (V : SetSystem A n) (a : Morphism V S) (b : Morphism V T),
        f.toFun ∘ a.toFun = g.toFun ∘ b.toFun →
        ∃! h : Morphism V P, p.toFun ∘ h.toFun = a.toFun ∧ q.toFun ∘ h.toFun = b.toFun) ∧
      (f.LocallySurjective → q.LocallySurjective) ∧
      (g.LocallySurjective → p.LocallySurjective)

axiom unfold_equivalence (A : RankedSet) (n : ℕ) :
  Equivalence (@UnfoldEquivalent A n)

axiom system_morphism_locally_surjective {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ}
    (S T : System A n) (f : Morphism S.val T.val) : f.LocallySurjective

axiom morphism_yields {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {S T : SetSystem A n}
    (f : Morphism S T) : YieldBelow S T ∧ (f.LocallySurjective → YieldEquivalent S T)

axiom system_yield_equivalence {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S T : System A n) :
  UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val ↔ YieldEquivalent S.val T.val

end Lax369799.MorphismTheorems

statements.signature:
composition : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat} {S T U : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A n}
  (f : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism S T) (g : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism T U),
  Exists fun h =>
    And (Eq h.toFun (Function.comp g.toFun f.toFun)) (f.LocallySurjective → g.LocallySurjective → h.LocallySurjective)

pullback : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat} {S T U : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A n}
  (f : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism S U) (g : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism T U),
  Exists fun P =>
    Exists fun p =>
      Exists fun q =>
        And (Eq (Function.comp f.toFun p.toFun) (Function.comp g.toFun q.toFun))
          (And
            (∀ (V : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A n) (a : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism V S)
              (b : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism V T),
              Eq (Function.comp f.toFun a.toFun) (Function.comp g.toFun b.toFun) →
                ExistsUnique fun h =>
                  And (Eq (Function.comp p.toFun h.toFun) a.toFun) (Eq (Function.comp q.toFun h.toFun) b.toFun))
            (And (f.LocallySurjective → q.LocallySurjective) (g.LocallySurjective → p.LocallySurjective)))

system_morphism_locally_surjective : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat} (S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A n)
  (f : Lax369799.Morphisms.Morphism S.val T.val), f.LocallySurjective

system_yield_equivalence : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat} (S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A n),
  Iff (Lax369799.Morphisms.UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val) (Lax369799.Morphisms.YieldEquivalent S.val T.val)
unfold_equivalence : ∀ (A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet) (n : Nat), Equivalence Lax369799.Morphisms.UnfoldEquivalent

An MSO sentence on finite transition systems defines, through decoding, a

This is `lemma:MSO-is-recognisable` in Section 6.2. The vocabulary uses a

concepts.title: MSO translation and bisimulation invariance of the mu-calculus
concepts.description:
Every modal mu-calculus sentence has an equivalent MSO sentence, and its
truth is preserved by bisimulation. These standard results supply the
reverse implication of the main theorem. The semantic monotonicity lemma
justifies the fixed-point clauses of the mu-calculus semantics.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder
import Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus

/-!
---
title: MSO translation and bisimulation invariance of the mu-calculus
type: theorem
---
Every modal mu-calculus sentence has an equivalent MSO sentence, and its
truth is preserved by bisimulation. These standard results supply the
reverse implication of the main theorem. The semantic monotonicity lemma
justifies the fixed-point clauses of the mu-calculus semantics.
-/

namespace Lax369799.MuCalculusTheorems
open TransitionSystems

axiom eval_monotone {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) {n : ℕ}
    (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) (ρ σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex)
    (h : ∀ i, ρ i ⊆ σ i) : φ.eval S ρ ⊆ φ.eval S σ

axiom mu_to_mso {P : Type} (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) :
  ∃ ψ : MonadicSecondOrder.Sentence P, ∀ S,
    ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ ↔ MonadicSecondOrder.Models S ψ

axiom mu_bisimulation_invariant {P : Type} (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) :
  BisimulationInvariant {S | ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ}

end Lax369799.MuCalculusTheorems

  (ρ σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex),
  (∀ (i : Fin n), Set.instLE.le (ρ i) (σ i)) →
    Set.instLE.le (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S φ ρ) (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S φ σ)

  Lax369799.TransitionSystems.BisimulationInvariant (Set.ofPred fun S => Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ)

  Exists fun ψ =>
    ∀ (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P),
      Iff (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ) (Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder.Models S ψ)

concepts.title: Substitution in modal fixed-point formulas
concepts.description:
Renaming and simultaneous substitution preserve variable binding. Their
semantic laws allow finite systems of modal fixed-point equations to be
eliminated into the scalar syntax of the modal mu-calculus.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus

/-!
---
title: Substitution in modal fixed-point formulas
type: theorem
---
Renaming and simultaneous substitution preserve variable binding. Their
semantic laws allow finite systems of modal fixed-point equations to be
eliminated into the scalar syntax of the modal mu-calculus.
-/
namespace Lax369799.MuSubstitution
open ModalMuCalculus TransitionSystems

def lift {n m : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin m) : Fin (n + 1) → Fin (m + 1) :=
  Fin.cases 0 (fun i => (f i).succ)

def rename {P : Type} {n m : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin m) : Formula P n → Formula P m
  | .top => .top
  | .bot => .bot
  | .proposition p => .proposition p
  | .negProposition p => .negProposition p
  | .variable i => .variable (f i)
  | .conj φ ψ => .conj (rename f φ) (rename f ψ)
  | .disj φ ψ => .disj (rename f φ) (rename f ψ)
  | .diamond φ => .diamond (rename f φ)
  | .box φ => .box (rename f φ)
  | .mu φ => .mu (rename (lift f) φ)
  | .nu φ => .nu (rename (lift f) φ)

def liftSubstitution {P : Type} {n m : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → Formula P m) :
    Fin (n + 1) → Formula P (m + 1) :=
  Fin.cases (.variable 0) (fun i => rename Fin.succ (θ i))

def substitute {P : Type} {n m : ℕ} (θ : Fin n → Formula P m) : Formula P n → Formula P m
  | .top => .top
  | .bot => .bot
  | .proposition p => .proposition p
  | .negProposition p => .negProposition p
  | .variable i => θ i
  | .conj φ ψ => .conj (substitute θ φ) (substitute θ ψ)
  | .disj φ ψ => .disj (substitute θ φ) (substitute θ ψ)
  | .diamond φ => .diamond (substitute θ φ)
  | .box φ => .box (substitute θ φ)
  | .mu φ => .mu (substitute (liftSubstitution θ) φ)
  | .nu φ => .nu (substitute (liftSubstitution θ) φ)

axiom eval_rename {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) {n m : ℕ}
    (φ : Formula P n) (f : Fin n → Fin m) (ρ : Fin m → Set S.Vertex) :
    (rename f φ).eval S ρ = φ.eval S (ρ ∘ f)

axiom eval_substitute {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) {n m : ℕ}
    (φ : Formula P n) (θ : Fin n → Formula P m) (ρ : Fin m → Set S.Vertex) :
    (substitute θ φ).eval S ρ = φ.eval S (fun i => (θ i).eval S ρ)

end Lax369799.MuSubstitution

statements.signature:
eval_rename : ∀ {P : Type} (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) {n m : Nat}
  (φ : Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) (f : Fin n → Fin m) (ρ : Fin m → Set S.Vertex),
  Eq (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (Lax369799.MuSubstitution.rename f φ) ρ)
    (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S φ (Function.comp ρ f))

eval_substitute : ∀ {P : Type} (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) {n m : Nat}
  (φ : Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) (θ : Fin n → Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula P m)
  (ρ : Fin m → Set S.Vertex),
  Eq (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (Lax369799.MuSubstitution.substitute θ φ) ρ)
    (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S φ fun i => Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S (θ i) ρ)

concepts.title: Nonempty powerset algebras
concepts.description:
The nonempty subsets of each sort form an algebra by choosing one allowed
label at each vertex and collecting all resulting evaluations. Nonemptiness
allows arbitrary choices at components removed by reachable restriction.
This construction is used for projections that forget extra vertex marks.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PolynomialContexts
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset

/-!
---
title: Nonempty powerset algebras
type: theorem
---
The nonempty subsets of each sort form an algebra by choosing one allowed
label at each vertex and collecting all resulting evaluations. Nonemptiness
allows arbitrary choices at components removed by reachable restriction.
This construction is used for projections that forget extra vertex marks.
-/
namespace Lax369799.NonemptyPowersets
open RankedSystems Algebras PolynomialContexts

abbrev Carrier (B : RankedSet) : RankedSet := fun n => {s : Set (B n) // s.Nonempty}

def values {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) {n : ℕ} (S : System (Carrier B) n) : Set (B n) :=
  {b | ∃ q : ∀ v, B (S.val.graph.label v).1,
    (∀ v, q v ∈ (S.val.graph.label v).2.val) ∧ E.eval n (withLabels S q) = b}

noncomputable def evaluate {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (n : ℕ)
    (S : System (Carrier B) n) : Carrier B n :=
  ⟨values E S, by
    let q := fun v => Classical.choose (S.val.graph.label v).2.property
    exact ⟨E.eval n (withLabels S q), q,
      fun v => Classical.choose_spec (S.val.graph.label v).2.property, rfl⟩⟩

axiom algebra {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) :
    ∃ F : Algebra (Carrier B), F.eval = evaluate E

axiom finite_carrier {B : RankedSet} (hB : RankwiseFinite B) : RankwiseFinite (Carrier B)

end Lax369799.NonemptyPowersets

statements.signature:
algebra : ∀ {B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B),
  Exists fun F => Eq F.eval (Lax369799.NonemptyPowersets.evaluate E)

finite_carrier : ∀ {B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet},
  Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankwiseFinite B →
    Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankwiseFinite (Lax369799.NonemptyPowersets.Carrier B)

concepts.title: Bounded profiles in root-free substitution patterns
concepts.description:
A finite outer presentation need not be reachable. If its inner set-systems
have no roots, equality of their bounded initial profiles suffices to
transfer every observed value of the closed substitution.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PresentationObservations
import Lax369799.ProfileSubstitution

/-!
---
title: Bounded profiles in root-free substitution patterns
type: theorem
---
A finite outer presentation need not be reachable. If its inner set-systems
have no roots, equality of their bounded initial profiles suffices to
transfer every observed value of the closed substitution.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution
open RankedSystems Algebras

def finiteLabels {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {V : Type}
    (P : Presentation (SetSystem A) n V) :
    Presentation (FinitePresentations.FiniteSystem A) n V := {
  P with label := fun v => ⟨(P.label v).1, FinitePresentations.ofSetSystem (P.label v).2⟩ }

def replaceLabels {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {V : Type}
    (P : Presentation (SetSystem A) n V) (Q : ∀ v, SetSystem A (P.label v).1) :
    Presentation (SetSystem A) n V := { P with label := fun v => ⟨(P.label v).1, Q v⟩ }

axiom transfer_value {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (hE : UnfoldInvariant E)
    [Finite (B 1)] (η : RankedMap A B) {V : Type} [Fintype V]
    (P : Presentation (SetSystem A) 0 V) (Q : ∀ v, SetSystem A (P.label v).1)
    (hP : ∀ v, (P.label v).2.graph.root = ∅) (hQ : ∀ v, (Q v).graph.root = ∅)
    (h : ∀ v, FiniteProfiles.BoundedProfile (Nat.card (B 1) + 1)
        (fun k R => E.eval k (relabelSystem η R)) (P.label v).2 =
      FiniteProfiles.BoundedProfile (Nat.card (B 1) + 1)
        (fun k R => E.eval k (relabelSystem η R)) (Q v)) :
    PresentationObservations.values E η (FinitePresentations.flattenPresentation (finiteLabels P)) ⊆
      PresentationObservations.values E η
        (FinitePresentations.flattenPresentation (finiteLabels (replaceLabels P Q)))

end Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution

statements.signature:
transfer_value : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B),
  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariant E →
    ∀ [Finite (B 1)] (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B) {V : Type} [inst : Fintype V]
      (P : Lax369799.RankedSystems.Presentation (Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A) 0 V)
      (Q : (v : V) → Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A (P.label v).fst),
      (∀ (v : V), Eq (P.label v).snd.graph.root Set.instEmptyCollection.emptyCollection) →
        (∀ (v : V), Eq (Q v).graph.root Set.instEmptyCollection.emptyCollection) →
          (∀ (v : V),
              Eq
                (Lax369799.FiniteProfiles.BoundedProfile (instHAdd.hAdd (Nat.card (B 1)) 1)
                  (fun k R => E.eval k (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η R)) (P.label v).snd)
                (Lax369799.FiniteProfiles.BoundedProfile (instHAdd.hAdd (Nat.card (B 1)) 1)
                  (fun k R => E.eval k (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η R)) (Q v))) →
            Set.instLE.le
              (Lax369799.PresentationObservations.values E η
                (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.flattenPresentation (Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution.finiteLabels P)))
              (Lax369799.PresentationObservations.values E η
                (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.flattenPresentation
                  (Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution.finiteLabels (Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution.replaceLabels P Q))))

concepts.title: Determinization of infinite-word automata
concepts.description:
Every nondeterministic Büchi word automaton has an equivalent finite
deterministic parity word automaton. This is the word-automaton ingredient
of Section 6.3. The parity condition uses the least recurring priority.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata

/-!
---
title: Determinization of infinite-word automata
type: theorem
---
Every nondeterministic Büchi word automaton has an equivalent finite
deterministic parity word automaton. This is the word-automaton ingredient
of Section 6.3. The parity condition uses the least recurring priority.
-/

namespace Lax369799.OmegaDeterminization
open UnfoldAutomata

structure Buchi (alphabet : ℕ) where
  states : ℕ
  initial : Set (Fin states)
  transition : Fin states → Fin alphabet → Fin states → Prop
  accepting : Set (Fin states)

def Buchi.Accepts {u : ℕ} (B : Buchi u) (w : ℕ → Fin u) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℕ → Fin B.states, r 0 ∈ B.initial ∧
    (∀ n, B.transition (r n) (w n) (r (n + 1))) ∧
    {n | r n ∈ B.accepting}.Infinite

axiom determinization {u z : ℕ} (B : Buchi u) :
    ∃ D : WordCondition u z, ∀ w, D.AcceptsInfinite w ↔ B.Accepts w

end Lax369799.OmegaDeterminization

statements.signature:
determinization : ∀ {u z : Nat} (B : Lax369799.OmegaDeterminization.Buchi u),
  Exists fun D => ∀ (w : Nat → Fin u), Iff (D.AcceptsInfinite w) (B.Accepts w)

concepts.title: Regular infinite products of linked pairs
concepts.description:
For a finite monoid, a union of languages V_a(V_e)^ω over linked pairs
ae = a and ee = e is recognized by a deterministic parity word automaton.
Here V_a consists of nonempty words of product a. Increasing cut points
give the nonempty prefix and the successive nonempty blocks explicitly.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.OmegaDeterminization
import Lax369799.WordFactorization

/-!
---
title: Regular infinite products of linked pairs
type: theorem
---
For a finite monoid, a union of languages V_a(V_e)^ω over linked pairs
ae = a and ee = e is recognized by a deterministic parity word automaton.
Here V_a consists of nonempty words of product a. Increasing cut points
give the nonempty prefix and the successive nonempty blocks explicitly.
-/

namespace Lax369799.OmegaProducts
open UnfoldAutomata WordFactorization

def Accepts {M : Type} [Monoid M] {u : ℕ} (f : Fin u → M)
    (P : M → M → Prop) (w : ℕ → Fin u) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a e : M) (cut : ℕ → ℕ), P a e ∧ e * e = e ∧ a * e = a ∧
    StrictMono cut ∧ 0 < cut 0 ∧ block (f ∘ w) 0 (cut 0) = a ∧
    ∀ i, block (f ∘ w) (cut i) (cut (i + 1)) = e

axiom regular {M : Type} [Monoid M] [Finite M] {u z : ℕ}
    (f : Fin u → M) (P : M → M → Prop) :
    ∃ D : WordCondition u z, ∀ w, D.AcceptsInfinite w ↔ Accepts f P w

end Lax369799.OmegaProducts

statements.signature:
regular : ∀ {M : Type} [inst : Monoid M] [Finite M] {u z : Nat} (f : Fin u → M) (P : M → M → Prop),
  Exists fun D => ∀ (w : Nat → Fin u), Iff (D.AcceptsInfinite w) (Lax369799.OmegaProducts.Accepts f P w)

concepts.title: Bounded optimal flatten-resolutions
concepts.description:
Every closed flatten-resolution can be replaced by one whose variable-map
fibres have at most |B₁|+1 elements, preserving the value of its flattening
in an unfold-invariant observing algebra. The additional observation
retains identity continuations at direct hole loops. Only the unary sort
needs to be finite for this step.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ContextSmallification
import Lax369799.ResolutionCompression

/-!
---
title: Bounded optimal flatten-resolutions
type: theorem
---
Every closed flatten-resolution can be replaced by one whose variable-map
fibres have at most |B₁|+1 elements, preserving the value of its flattening
in an unfold-invariant observing algebra. The additional observation
retains identity continuations at direct hole loops. Only the unary sort
needs to be finite for this step.
-/
namespace Lax369799.OptimalResolutions
open RankedSystems Flattening Resolutions Algebras

def BoundedMap {m n : ℕ} (bound : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, Nat.card {i // σ i = j} ≤ bound

axiom optimal_flatten_resolution {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (hE : UnfoldInvariant E)
    [Finite (B 1)] (η : RankedMap A B) (S : SetSystem (SetSystem A) 0)
    (T : System (System A) 0) (r : FlattenResolution S T)
    (R : System A 0) (hR : SystemFlattening T R) :
    ∃ (U : System (System A) 0) (V : System A 0) (r' : FlattenResolution S U),
      SystemFlattening U V ∧
      (∀ v, BoundedMap (Nat.card (B 1) + 1) (r'.variableMap v)) ∧
      E.eval 0 (relabelSystem η R) = E.eval 0 (relabelSystem η V)

end Lax369799.OptimalResolutions

optimal_flatten_resolution : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B),
  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariant E →
    ∀ [Finite (B 1)] (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B)
      (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem (Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A) 0)
      (T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System (Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A) 0)
      (r : Lax369799.Resolutions.FlattenResolution S T) (R : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A 0),
      Lax369799.Flattening.SystemFlattening T R →
        Exists fun U =>

                (And

                  (Eq (E.eval 0 (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η R))
                    (E.eval 0 (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η V))))

concepts.title: Evaluation after compressing parallel tuples
concepts.description:
Taking the meet of each block in a parallel tuple has the same evaluation
as renaming all ports in that block to one output. This is the local
substitution identity used to compress a duplicated run in Lemma 108.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PortReindexing
import Lax369799.CloneTransitions
import Lax369799.DeterministicElements

/-!
---
title: Evaluation after compressing parallel tuples
type: theorem
---
Taking the meet of each block in a parallel tuple has the same evaluation
as renaming all ports in that block to one output. This is the local
substitution identity used to compress a duplicated run in Lemma 108.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ParallelCompression
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FinitePresentations SetSystemAlgebras CloneTransitions PortReindexing
variable {A : RankedSet} {n k : ℕ} (b : Fin (n * k) → A 1)

axiom evaluation (E : SetAlgebra A) :
    E.eval n (ofSetSystem (DeterministicElements.parallel (compress E b))) =
      E.eval n (rename (ofSetSystem (DeterministicElements.parallel b)) (fun i => i.divNat))

end Lax369799.ParallelCompression

statements.signature:
evaluation : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n k : Nat} (b : Fin (instHMul.hMul n k) → A 1)
  (E : Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras.SetAlgebra A),
  Eq
    (E.eval n
      (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.ofSetSystem
        (Lax369799.DeterministicElements.parallel (Lax369799.CloneTransitions.compress E b))))
    (E.eval n
      (Lax369799.PortReindexing.rename
        (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.ofSetSystem (Lax369799.DeterministicElements.parallel b)) fun i => i.divNat))

concepts.title: Parallel replacements in accepting contexts
concepts.description:
The split extremal witness is a parallel tuple of unary values. It lies
below the original value and preserves acceptance in the chosen context.
This is an existence result for accepting contexts, not a normal form for
all deterministic values.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.SplitExtremal
import Lax369799.ExpandedSyntacticAlgebra

/-!
---
title: Parallel replacements in accepting contexts
type: theorem
---
The split extremal witness is a parallel tuple of unary values. It lies
below the original value and preserves acceptance in the chosen context.
This is an existence result for accepting contexts, not a normal form for
all deterministic values.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ParallelReplacement
open RankedSystems (RankedSet)
open FinitePresentations FiniteContexts FiniteContextualOrder FiniteAcceptance FiniteSyntacticAlgebra
open ExpandedSyntacticAlgebra

axiom accepting_parallel {A : RankedSet} (L : Algebras.Language A)
    (hL : Algebras.UnfoldInvariantLanguage L) (hrec : Algebras.Recognizable L)
    (E : SyntacticAlgebra L) {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (C : Context (Carrier (Accepting L)) k 0) (a : Carrier (Accepting L) k)
    (ha : AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug C (atomic a)))) :
    ∃ b : Fin k → Carrier (Accepting L) 1,
      ClassBelow (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval k (ofSetSystem (DeterministicElements.parallel b))) a ∧
      AcceptingClass (Accepting L) (E.algebra.eval 0 (plug C
        (atomic (E.algebra.eval k (ofSetSystem (DeterministicElements.parallel b))))))

end Lax369799.ParallelReplacement

  Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariantLanguage L →
    Lax369799.Algebras.Recognizable L →
      ∀ (E : Lax369799.ExpandedSyntacticAlgebra.SyntacticAlgebra L) {k : Nat},
        instLENat.le 1 k →
          ∀
            (C :
              Lax369799.FiniteContexts.Context
                (Lax369799.FiniteContextualOrder.Carrier (Lax369799.FiniteAcceptance.Accepting L)) k 0)
            (a : Lax369799.FiniteContextualOrder.Carrier (Lax369799.FiniteAcceptance.Accepting L) k),
            Lax369799.FiniteSyntacticAlgebra.AcceptingClass (Lax369799.FiniteAcceptance.Accepting L)
                (E.algebra.eval 0 (Lax369799.FiniteContexts.plug C (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.atomic a))) →
              Exists fun b =>

                  (Lax369799.FiniteContextualOrder.ClassBelow (Lax369799.FiniteAcceptance.Accepting L)

                        (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.atomic
                          (E.algebra.eval k
                            (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.ofSetSystem
                              (Lax369799.DeterministicElements.parallel b)))))))

concepts.title: Eliminating one priority by a fixed point
concepts.description:
Stop a finite parity game on a set of vertices with priority p. A stopped
vertex is winning precisely when the player can force a successor in the
parameter set. Repeated visits to that priority select a greatest fixed
point when p is even and a least fixed point when p is odd. Priorities
above p are allowed only at absorbing vertices; this permits the result
to be iterated with previously stopped priorities.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions
import Mathlib.Order.FixedPoints

/-!
---
title: Eliminating one priority by a fixed point
type: theorem
---
Stop a finite parity game on a set of vertices with priority p. A stopped
vertex is winning precisely when the player can force a successor in the
parameter set. Repeated visits to that priority select a greatest fixed
point when p is even and a least fixed point when p is odd. Priorities
above p are allowed only at absorbing vertices; this permits the result
to be iterated with previously stopped priorities.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ParityFixedPoints
open FiniteParityGames ParityWinningRegions
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

def Owned {V : Type} (G : Game V) (player : Bool) (v : V) : Prop :=
  G.eve v ↔ player = true

def pre {V : Type} (G : Game V) (player : Bool) (X : Set V) : Set V :=
  {v | (Owned G player v → ∃ w, G.edge v w ∧ w ∈ X) ∧
    (¬ Owned G player v → ∀ w, G.edge v w → w ∈ X)}

noncomputable def stop {V : Type} (G : Game V) (C W : Set V) : Game V where
  eve := G.eve
  edge := fun v w => if v ∈ C then w = v else G.edge v w
  priority := fun v => if v ∈ C then if v ∈ W then 0 else 1 else G.priority v
  total := by
    classical
    intro v
    by_cases h : v ∈ C
    · exact ⟨v, by simp [h]⟩
    · obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := G.total v
      exact ⟨w, by simp [h, hw]⟩

noncomputable def phase {V : Type} (G : Game V) (C : Set V) (player : Bool)
    (X : Set V) : Game V :=
  stop G C {v | v ∈ pre G player X ↔ player = true}

axiom greatest {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (C : Set V) (p : ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ v ∈ C, G.priority v = p)
    (hbound : ∀ v, p < G.priority v → ∀ w, G.edge v w → w = v)
    (hp : Even p) : (Winning G true : Set V) = (sSup {X : Set V | X ⊆ Winning (phase G C true X) true} : Set V)

axiom least {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (C : Set V) (p : ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ v ∈ C, G.priority v = p)
    (hbound : ∀ v, p < G.priority v → ∀ w, G.edge v w → w = v)
    (hp : ¬ Even p) : (Winning G true : Set V) = (sInf {X : Set V | Set.Subset (Winning (phase G C true X) true) X} : Set V)

end Lax369799.ParityFixedPoints

greatest : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (C : Set V) (p : Nat),
  (∀ (v : V), Set.instMembership.mem C v → Eq (G.priority v) p) →
    (∀ (v : V), instLTNat.lt p (G.priority v) → ∀ (w : V), G.edge v w → Eq w v) →
      Even p →
        Eq (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true)
          (Set.instSupSet.sSup
            (Set.ofPred fun X =>
              Set.instLE.le X
                (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ParityFixedPoints.phase G C Bool.true X) Bool.true)))

least : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (C : Set V) (p : Nat),
  (∀ (v : V), Set.instMembership.mem C v → Eq (G.priority v) p) →
    (∀ (v : V), instLTNat.lt p (G.priority v) → ∀ (w : V), G.edge v w → Eq w v) →
      Not (Even p) →
        Eq (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true)
          (Set.instInfSet.sInf
            (Set.ofPred fun X =>
              Set.Subset
                (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ParityFixedPoints.phase G C Bool.true X) Bool.true)
                X))

concepts.title: Nested fixed-point equations for finite parity games
concepts.description:
At depth zero every position is stopped and tested by its controlled
predecessor condition. Increasing the depth binds the next priority by a
greatest fixed point for even priorities and a least fixed point for odd
priorities. Once the depth exceeds every priority, these nested equations
define precisely Eve's positional winning region. The free boundary
valuation is then immaterial.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ParityFixedPoints

/-!
---
title: Nested fixed-point equations for finite parity games
type: theorem
---
At depth zero every position is stopped and tested by its controlled
predecessor condition. Increasing the depth binds the next priority by a
greatest fixed point for even priorities and a least fixed point for odd
priorities. Once the depth exceeds every priority, these nested equations
define precisely Eve's positional winning region. The free boundary
valuation is then immaterial.
-/
namespace Lax369799.ParityGameEquations
open FiniteParityGames ParityWinningRegions ParityFixedPoints
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

noncomputable def cut {V : Type} (G : Game V) (n : ℕ) (ρ : ℕ → Set V) : Game V :=
  stop G {v | n ≤ G.priority v} {v | v ∈ pre G true (ρ (G.priority v))}

noncomputable def solve {V : Type} (G : Game V) : ℕ → (ℕ → Set V) → Set V
  | 0, ρ => {v | v ∈ pre G true (ρ (G.priority v))}
  | n + 1, ρ => if Even n then
      sSup {X : Set V | X ⊆ solve G n (Function.update ρ n X)}
    else sInf {X : Set V | Set.Subset (solve G n (Function.update ρ n X)) X}

axiom solve_cut {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (n : ℕ) (ρ : ℕ → Set V) :
    (Winning (cut G n ρ) true : Set V) = solve G n ρ

axiom winning {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (n : ℕ)
    (hn : ∀ v, G.priority v < n) (ρ : ℕ → Set V) :
    (Winning G true : Set V) = solve G n ρ

end Lax369799.ParityGameEquations

statements.signature:
solve_cut : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (n : Nat) (ρ : Nat → Set V),
  Eq (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning (Lax369799.ParityGameEquations.cut G n ρ) Bool.true)
    (Lax369799.ParityGameEquations.solve G n ρ)

winning : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (n : Nat),
  (∀ (v : V), instLTNat.lt (G.priority v) n) →
    ∀ (ρ : Nat → Set V),
      Eq (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true) (Lax369799.ParityGameEquations.solve G n ρ)

concepts.title: Transfer of winning through alternating game simulation
concepts.description:
The simulation preserves owners and priorities, matching Eve's source
choices and lifting Adam's target choices. Finite target determinacy
then transfers a source winning strategy.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions

/-!
---
title: Transfer of winning through alternating game simulation
type: theorem
---
The simulation preserves owners and priorities, matching Eve's source
choices and lifting Adam's target choices. Finite target determinacy
then transfers a source winning strategy.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ParityGameSimulation
open FiniteParityGames

structure Simulation {V W : Type} (G : Game V) (H : Game W) (R : V → W → Prop) where
  owner : ∀ v w,R v w → (G.eve v ↔ H.eve w)
  priority : ∀ v w,R v w → G.priority v = H.priority w
  eve_step : ∀ v w,R v w → G.eve v → ∀ v',G.edge v v' → ∃ w',H.edge w w' ∧ R v' w'
  adam_step : ∀ v w,R v w → ¬G.eve v → ∀ w',H.edge w w' → ∃ v',G.edge v v' ∧ R v' w'

open ParityWinningRegions

axiom winning {V W : Type} [Finite W] (G : Game V) (H : Game W) (R : V → W → Prop)
    (s : Simulation G H R) (v : V) (w : W) (hR : R v w)
    (h : Winning G true v) : Winning H true w

end Lax369799.ParityGameSimulation

statements.signature:
winning : ∀ {V W : Type} [Finite W] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (H : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game W)
  (R : V → W → Prop),
  Lax369799.ParityGameSimulation.Simulation G H R →
    ∀ (v : V) (w : W),
      R v w →
        Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true v → Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning H Bool.true w

concepts.title: Winning regions and controlled predecessors
concepts.description:
The two positional winning regions of a finite parity game partition its
vertices. A single strategy wins throughout each region. Since parity is
unaffected by a finite prefix, the winning region is stable under the
corresponding controlled predecessor operation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.FiniteParityGames

/-!
---
title: Winning regions and controlled predecessors
type: theorem
---
The two positional winning regions of a finite parity game partition its
vertices. A single strategy wins throughout each region. Since parity is
unaffected by a finite prefix, the winning region is stable under the
corresponding controlled predecessor operation.
-/

namespace Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions
open FiniteParityGames

def Winning {V : Type} (G : Game V) (player : Bool) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f, G.Legal player f ∧ G.WinsFrom player f v

def Pre {V : Type} (G : Game V) (X : Set V) : Set V :=
  {v | (G.eve v → ∃ w, G.edge v w ∧ w ∈ X) ∧
    (¬ G.eve v → ∀ w, G.edge v w → w ∈ X)}

axiom move {V : Type} (G : Game V) (player : Bool) (f : V → V) (v w : V)
    (hv : G.WinsFrom player f v) (he : G.edge v w)
    (hf : (G.eve v ↔ player = true) → w = f v) : G.WinsFrom player f w

axiom disjoint {V : Type} (G : Game V) (v : V) :
    ¬ (Winning G true v ∧ Winning G false v)

axiom uniform {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (player : Bool) :
    ∃ f, G.Legal player f ∧ ∀ v, Winning G player v → G.WinsFrom player f v

axiom complementary {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (v : V) :
    Winning G false v ↔ ¬ Winning G true v

axiom predecessor {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Game V) (v : V) :
    Winning G true v ↔ v ∈ Pre G (Winning G true)

end Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions

statements.signature:
complementary : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (v : V),
  Iff (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.false v)
    (Not (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true v))

disjoint : ∀ {V : Type} (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (v : V),
  Not
    (And (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true v) (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.false v))

move : ∀ {V : Type} (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (player : Bool) (f : V → V) (v w : V),
  G.WinsFrom player f v → G.edge v w → (Iff (G.eve v) (Eq player Bool.true) → Eq w (f v)) → G.WinsFrom player f w

predecessor : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (v : V),
  Iff (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true v)
    (Set.instMembership.mem (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Pre G (Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G Bool.true))
      v)

uniform : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : Lax369799.FiniteParityGames.Game V) (player : Bool),
  Exists fun f =>
    And (G.Legal player f) (∀ (v : V), Lax369799.ParityWinningRegions.Winning G player v → G.WinsFrom player f v)

concepts.title: Finite path-summary algebras
concepts.description:
An element records, for each entry state, the possible final states and
variable exits with their states. Evaluation follows a finite path through
the system, composing local summaries. This gives a rankwise-finite algebra
when the state set is finite, suitable for recognizing local predicates
along paths from the initial vertex.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.InitialAlgebra
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod

/-!
---
title: Finite path-summary algebras
type: theorem
---
An element records, for each entry state, the possible final states and
variable exits with their states. Evaluation follows a finite path through
the system, composing local summaries. This gives a rankwise-finite algebra
when the state set is finite, suitable for recognizing local predicates
along paths from the initial vertex.
-/
namespace Lax369799.PathAlgebra
open RankedSystems Algebras InitialAlgebra

abbrev Result (Q : Type) (n : ℕ) := Q ⊕ (Fin n × Q)
abbrev Carrier (Q : Type) : RankedSet := fun n => Q → Set (Result Q n)

def Halt {Q : Type} (a : Symbol (Carrier Q)) (q r : Q) : Prop :=
  Sum.inl r ∈ a.2 q

def Exit {Q : Type} (a : Symbol (Carrier Q)) (d : ℕ) (q r : Q) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : Fin a.1, i.val = d ∧ Sum.inr (i, r) ∈ a.2 q

inductive Run {Q V : Type} {n : ℕ} (G : Presentation (Carrier Q) n V) :
    V → Q → Result Q n → Prop
  | halt {v q r} (h : Halt (G.label v) q r) : Run G v q (.inl r)
  | exit {v q r i} (d : ℕ)
      (h : Exit (G.label v) d q r) (he : G.edge v d (.inr i)) :
      Run G v q (.inr (i, r))
  | step {v w q r out} (d : ℕ)
      (h : Exit (G.label v) d q r) (he : G.edge v d (.inl w))
      (tail : Run G w r out) : Run G v q out

noncomputable def evaluate {Q : Type} (n : ℕ) (S : System (Carrier Q) n) : Carrier Q n :=
  fun q out => Run S.val.graph (initial S) q out

axiom algebra (Q : Type) : ∃ E : Algebra (Carrier Q), E.eval = evaluate

axiom finite_carrier (Q : Type) [Finite Q] : RankwiseFinite (Carrier Q)

end Lax369799.PathAlgebra

statements.signature: algebra : ∀ (Q : Type), Exists fun E => Eq E.eval Lax369799.PathAlgebra.evaluate
finite_carrier : ∀ (Q : Type) [Finite Q], Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankwiseFinite (Lax369799.PathAlgebra.Carrier Q)

concepts.title: Ultimately periodic witnesses in finite parity graphs
concepts.description:
Every infinite path in a finite graph has an ultimately periodic path
with the same initial vertex and least recurring priority. This supplies
the periodic witness for checking a finite-state parity branch condition.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.WordParity

/-!
---
title: Ultimately periodic witnesses in finite parity graphs
type: theorem
---
Every infinite path in a finite graph has an ultimately periodic path
with the same initial vertex and least recurring priority. This supplies
the periodic witness for checking a finite-state parity branch condition.
-/
namespace Lax369799.PeriodicPaths

def UltimatelyPeriodic {Q : Type} (r : ℕ → Q) : Prop :=
  ∃ N p, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n, N ≤ n → r (n + p) = r n

axiom periodic_witness {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (R : Q → Q → Prop)
    (priority : Q → ℕ) (r : ℕ → Q) (hr : ∀ n, R (r n) (r (n + 1)))
    (c : ℕ) (hc : WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c) :
    ∃ s : ℕ → Q, s 0 = r 0 ∧ (∀ n, R (s n) (s (n + 1))) ∧
      UltimatelyPeriodic s ∧ WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (s n)) c

axiom periodic_test {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (R : Q → Q → Prop)
    (priority : Q → ℕ) (q : Q) :
    (∀ r : ℕ → Q, r 0 = q → (∀ n, R (r n) (r (n + 1))) → UltimatelyPeriodic r →
      ∃ c, Even c ∧ WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c) ↔
    (∀ r : ℕ → Q, r 0 = q → (∀ n, R (r n) (r (n + 1))) →
      ∃ c, Even c ∧ WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c)

end Lax369799.PeriodicPaths

statements.signature:
periodic_test : ∀ {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (R : Q → Q → Prop) (priority : Q → Nat) (q : Q),
  Iff
    (∀ (r : Nat → Q),
      Eq (r 0) q →
        (∀ (n : Nat), R (r n) (r (instHAdd.hAdd n 1))) →
          Lax369799.PeriodicPaths.UltimatelyPeriodic r →
            Exists fun c => And (Even c) (Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c))
    (∀ (r : Nat → Q),
      Eq (r 0) q →
        (∀ (n : Nat), R (r n) (r (instHAdd.hAdd n 1))) →
          Exists fun c => And (Even c) (Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c))

periodic_witness : ∀ {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (R : Q → Q → Prop) (priority : Q → Nat) (r : Nat → Q),
  (∀ (n : Nat), R (r n) (r (instHAdd.hAdd n 1))) →
    ∀ (c : Nat),
      Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c →
        Exists fun s =>
          And (Eq (s 0) (r 0))
            (And (∀ (n : Nat), R (s n) (s (instHAdd.hAdd n 1)))
              (And (Lax369799.PeriodicPaths.UltimatelyPeriodic s)
                (Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (s n)) c)))

concepts.title: Polynomial contexts of a system algebra
concepts.description:
Polynomial contexts are functions obtained from a variable and constants by
system evaluation. They may use the variable at several vertices. Testing
all closed polynomial contexts against an accepting set gives a congruence
for evaluation. This construction does not presume unfolding invariance.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.Algebras

/-!
---
title: Polynomial contexts of a system algebra
type: theorem
---
Polynomial contexts are functions obtained from a variable and constants by
system evaluation. They may use the variable at several vertices. Testing
all closed polynomial contexts against an accepting set gives a congruence
for evaluation. This construction does not presume unfolding invariance.
-/
namespace Lax369799.PolynomialContexts
open RankedSystems Algebras

abbrev Shape := System (fun _ => Unit)

def withLabels {A B : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (P : System A n)
    (f : ∀ v, B (P.val.graph.label v).1) : System B n :=
  ⟨{ P.val with graph := { P.val.graph with label := fun v => ⟨(P.val.graph.label v).1, f v⟩ } }, P.property⟩

inductive Polynomial {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (k : ℕ) : ∀ n, (B k → B n) → Prop
  | variable : Polynomial E k k id
  | constant (n : ℕ) (b : B n) : Polynomial E k n (fun _ => b)
  | evaluation {n : ℕ} (P : Shape n) (f : ∀ v, B k → B (P.val.graph.label v).1)
      (hf : ∀ v, Polynomial E k (P.val.graph.label v).1 (f v)) :
      Polynomial E k n (fun x => E.eval n (withLabels P (fun v => f v x)))

def Equivalent {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) {n : ℕ} (a b : B n) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : B n → B 0, Polynomial E n 0 p → (p a ∈ F ↔ p b ∈ F)

axiom composition {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) {k m n : ℕ}
    {f : B m → B n} {g : B k → B m} (hf : Polynomial E m n f) (hg : Polynomial E k m g) :
    Polynomial E k n (f ∘ g)

axiom evaluation_congruence {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0))
    {n : ℕ} (P : System A n) (q r : ∀ v, B (P.val.graph.label v).1)
    (h : ∀ v, Equivalent E F (q v) (r v)) :
    Equivalent E F (E.eval n (withLabels P q)) (E.eval n (withLabels P r))

end Lax369799.PolynomialContexts

statements.signature:
composition : ∀ {B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B) {k m n : Nat} {f : B m → B n}
  {g : B k → B m},
  Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.Polynomial E m n f →
    Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.Polynomial E k m g → Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.Polynomial E k n (Function.comp f g)

evaluation_congruence : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) {n : Nat}
  (P : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A n) (q r : (v : Fin P.val.size) → B (P.val.graph.label v).fst),
  (∀ (v : Fin P.val.size), Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.Equivalent E F (q v) (r v)) →
    Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.Equivalent E F (E.eval n (Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.withLabels P q))
      (E.eval n (Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.withLabels P r))

concepts.title: Quotients by polynomial acceptance tests
concepts.description:
Testing all closed polynomial contexts against an accepting set defines
an algebra congruence. Evaluation descends to the quotient, the quotient
preserves recognition, and finite sorts remain finite.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PolynomialContexts

/-!
---
title: Quotients by polynomial acceptance tests
type: theorem
---
Testing all closed polynomial contexts against an accepting set defines
an algebra congruence. Evaluation descends to the quotient, the quotient
preserves recognition, and finite sorts remain finite.
-/
namespace Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient
open RankedSystems Algebras PolynomialContexts

abbrev Carrier {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) : RankedSet :=
  fun n => Quot (@Equivalent B E F n)

def classMap {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) : RankedMap B (Carrier E F) :=
  fun _ => Quot.mk _

def Accepting {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) (a : Carrier E F 0) : Prop :=
  ∃ b, classMap E F 0 b = a ∧ b ∈ F

axiom algebra {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) :
    ∃ Q : Algebra (Carrier E F), ∀ n (S : System B n),
      Q.eval n (relabelSystem (classMap E F) S) = classMap E F n (E.eval n S)

axiom finite_carrier {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0))
    (hB : RankwiseFinite B) : RankwiseFinite (Carrier E F)

axiom accepting_class {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) (b : B 0) :
    Accepting E F (classMap E F 0 b) ↔ b ∈ F

axiom recognition {A B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0))
    (Q : Algebra (Carrier E F))
    (hQ : ∀ n (S : System B n), Q.eval n (relabelSystem (classMap E F) S) = classMap E F n (E.eval n S))
    (η : RankedMap A B) (L : Language A) (hL : Recognizes E η F L) :
    Recognizes Q (fun n a => classMap E F n (η n a)) (Accepting E F) L

end Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient

  Iff (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.Accepting E F (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F 0 b))
    (Set.instMembership.mem F b)

  Exists fun Q =>
    ∀ (n : Nat) (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System B n),
      Eq (Q.eval n (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F) S))
        (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F n (E.eval n S))

  Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankwiseFinite B →
    Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankwiseFinite (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.Carrier E F)

recognition : ∀ {A B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0))
  (Q : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.Carrier E F)),
  (∀ (n : Nat) (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System B n),
      Eq (Q.eval n (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F) S))
        (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F n (E.eval n S))) →
    ∀ (η : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedMap A B) (L : Lax369799.Algebras.Language A),
      Lax369799.Algebras.Recognizes E η F L →
        Lax369799.Algebras.Recognizes Q (fun n a => Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F n (η n a))
          (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.Accepting E F) L

concepts.title: Unfolding through polynomial contexts
concepts.description:
A polynomial applied to a system value can be realized by an actual system.
For unfold-equivalent inputs, choose unfold-equivalent realizations. Thus
closed acceptance invariance under unfolding makes the polynomial quotient
an unfolding-invariant algebra in every rank.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient
import Lax369799.SystemSubstitution

/-!
---
title: Unfolding through polynomial contexts
type: theorem
---
A polynomial applied to a system value can be realized by an actual system.
For unfold-equivalent inputs, choose unfold-equivalent realizations. Thus
closed acceptance invariance under unfolding makes the polynomial quotient
an unfolding-invariant algebra in every rank.
-/
namespace Lax369799.PolynomialUnfolding
open RankedSystems Algebras Morphisms PolynomialContexts

def ClosedInvariant {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)) : Prop :=
  ∀ S T : System B 0, UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val → (E.eval 0 S ∈ F ↔ E.eval 0 T ∈ F)

axiom realization {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) {k n : ℕ} {p : B k → B n}
    (hp : Polynomial E k n p) (S T : System B k) (h : UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val) :
    ∃ U V : System B n, E.eval n U = p (E.eval k S) ∧ E.eval n V = p (E.eval k T) ∧
      UnfoldEquivalent U.val V.val

axiom quotient_unfold_invariant {B : RankedSet} (E : Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0))
    (hF : ClosedInvariant E F) (Q : Algebra (PolynomialQuotient.Carrier E F))
    (hQ : ∀ n (S : System B n), Q.eval n (relabelSystem (PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F) S) =
      PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F n (E.eval n S)) : UnfoldInvariant Q

end Lax369799.PolynomialUnfolding

statements.signature:
quotient_unfold_invariant : ∀ {B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B) (F : Set (B 0)),
  Lax369799.PolynomialUnfolding.ClosedInvariant E F →
    ∀ (Q : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.Carrier E F)),
      (∀ (n : Nat) (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System B n),
          Eq (Q.eval n (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F) S))
            (Lax369799.PolynomialQuotient.classMap E F n (E.eval n S))) →
        Lax369799.Algebras.UnfoldInvariant Q

realization : ∀ {B : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (E : Lax369799.Algebras.Algebra B) {k n : Nat} {p : B k → B n},
  Lax369799.PolynomialContexts.Polynomial E k n p →
    ∀ (S T : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System B k),
      Lax369799.Morphisms.UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val →
        Exists fun U =>
          Exists fun V =>
            And (Eq (E.eval n U) (p (E.eval k S)))
              (And (Eq (E.eval n V) (p (E.eval k T))) (Lax369799.Morphisms.UnfoldEquivalent U.val V.val))

concepts.title: Substitution after reindexing directions
concepts.description:
Reindexing the directions of an outer system and renaming the ports of
its substituted pieces give the same flattened graph. Evaluation is
therefore unchanged. All vertices and marks are retained.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.DirectionReindexing
import Lax369799.SetSystemAlgebras

/-!
---
title: Substitution after reindexing directions
type: theorem
---
Reindexing the directions of an outer system and renaming the ports of
its substituted pieces give the same flattened graph. Evaluation is
therefore unchanged. All vertices and marks are retained.
-/
namespace Lax369799.PortReindexing
open RankedSystems (RankedSet System)
open TransitionEncoding FinitePresentations SetSystemAlgebras DirectionReindexing

def rename {Y : RankedSet} {m n : ℕ} (P : FiniteSystem Y m) (σ : Fin m → Fin n) :
    FiniteSystem Y n where
  size := P.size
  graph := {
    label := P.graph.label
    initial := P.graph.initial
    root := P.graph.root
    edge := fun v d t => match t with
      | .inl w => P.graph.edge v d (.inl w)
      | .inr i => ∃ j, σ j = i ∧ P.graph.edge v d (.inr j)
    direction_valid := by
      intro v d t h
      cases t with
      | inl w => exact P.graph.direction_valid _ _ _ h
      | inr i => obtain ⟨j, _, hj⟩ := h; exact P.graph.direction_valid _ _ _ hj }


axiom evaluation {P : Type} {Y : RankedSet} (S : System (TransitionAlphabet P) 0)
    (R : Reindexing S) (B : ∀ v : S.val.Vertex, FiniteSystem Y (R.arity v)) (E : SetAlgebra Y) :
    E.eval 0 (withLabels (ofSetSystem S.val) (fun v => E.eval _ (rename (B v) (R.map v)))) =
      E.eval 0 (withLabels (ofSetSystem (DirectionReindexing.system S R).val)
        (fun v => E.eval _ (B v)))

end Lax369799.PortReindexing
