      (∀ (v : V), Eq (P.label v).snd.graph.root Set.instEmptyCollection.emptyCollection) →
        (∀ (v : V), Eq (Q v).graph.root Set.instEmptyCollection.emptyCollection) →
          (∀ (v : V),
              Eq
                (Lax369799.Resolutions.Profile (fun k R => E.eval k (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η R))
                  (P.label v).snd)
                (Lax369799.Resolutions.Profile (fun k R => E.eval k (Lax369799.RankedSystems.relabelSystem η R))
                  (Q v))) →
            Set.instLE.le
              (Lax369799.PresentationObservations.values E η
                (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.flattenPresentation (Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution.finiteLabels P)))
              (Lax369799.PresentationObservations.values E η
                (Lax369799.FinitePresentations.flattenPresentation
                  (Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution.finiteLabels (Lax369799.ObservedSubstitution.replaceLabels P Q))))

concepts.title: Unfold-automata and regular-tree acceptance
concepts.description:
An unfold-automaton has finitely many unary and nullary types. At each
internal vertex it chooses a tuple of unary types, one for each outgoing
direction; at a leaf it chooses a nullary type. Every branch must satisfy
a common regular word condition. Here that condition is represented by a
finite deterministic parity word automaton, with a final-state condition
for finite words. Parity uses the least priority occurring infinitely
often, which must be even.

Acceptance permits a run on any finite system representing the same
regular tree, as in Section 6.3; a run on the input presentation alone is
not required. Both finite branches ending at leaves and infinite branches
are checked.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.Algebras
import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Parity

/-!
---
title: Unfold-automata and regular-tree acceptance
type: definition
---
An unfold-automaton has finitely many unary and nullary types. At each
internal vertex it chooses a tuple of unary types, one for each outgoing
direction; at a leaf it chooses a nullary type. Every branch must satisfy
a common regular word condition. Here that condition is represented by a
finite deterministic parity word automaton, with a final-state condition
for finite words. Parity uses the least priority occurring infinitely
often, which must be even.

Acceptance permits a run on any finite system representing the same
regular tree, as in Section 6.3; a run on the input presentation alone is
not required. Both finite branches ending at leaves and infinite branches
are checked.
-/

namespace Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata
open RankedSystems Morphisms Algebras

structure WordCondition (unary nullary : ℕ) where
  states : ℕ
  initial : Fin states
  step : Fin states → (Fin unary ⊕ Fin nullary) → Fin states
  priority : Fin states → ℕ
  final : Set (Fin states)

def WordCondition.run {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z) (w : ℕ → Fin u) : ℕ → Fin D.states
  | 0 => D.initial
  | n + 1 => D.step (D.run w n) (.inl (w n))

def WordCondition.AcceptsInfinite {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z)
    (w : ℕ → Fin u) : Prop :=
  ∃ c, Even c ∧ (∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ D.priority (D.run w n) = c) ∧
    ∀ b, b < c → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → D.priority (D.run w n) ≠ b

def WordCondition.AcceptsFinite {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z)
    (w : List (Fin u)) (a : Fin z) : Prop :=
  D.step (w.foldl (fun q b => D.step q (.inl b)) D.initial) (.inr a) ∈ D.final

structure UnfoldAutomaton (A : RankedSet) where
  unary : ℕ
  nullary : ℕ
  transition : ∀ n, A (n + 1) → Set (Fin (n + 1) → Fin unary)
  leafTransition : A 0 → Set (Fin nullary)
  condition : WordCondition unary nullary

abbrev Rank {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S : System A n) (v : S.val.Vertex) :=
  (S.val.graph.label v).1

/-- An assignment of branch types, before imposing transition constraints. -/
structure Labelling {A : RankedSet} (u z : ℕ) (S : System A 0) where
  edgeType : ∀ v, Fin (Rank S v) → Fin u
  leafType : ∀ v, Rank S v = 0 → Fin z

structure Run {A : RankedSet} (M : UnfoldAutomaton A) (S : System A 0) where
  edgeType : ∀ v, Fin (Rank S v) → Fin M.unary
  leafType : ∀ v, Rank S v = 0 → Fin M.nullary
  transitions : ∀ v k (h : Rank S v = k + 1),
    (fun i => edgeType v (Fin.cast h.symm i)) ∈
      M.transition k (h ▸ (S.val.graph.label v).2)
  leaves : ∀ v (h : Rank S v = 0),
    leafType v h ∈ M.leafTransition (h ▸ (S.val.graph.label v).2)

abbrev Run.toLabelling {A : RankedSet} {M : UnfoldAutomaton A} {S : System A 0}
    (r : Run M S) : Labelling M.unary M.nullary S := ⟨r.edgeType, r.leafType⟩

/-- The automaton imposing only the branch condition. -/
def unrestricted {A : RankedSet} {u z : ℕ} (D : WordCondition u z) : UnfoldAutomaton A :=
  ⟨u, z, fun _ _ => Set.univ, fun _ => Set.univ, D⟩

def Labelling.asRun {A : RankedSet} {u z : ℕ} {S : System A 0}
    (r : Labelling u z S) (D : WordCondition u z) : Run (unrestricted D) S :=
  ⟨r.edgeType, r.leafType, fun _ _ _ => trivial, fun _ _ => trivial⟩

structure FiniteBranch {A : RankedSet} (S : System A 0) (length : ℕ) where
  vertex : Fin (length + 1) → S.val.Vertex
  direction : ∀ i : Fin length, Fin (Rank S (vertex i.castSucc))
  starts : vertex 0 ∈ S.val.graph.initial
  follows : ∀ i, S.val.graph.edge (vertex i.castSucc) (direction i).val (.inl (vertex i.succ))
  ends : Rank S (vertex (Fin.last length)) = 0

structure InfiniteBranch {A : RankedSet} (S : System A 0) where
  vertex : ℕ → S.val.Vertex
  direction : ∀ i, Fin (Rank S (vertex i))
  starts : vertex 0 ∈ S.val.graph.initial
  follows : ∀ i, S.val.graph.edge (vertex i) (direction i).val (.inl (vertex (i + 1)))

def Run.Accepting {A : RankedSet} {M : UnfoldAutomaton A} {S : System A 0}
    (r : Run M S) : Prop :=
  (∀ k (b : FiniteBranch S k), M.condition.AcceptsFinite
    (List.ofFn (fun i => r.edgeType (b.vertex i.castSucc) (b.direction i)))
    (r.leafType (b.vertex (Fin.last k)) b.ends)) ∧
  (∀ b : InfiniteBranch S, M.condition.AcceptsInfinite
    (fun i => r.edgeType (b.vertex i) (b.direction i)))

def Labelling.Accepting {A : RankedSet} {u z : ℕ} {S : System A 0}
    (r : Labelling u z S) (D : WordCondition u z) : Prop := (r.asRun D).Accepting

def Accepts {A : RankedSet} (M : UnfoldAutomaton A) (S : System A 0) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : System A 0, UnfoldEquivalent S.val T.val ∧ ∃ r : Run M T, r.Accepting

def Recognizes {A : RankedSet} (M : UnfoldAutomaton A) (L : Language A) : Prop :=
  ∀ S, S ∈ L ↔ Accepts M S

end Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata

concepts.title: Periodic branch test for unfold-automata
concepts.description:
On a finite system, checking the parity condition on ultimately periodic
branches suffices for all infinite branches. Periodicity records both the
vertex and the chosen outgoing direction.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.PeriodicPaths

/-!
---
title: Periodic branch test for unfold-automata
type: theorem
---
On a finite system, checking the parity condition on ultimately periodic
branches suffices for all infinite branches. Periodicity records both the
vertex and the chosen outgoing direction.
-/
namespace Lax369799.UnfoldBranches
open RankedSystems UnfoldAutomata

def Periodic {A : RankedSet} {S : System A 0} (b : InfiniteBranch S) : Prop :=
  PeriodicPaths.UltimatelyPeriodic
    (fun n => (⟨b.vertex n, b.direction n⟩ : (v : S.val.Vertex) × Fin (Rank S v)))

axiom periodic_test {A : RankedSet} (M : UnfoldAutomaton A) (S : System A 0) (r : Run M S) :
    (∀ b : InfiniteBranch S, Periodic b → M.condition.AcceptsInfinite
      (fun n => r.edgeType (b.vertex n) (b.direction n))) ↔
    (∀ b : InfiniteBranch S, M.condition.AcceptsInfinite
      (fun n => r.edgeType (b.vertex n) (b.direction n)))

end Lax369799.UnfoldBranches

statements.signature:
periodic_test : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} (M : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.UnfoldAutomaton A)
  (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A 0) (r : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.Run M S),
  Iff
    (∀ (b : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.InfiniteBranch S),
      Lax369799.UnfoldBranches.Periodic b →
        M.condition.AcceptsInfinite fun n => r.edgeType (b.vertex n) (b.direction n))
    (∀ (b : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.InfiniteBranch S),
      M.condition.AcceptsInfinite fun n => r.edgeType (b.vertex n) (b.direction n))

concepts.title: Logic on arbitrary transition systems
concepts.description:
Transition systems may have arbitrary state spaces. The usual MSO and
modal fixed-point semantics agree with the finite-system semantics on
finite presentations. The modal mu-calculus translates to MSO and is
bisimulation invariant on arbitrary state spaces.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems
import Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder
import Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus
import Mathlib.Order.FixedPoints
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Lattice

/-!
---
title: Logic on arbitrary transition systems
type: theorem
---
Transition systems may have arbitrary state spaces. The usual MSO and
modal fixed-point semantics agree with the finite-system semantics on
finite presentations. The modal mu-calculus translates to MSO and is
bisimulation invariant on arbitrary state spaces.
-/

namespace Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic
open UnrestrictedTransitionSystems

def muEval {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) :
    {n : ℕ} → ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n → (Fin n → Set S.Vertex) → Set S.Vertex
  | _, .top, _ => Set.univ
  | _, .bot, _ => ∅
  | _, .proposition p, _ => {v | p ∈ S.valuation v}
  | _, .negProposition p, _ => {v | p ∉ S.valuation v}
  | _, .variable i, ρ => ρ i
  | _, .conj φ ψ, ρ => muEval S φ ρ ∩ muEval S ψ ρ
  | _, .disj φ ψ, ρ => muEval S φ ρ ∪ muEval S ψ ρ
  | _, .diamond φ, ρ => {v | ∃ w, S.edge v w ∧ w ∈ muEval S φ ρ}
  | _, .box φ, ρ => {v | ∀ w, S.edge v w → w ∈ muEval S φ ρ}
  | _, .mu φ, ρ => sInf {X | muEval S φ (Fin.cases X ρ) ⊆ X}
  | _, .nu φ, ρ => sSup {X | X ⊆ muEval S φ (Fin.cases X ρ)}

def msoEval {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) :
    {m n : ℕ} → MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n → (Fin m → S.Vertex) →
      (Fin n → Set S.Vertex) → Prop
  | _, _, .equal x y, ρ, _ => ρ x = ρ y
  | _, _, .initial x, ρ, _ => ρ x = S.initial
  | _, _, .proposition p x, ρ, _ => p ∈ S.valuation (ρ x)
  | _, _, .edge x y, ρ, _ => S.edge (ρ x) (ρ y)
  | _, _, .member x X, ρ, σ => ρ x ∈ σ X
  | _, _, .neg φ, ρ, σ => ¬ msoEval S φ ρ σ
  | _, _, .disj φ ψ, ρ, σ => msoEval S φ ρ σ ∨ msoEval S ψ ρ σ
  | _, _, .existsVertex φ, ρ, σ => ∃ v, msoEval S φ (Fin.cases v ρ) σ
  | _, _, .existsSet φ, ρ, σ => ∃ X, msoEval S φ ρ (Fin.cases X σ)

def MuModels {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) : Prop :=
  S.initial ∈ muEval S φ Fin.elim0

def MSOModels {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) (φ : MonadicSecondOrder.Sentence P) : Prop :=
  msoEval S φ Fin.elim0 Fin.elim0

def MuDefinable {P : Type} (L : Set (TransitionSystem P)) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P, ∀ S, S ∈ L ↔ MuModels S φ

def MSODefinable {P : Type} (L : Set (TransitionSystem P)) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : MonadicSecondOrder.Sentence P, ∀ S, S ∈ L ↔ MSOModels S φ

def conjunction {P : Type} {m n : ℕ}
    (φ ψ : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n) : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n :=
  .neg (.disj (.neg φ) (.neg ψ))

def implication {P : Type} {m n : ℕ}
    (φ ψ : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n) : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n :=
  .disj (.neg φ) ψ

def allVertex {P : Type} {m n : ℕ}
    (φ : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P (m + 1) n) : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n :=
  .neg (.existsVertex (.neg φ))

def allSet {P : Type} {m n : ℕ}
    (φ : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m (n + 1)) : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n :=
  .neg (.existsSet (.neg φ))

/-- Translate satisfaction at a designated first-order variable. -/
def translate {P : Type} : {n : ℕ} → ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n →
    {m : ℕ} → Fin m → MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n
  | _, .top, _, x => .equal x x
  | _, .bot, _, x => .neg (.equal x x)
  | _, .proposition p, _, x => .proposition p x
  | _, .negProposition p, _, x => .neg (.proposition p x)
  | _, .variable i, _, x => .member x i
  | _, .conj φ ψ, _, x => conjunction (translate φ x) (translate ψ x)
  | _, .disj φ ψ, _, x => .disj (translate φ x) (translate ψ x)
  | _, .diamond φ, _, x => .existsVertex (conjunction (.edge x.succ 0) (translate φ 0))
  | _, .box φ, _, x => allVertex (implication (.edge x.succ 0) (translate φ 0))
  | _, .mu φ, _, x => allSet (implication
      (allVertex (implication (translate φ 0) (.member 0 0))) (.member x 0))
  | _, .nu φ, _, x => .existsSet (conjunction (.member x 0)
      (allVertex (implication (.member 0 0) (translate φ 0))))

def sentence {P : Type} (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) : MonadicSecondOrder.Sentence P :=
  .existsVertex (conjunction (.initial 0) (translate φ 0))

axiom finite_mu {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) {n : ℕ}
    (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) (ρ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex) :
    muEval (ofFinite S) φ ρ = φ.eval S ρ

axiom finite_mso {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) {m n : ℕ}
    (φ : MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n) (ρ : Fin m → S.Vertex) (σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex) :
    msoEval (ofFinite S) φ ρ σ ↔ φ.eval S ρ σ

axiom eval_monotone {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) {n : ℕ}
    (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) (ρ σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex)
    (h : ∀ i, ρ i ⊆ σ i) : muEval S φ ρ ⊆ muEval S φ σ

axiom translate_correct {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystem P) {n : ℕ}
    (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) {m : ℕ} (x : Fin m)
    (ρ : Fin m → S.Vertex) (σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex) :
    msoEval S (translate φ x) ρ σ ↔ ρ x ∈ muEval S φ σ

axiom mu_to_mso {P : Type} (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) :
    ∃ ψ : MonadicSecondOrder.Sentence P, ∀ S : TransitionSystem P,
      MuModels S φ ↔ MSOModels S ψ

axiom mu_bisimulation_invariant {P : Type} (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) :
    BisimulationInvariant {S | MuModels S φ}

axiom mu_definable_implies_mso_invariant {P : Type} (L : Set (TransitionSystem P))
    (hL : MuDefinable L) : MSODefinable L ∧ BisimulationInvariant L

axiom finite_bisimulation {P : Type} (S T : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P)
    (R : S.Vertex → T.Vertex → Prop) :
    Bisimulation (ofFinite S) (ofFinite T) R ↔ TransitionSystems.Bisimulation S T R

axiom finite_mu_models {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P)
    (φ : ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P) : MuModels (ofFinite S) φ ↔ ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ

axiom finite_mso_models {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P)
    (φ : MonadicSecondOrder.Sentence P) : MSOModels (ofFinite S) φ ↔ MonadicSecondOrder.Models S φ

end Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic

  (φ : Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n) (ρ σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex),
  (∀ (i : Fin n), Set.instLE.le (ρ i) (σ i)) →
    Set.instLE.le (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.muEval S φ ρ) (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.muEval S φ σ)

finite_bisimulation : ∀ {P : Type} (S T : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (R : S.Vertex → T.Vertex → Prop),
  Iff
    (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.Bisimulation (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.ofFinite S)
      (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.ofFinite T) R)
    (Lax369799.TransitionSystems.Bisimulation S T R)

finite_mso : ∀ {P : Type} (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) {m n : Nat}
  (φ : Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder.Formula P m n) (ρ : Fin m → S.Vertex) (σ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex),
  Iff (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.msoEval (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.ofFinite S) φ ρ σ)
    (Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder.Formula.eval S φ ρ σ)

  Iff (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.MSOModels (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.ofFinite S) φ)
    (Lax369799.MonadicSecondOrder.Models S φ)

finite_mu : ∀ {P : Type} (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) {n : Nat} (φ : Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula P n)
  (ρ : Fin n → Set S.Vertex),
  Eq (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.muEval (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.ofFinite S) φ ρ)
    (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Formula.eval S φ ρ)

finite_mu_models : ∀ {P : Type} (S : Lax369799.TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) (φ : Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Sentence P),
  Iff (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.MuModels (Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.ofFinite S) φ)
    (Lax369799.ModalMuCalculus.Models S φ)

  Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.BisimulationInvariant
    (Set.ofPred fun S => Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.MuModels S φ)

  Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.MuDefinable L →

  Exists fun ψ =>
    ∀ (S : Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P),
      Iff (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.MuModels S φ) (Lax369799.UnrestrictedLogic.MSOModels S ψ)

concepts.title: Arbitrary transition systems and bisimulations
concepts.description:
A pointed transition system may have an arbitrary state space. The usual
back-and-forth definition of bisimulation imposes no finiteness or
reachability assumption. Finite transition systems embed by retaining
their vertices, initial point, edges, and proposition valuations.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.TransitionSystems

/-!
---
title: Arbitrary transition systems and bisimulations
type: definition
---
A pointed transition system may have an arbitrary state space. The usual
back-and-forth definition of bisimulation imposes no finiteness or
reachability assumption. Finite transition systems embed by retaining
their vertices, initial point, edges, and proposition valuations.
-/

namespace Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems

structure TransitionSystem (P : Type) where
  Vertex : Type
  initial : Vertex
  edge : Vertex → Vertex → Prop
  valuation : Vertex → Set P

def ofFinite {P : Type} (S : TransitionSystems.TransitionSystem P) : TransitionSystem P :=
  ⟨S.Vertex,S.initial,S.edge,S.valuation⟩

def Bisimulation {P : Type} (S T : TransitionSystem P)
    (R : S.Vertex → T.Vertex → Prop) : Prop :=
  R S.initial T.initial ∧ ∀ v w, R v w →
    S.valuation v = T.valuation w ∧
    (∀ v', S.edge v v' → ∃ w', T.edge w w' ∧ R v' w') ∧
    (∀ w', T.edge w w' → ∃ v', S.edge v v' ∧ R v' w')

def Bisimilar {P : Type} (S T : TransitionSystem P) : Prop :=
  ∃ R, Bisimulation S T R

def BisimulationInvariant {P : Type} (L : Set (TransitionSystem P)) : Prop :=
  ∀ S T, Bisimilar S T → (S ∈ L ↔ T ∈ L)

end Lax369799.UnrestrictedTransitionSystems

concepts.title: Compression of variable maps by finite observations
concepts.description:
Group variables by their target and a finite observation. Choosing one
representative of each group preserves both observations and bounds each
new target fibre by the number of possible observations.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.Resolutions
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.EquivFin

/-!
---
title: Compression of variable maps by finite observations
type: theorem
---
Group variables by their target and a finite observation. Choosing one
representative of each group preserves both observations and bounds each
new target fibre by the number of possible observations.
-/
namespace Lax369799.VariableCompression

axiom compress {V : Type} [Finite V] {m n : ℕ} (σ : Fin m → Fin n) (observe : Fin m → V) :
    ∃ (m' : ℕ) (τ : Fin m → Fin m') (sectionMap : Fin m' → Fin m),
      (∀ j, τ (sectionMap j) = j) ∧
      (∀ i, σ (sectionMap (τ i)) = σ i) ∧
      (∀ i, observe (sectionMap (τ i)) = observe i) ∧
      (∀ j, Nat.card {i // σ (sectionMap i) = j} ≤ Nat.card V)

end Lax369799.VariableCompression

statements.signature:
compress : ∀ {V : Type} [Finite V] {m n : Nat} (σ : Fin m → Fin n) (observe : Fin m → V),
  Exists fun m' =>
    Exists fun τ =>
      Exists fun sectionMap =>
        And (∀ (j : Fin m'), Eq (τ (sectionMap j)) j)
          (And (∀ (i : Fin m), Eq (σ (sectionMap (τ i))) (σ i))
            (And (∀ (i : Fin m), Eq (observe (sectionMap (τ i))) (observe i))
              (∀ (j : Fin n), instLENat.le (Nat.card (Subtype fun i => Eq (σ (sectionMap i)) j)) (Nat.card V))))

concepts.title: Contexts obtained by marking a vertex
concepts.description:
Replacing the label of a selected vertex by the hole preserves its rank,
marks, edges, and reachability. Filling the hole by the original letter
recovers the system. This permits local changes to an outer deterministic
system before flattening its labels.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ContextRelabelling
import Lax369799.ContextSmallification

/-!
---
title: Contexts obtained by marking a vertex
type: theorem
---
Replacing the label of a selected vertex by the hole preserves its rank,
marks, edges, and reachability. Filling the hole by the original letter
recovers the system. This permits local changes to an outer deterministic
system before flattening its labels.
-/
namespace Lax369799.VertexContexts
open RankedSystems Flattening SystemEvaluation

noncomputable def atVertex {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S : System A n) (v : S.val.Vertex) :
    SetContext A (S.val.graph.label v).1 n := by
  classical
  let G : Presentation (WithHole A (S.val.graph.label v).1) n S.val.Vertex := {
    label := fun w => ⟨(S.val.graph.label w).1,
      if h : w = v then Sum.inr ⟨by rw [h]⟩ else Sum.inl (S.val.graph.label w).2⟩
    initial := S.val.graph.initial
    root := S.val.graph.root
    edge := S.val.graph.edge
    direction_valid := S.val.graph.direction_valid }
  refine ⟨⟨S.val.size, G, S.val.reachable⟩, v, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact ⟨⟨rfl⟩, by simp [G]⟩
  · intro w hw
    by_contra h
    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hw
    simp only [G, dif_neg h] at hp
    cases hp

axiom deterministic {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S : System A n) (v : S.val.Vertex) :
    (atVertex S v).system.Deterministic

axiom fill_vertex {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} (S : System A n) (v : S.val.Vertex) :
    relabel (fillLetter (S.val.graph.label v).2) (atVertex S v).system = S.val

axiom smallification {A : RankedSet} (E : Algebras.Algebra A) (hE : Algebras.UnfoldInvariant E)
    [Finite (A 1)] (S : System A 0) (v : S.val.Vertex) {n : ℕ}
    (σ : Fin (S.val.graph.label v).1 → Fin n) :
    ∃ (m' : ℕ) (τ : Fin (S.val.graph.label v).1 → Fin m')
      (sectionMap : Fin m' → Fin (S.val.graph.label v).1),
      (∀ j, τ (sectionMap j) = j) ∧
      (∀ i, σ (sectionMap (τ i)) = σ i) ∧
      (∀ j, Nat.card {i // σ (sectionMap i) = j} ≤ Nat.card (A 1) + 1) ∧
      ∃ T : System A 0,
        T.val = relabel (fillLetter (E.eval _
          (Renaming.renameSystem (sectionMap ∘ τ) (atomicSystem (S.val.graph.label v).2))))
          (atVertex S v).system ∧ E.eval 0 S = E.eval 0 T

end Lax369799.VertexContexts

concepts.title: Idempotent factorization of infinite words
concepts.description:
An infinite word in a finite monoid has a nonempty initial block of value
`a`, followed by nonempty blocks of a common idempotent value `e`, with
`a * e = a`. The increasing cuts are cofinal and every union of consecutive
blocks after the first again has value `e`.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.InfiniteRamsey
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.List.Basic

/-!
---
title: Idempotent factorization of infinite words
type: theorem
---
An infinite word in a finite monoid has a nonempty initial block of value
`a`, followed by nonempty blocks of a common idempotent value `e`, with
`a * e = a`. The increasing cuts are cofinal and every union of consecutive
blocks after the first again has value `e`.
-/
namespace Lax369799.WordFactorization

/-- Product of the half-open interval of letters [i,j). -/
def block {M : Type} [Monoid M] (w : ℕ → M) (i j : ℕ) : M :=
  ((List.range' i (j - i)).map w).prod

axiom factorization {M : Type} [Monoid M] [Finite M] (w : ℕ → M) :
    ∃ (cut : ℕ → ℕ) (a e : M), StrictMono cut ∧ 0 < cut 0 ∧
      e * e = e ∧ a * e = a ∧
      (∀ i, block w 0 (cut i) = a) ∧
      (∀ i j, i < j → block w (cut i) (cut j) = e)

end Lax369799.WordFactorization

statements.signature:
factorization : ∀ {M : Type} [inst : Monoid M] [Finite M] (w : Nat → M),
  Exists fun cut =>
    Exists fun a =>
      Exists fun e =>
        And (StrictMono cut)
          (And (instLTNat.lt 0 (cut 0))
            (And (Eq (instHMul.hMul e e) e)
              (And (Eq (instHMul.hMul a e) a)
                (And (∀ (i : Nat), Eq (Lax369799.WordFactorization.block w 0 (cut i)) a)
                  (∀ (i j : Nat), instLTNat.lt i j → Eq (Lax369799.WordFactorization.block w (cut i) (cut j)) e)))))

concepts.title: Recurring priorities in finite-state runs
concepts.description:
A run over finitely many states has a unique least recurring priority.
Finite prefixes do not affect recurrence. A state with this least priority
occurs twice arbitrarily far out, with no lower priority between the two
occurrences; this is the cycle used in periodic branch arguments.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata

/-!
---
title: Recurring priorities in finite-state runs
type: theorem
---
A run over finitely many states has a unique least recurring priority.
Finite prefixes do not affect recurrence. A state with this least priority
occurs twice arbitrarily far out, with no lower priority between the two
occurrences; this is the cycle used in periodic branch arguments.
-/
namespace Lax369799.WordParity

def Recurrent (p : ℕ → ℕ) (c : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ N, ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ p n = c

def LeastRecurring (p : ℕ → ℕ) (c : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Recurrent p c ∧ ∀ b, b < c → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → p n ≠ b

axiom least_recurring {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (priority : Q → ℕ) (r : ℕ → Q) :
    ∃! c, LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c

axiom recurrent_shift (p : ℕ → ℕ) (c k : ℕ) :
    Recurrent (fun n => p (n + k)) c ↔ Recurrent p c

axiom minimum_cycle {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (priority : Q → ℕ) (r : ℕ → Q)
    (c : ℕ) (hc : LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ i j, N ≤ i ∧ i < j ∧ r i = r j ∧ priority (r i) = c ∧
      ∀ k, i ≤ k → k ≤ j → c ≤ priority (r k)

axiom acceptance_iff {u z : ℕ} (D : UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition u z)
    (w : ℕ → Fin u) (c : ℕ)
    (hc : LeastRecurring (fun n => D.priority (D.run w n)) c) :
    D.AcceptsInfinite w ↔ Even c

end Lax369799.WordParity

statements.signature:
acceptance_iff : ∀ {u z : Nat} (D : Lax369799.UnfoldAutomata.WordCondition u z) (w : Nat → Fin u) (c : Nat),
  Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => D.priority (D.run w n)) c → Iff (D.AcceptsInfinite w) (Even c)

least_recurring : ∀ {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (priority : Q → Nat) (r : Nat → Q),
  ExistsUnique fun c => Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c

minimum_cycle : ∀ {Q : Type} [Finite Q] (priority : Q → Nat) (r : Nat → Q) (c : Nat),
  Lax369799.WordParity.LeastRecurring (fun n => priority (r n)) c →
    ∀ (N : Nat),
      Exists fun i =>
        Exists fun j =>
          And (instLENat.le N i)
            (And (instLTNat.lt i j)
              (And (Eq (r i) (r j))
                (And (Eq (priority (r i)) c)
                  (∀ (k : Nat), instLENat.le i k → instLENat.le k j → instLENat.le c (priority (r k))))))

recurrent_shift : ∀ (p : Nat → Nat) (c k : Nat),
  Iff (Lax369799.WordParity.Recurrent (fun n => p (instHAdd.hAdd n k)) c) (Lax369799.WordParity.Recurrent p c)

concepts.title: Continuity of yields in a context
concepts.description:
Corollary 46 of arXiv v6 (Corollary 50 in the revised manuscript), using
the earlier reachable interface: every yield of a substituted context occurs when
the hole is replaced by a finite sum of yields of its label. Conversely,
every such finite sum gives only yields of the original substitution.
The sum stays inside the context, preserving independent choices at
different occurrences. Finite indexed families allow repetitions.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ContextResolutionApproximation

/-!
---
title: Continuity of yields in a context
type: theorem
---
Corollary 46 of arXiv v6 (Corollary 50 in the revised manuscript), using
the earlier reachable interface: every yield of a substituted context occurs when
the hole is replaced by a finite sum of yields of its label. Conversely,
every such finite sum gives only yields of the original substitution.
The sum stays inside the context, preserving independent choices at
different occurrences. Finite indexed families allow repetitions.
-/
namespace Lax369799.YieldContinuity
open RankedSystems Morphisms Flattening

def sumGraph {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {I : Type} (F : I → SetSystem A n) :
    Presentation A n ((i : I) × (F i).Vertex) where
  label := fun v => (F v.1).graph.label v.2
  initial := fun v => (F v.1).graph.initial v.2
  root := fun v => (F v.1).graph.root v.2
  edge := fun v d t => ∃ s, (F v.1).graph.edge v.2 d s ∧ t = Sum.map (Sigma.mk v.1) id s
  direction_valid := by rintro v d t ⟨s, hs, _⟩; exact (F v.1).graph.direction_valid v.2 d s hs

noncomputable def finiteSum {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ} {I : Type} [Fintype I]
    (F : I → SetSystem A n) : SetSystem A n := trim (sumGraph F)

axiom continuity {A : RankedSet} {k n : ℕ}
    (C : SetContext A k n) (S : SetSystem A k) (R : SetSystem A n) :
    Yield (plug C S) R ↔
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Fin m → SetSystem A k),
        (∀ i, Yield S (F i)) ∧ Yield (plug C (finiteSum F)) R

end Lax369799.YieldContinuity

statements.signature:
continuity : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {k n : Nat} (C : Lax369799.Flattening.SetContext A k n)
  (S : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A k) (R : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A n),
  Iff (Lax369799.Morphisms.Yield (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C S) R)
    (Exists fun m =>
      Exists fun F =>
        And (∀ (i : Fin m), Lax369799.Morphisms.Yield S (F i))
          (Lax369799.Morphisms.Yield (Lax369799.Flattening.plug C (Lax369799.YieldContinuity.finiteSum F)) R))

concepts.title: Substitution and yield inclusion
concepts.description:
Local yield inclusion transfers resolutions of a flattening. Variable
splitting allows different occurrences of an inner variable to take
different outer successors.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax369799.ProfileSubstitution

/-!
---
title: Substitution and yield inclusion
type: theorem
---
Local yield inclusion transfers resolutions of a flattening. Variable
splitting allows different occurrences of an inner variable to take
different outer successors.
-/
namespace Lax369799.YieldSubstitution
open RankedSystems Morphisms Flattening ProfileSubstitution

axiom transfer_resolution {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ}
    (P : SetSystem (SetSystem A) n) (Q : ∀ v, SetSystem A (P.graph.label v).1)
    (hQ : ∀ v, YieldBelow (Inner P v) (Q v))
    (R : System A n) (hR : DirectResolution (flatten P) R) :
    ∃ U : System A n, DirectResolution (flatten (withLabels P Q)) U ∧
      UnfoldsTo R.val U.val

axiom flatten_mono {A : RankedSet} {n : ℕ}
    (P : SetSystem (SetSystem A) n) (Q : ∀ v, SetSystem A (P.graph.label v).1)
    (hQ : ∀ v, YieldBelow (Inner P v) (Q v)) :
    YieldBelow (flatten P) (flatten (withLabels P Q))

end Lax369799.YieldSubstitution

statements.signature:
flatten_mono : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat}
  (P : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem (Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A) n)
  (Q : (v : Fin P.size) → Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A (P.graph.label v).fst),
  (∀ (v : P.Vertex), Lax369799.Morphisms.YieldBelow (Lax369799.Flattening.Inner P v) (Q v)) →
    Lax369799.Morphisms.YieldBelow (Lax369799.Flattening.flatten P)
      (Lax369799.Flattening.flatten (Lax369799.ProfileSubstitution.withLabels P Q))

transfer_resolution : ∀ {A : Lax369799.RankedSystems.RankedSet} {n : Nat}
  (P : Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem (Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A) n)
  (Q : (v : Fin P.size) → Lax369799.RankedSystems.SetSystem A (P.graph.label v).fst),
  (∀ (v : P.Vertex), Lax369799.Morphisms.YieldBelow (Lax369799.Flattening.Inner P v) (Q v)) →
    ∀ (R : Lax369799.RankedSystems.System A n),
      Lax369799.Morphisms.DirectResolution (Lax369799.Flattening.flatten P) R →
        Exists fun U =>
          And
            (Lax369799.Morphisms.DirectResolution
              (Lax369799.Flattening.flatten (Lax369799.ProfileSubstitution.withLabels P Q)) U)
            (Lax369799.Morphisms.UnfoldsTo R.val U.val)

proofs.description:
A system is one of its own yields. Every initial yield of a system is
unfold-equivalent to it, while no root yield exists because it has no
roots. Unfold invariance of the language gives the equivalence.

Locally surjective maps identify yields; a common cover therefore
identifies all acceptance tests.

Test the syntactic comparison in the context consisting of a single
initial hole. Its substitution covers the argument itself.

Lift the morphism through each test context. Its yield inclusion reverses
the universal acceptance condition.

Each direct resolution is its own yield. Every yield is unfolding-equivalent
to a direct resolution and therefore has the same observed value. The cover
of the reachable restriction also preserves all root observations.

Combine the linked-pair parity automaton with the finite evaluator. Its
second component records the composed action of the unary prefix on a
terminal nullary value.

Flatten a normal pattern labelled by the reachable unary pieces. Its
projection onto the planted original context preserves and lifts all
marks and edges, including the hole's self-loops. Associativity then
replaces each piece by its unary value.

Thin the factorization to a recurrent graph vertex. Nonempty monoid
products are still unary values, so thinning preserves the original
accepting linked pair.

Adjoin an identity to the finite unary semigroup. Nonempty interval
products still lie in the unary sort, so the linked-pair omega language
is exactly the language recognized by the finite-monoid construction.

Choose the deterministic witness supplied by the automaton property.
Express it as a parallel family of unary values and enumerate these
values as finite edge types. The original inequalities give transition
membership and acceptance preservation.

Use the finite unary and nullary sorts of the yield-syntactic algebra.
The linked-pair word condition makes accepting evaluated runs precisely
accepting automaton runs. Every accepted input has such a run, and
monotonicity transfers acceptance of a run back to the input.

Project each atomic component to its outer vertex. Atomic components have
one initial vertex and send each direction to the corresponding variable,
so this projection preserves and lifts every mark and edge.

The sole outer vertex contributes the given system without changing any
mark or transition. Projection to its inner vertex is locally surjective.

Normalize the planted context, then minimize both its boundary data and
unary values. The deterministic Delta witness is below the original
letter and remains accepting. Monotonicity and the algebraic normal form
transfer acceptance back to the original context.

The intermediate selection priorities are zero. Word positions have
positive priorities, so inserting selections preserves the parity test.

An opposing positional strategy selects a branch of the run. A first
leaf contradicts finite-branch acceptance; without a leaf, the selected
infinite branch contradicts the opposing strategy's parity guarantee.

The modal game has a sentence defining its winning region. Accepting runs
give winning plays, and sentence invariance transfers this across an
unfolding. Conversely, a winning strategy yields a bisimilar finite
presentation with an accepting run; the assumed language invariance
transfers acceptance back to the input presentation.

Take the disjoint union and quotient by vertex bisimilarity. The two
initial vertices have the same class. Every quotient class is reachable
from that class, and both projections lift successors.

Identity, converse, and relational composition preserve the valuation
and the two successor-matching conditions.

The finite bounded-profile quotient maps onto the contextual quotient,
because profile equality refines contextual equivalence in every rank.

Regularize an arbitrary recognizing algebra without changing its language
or rankwise finiteness, then apply bounded-profile finiteness.

In every context, equal bounded profiles at the hole transfer initial and
root observation values in both directions. The recognizing accepting set
therefore gives the same universal yield-acceptance test.

A variable map with fibres bounded by b has domain size at most n times b.
Thus the possible bounded entries form a finite
set, and initial/root profiles range over two finite powersets.

Transport the algebraic comparisons through the specification of the
finite and infinite word conditions.

Push each eligible unary prefix through choices. The accepting set tests
a choice by testing both summands, leaving precisely the finite paths.
Restricting a finite unary sort to eligible types preserves finiteness.
Choice preservation is closed under composition of unary actions.

The finite strategy graph records the word state and input vertex.
Uniform duplication realizes each marking while covering all input
successors. Trimming preserves the run and the bisimulation projection.
Finite branches use final states; infinite branches follow the winning
strategy and therefore satisfy the word parity condition.
Forget the additional accepting-run guarantee.

Choose the finite syntactic unary and nullary sorts and their algebraic
branch condition. Stabilization compresses an accepted duplicated run
into the recurrent clone table. Conversely, rerouting lifts a clone run
to an original run with larger labels and isomorphic decoding.

Apply local refinement at every nonleaf vertex and preserve the leaves.
The surjective direction maps preserve the decoded system, and every
branch projects to one with smaller labels in the original clone run.

Decode the unary type codes, apply closure under duplication, and
transport the resulting tuple along the positive target arity.
Duplicating each component by k and then by m duplicates it by km.
Each compressed label is the meet of its block of original labels.

Choose a recurrent compression with at least as many copies as the clone.
Cap excess copies at the last old direction. This map is surjective,
and every compressed label lies below its original component.

The space of compressed n-tuples is finite. Apply eventual containment
in the recurrent part of the sequence.

Take the maximum of the thresholds for the finitely many input labels
and arities; the tuple spaces may have different dimensions.
Normalize any accepting context of the witness. The component comparisons transfer acceptance to the original element; contextual separation gives the order inequality.
Embeddings of the original root mark and the sum of the two incoming pieces into the accepting test force both comparisons by extremality.
Merging the copied incoming piece with the outer one preserves labels, roots, and edges, and hence preserves acceptance in the original context.
Replace the closed witness by its equal extremal value in the comparison theorem. The reverse implication is monotonicity.
The witness decreases the hole element and is still accepted with the original data. Minimality of the whole situation identifies the two elements.

Expanding a nullary sum in a marked singleton gives the same two vertices
as summing the two lifted singletons. No pruning is used.

The second component tracks the unary action and applies it to the
terminal nullary type; the first component does not affect finality.

The first projection follows the original run and supplies exactly the
same priority at every position.

Flattening a component renamed by sectionMap composed with τ maps to the
flattening of the compressed outer pattern. Both are deterministic, so
unfold invariance and associativity identify their evaluations.

The context contains its hole, so its vertex set is nonempty. Apply
finite splitting to all targets.
Iterate binary splitting over a nonempty finite set of target vertices.

Normal decomposition turns target union into meet of boundary and piece
data. The principal extremal acceptance test preserves that meet.

Substitution preserves covering maps, including initial and root marks
and edges that return to the same component. Substitute a common cover
at the hole to obtain a common cover of the two plugged contexts.

Map each copied vertex to its original and the new hole to the original
hole. Every initial vertex, root, and successor has a preimage, including
initial/root holes and hole self-loops. Restrict this cover to reachable
vertices.

The recomposition itself is a common cover of the original and recomposed
systems: use the projection to the former and the identity to the latter.
Every copied vertex differs from the unique hole vertex.

Restrict the matching outer directions while renaming the argument
ports. The raw flattenings are isomorphic; reachable restriction and
deterministic substitution preserve that isomorphism.

The hole stays reachable until its first visit, since all earlier edges
are unchanged. The reachable restriction has one hole and deterministic
successors in every new permitted direction.

Relabel the context and use associativity to replace each inserted system
by its value. Equal values give the same filled context. Unfolding
invariance of the algebra is not needed.

Replace the ordinary letters by atomic systems and the hole by its
argument. This deterministic outer system has a deterministic flattening.

Relabelling commutes with flattening. For an ordinary letter the two
substitutions are atomic, and at the hole both use the relabelled argument.

Select the finite support at the unique hole. Every other label retains
its original resolutions; each selected hole resolution maps into the
finite disjoint family.

Apply finite approximation to a direct-resolution witness and compose
its unfolding. Conversely the disjoint family maps into the original
system, and this morphism extends through the context.

Take finite support in the root-entry expansion. Select all support
components located at the hole, retaining their initial or root entry
flags, and insert their disjoint family. The reverse inclusion follows
from the family's morphism to the original hole label.

Combine initial and root approximation, keeping each deterministic
component's entry flag. The family maps into the original system.

Compress by target and optional unary evaluation. Optional observations
preserve the direct-loop case. The deterministic normal form turns their
equality into equality of context values after variable redirection.

Relabel the context and argument into the observing algebra, apply
smallification there, and use commutation of relabelling with plugging
to recover the two substituted systems over the original alphabet.

Normalize an arbitrary accepting test context. Boundary and unary-piece
comparisons put the extremal context below its normal form. Acceptance
of the original letter then transfers to this test, and order separation
establishes the required inequality.

An extra root mark in the testing context makes a component center a
root. A loop in direction i returns the exit of U_i to its own center.
The corresponding subsystem morphisms and boundary minimality force
both features to be present in the extremal context already.

Duplicate the selected unary piece, using the test context's value on
its second copy. Evaluation of that pair is a meet. The resulting
subsystem embeds into the test of Delta, so minimality forces the
original unary value below the test context's unary value.

Project every copied a-vertex to the hole position and each copied unary
piece to its original position. The retained root mark and loop directions
make this a morphism even when the original hole carries these features.

Restrict to each variable and evaluate the resulting unary presentation.
Their parallel substitution has the same yields as the original unary
presentation. Continuity and the induced order identify their evaluations.

Evaluate the substituted system first. Reconstruct the deterministic context
from its unary pieces, representing an absent piece by a copy of the hole.
The reconstruction covers the filled context, and associativity evaluates
its pieces. Relabelling then gives the pattern of optional unary values.

The entry vertex is unique, roots are absent, and the successor function
provides exactly one edge in each direction. Trimming preserves these properties.

Compress by the target and the optional unary observation. The absent
observation distinguishes direct self-loops, giving the bound |V|+1.

The two alternatives for each piece identify precisely when its optional
system is absent: the missing piece records a direct boundary connection.

Use the unique successor in the selected hole direction. A self-loop
leaves no initial vertex in the cut piece. Every other successor gives
a unique initial vertex, and cutting edges preserves determinism.

The initial vertex is either the hole, giving the empty entry piece,
or a body vertex, giving its unique initial vertex.
Language membership is constant on the closed contextual classes.

Test the equivalence in the context consisting of a single hole. Plugging
into this context preserves unfolding, and hence language membership.

The quotient by equality of recognizing values embeds in the finite
recognizing sort. It maps onto the deterministic contextual quotient.

Unfold-equivalence is preserved by context substitution. The language is
constant on that equivalence, so every deterministic contextual test agrees.

Equal recognizing values remain equal in a deterministic context by
associativity. Membership then agrees by the recognizing accepting set.

An extremal element has a parallel presentation. Each canonical
projection is below its corresponding component; the reverse bound
comes from folding all projected copies to the original element.

Refine one canonical direction in the surrounding accepting context.
Minimality of the original situation fixes the parallel value. Projecting
back forces the refined unary element to equal the original direction.
The projection shape is fixed and only its label increases.

The chosen unary component maps into the projection of the parallel
family. Other components are retained, with their exits cut off.

Fold the separate projected copies back to the atomic element. This is
a morphism, so its evaluation reverses the comparison.

The vertex equivalence preserves the unique initial vertex and every
valuation. The direction map and its surjectivity give the two directions
of preservation of the decoded edge relation.

Keep the vertices, valuations and initial mark. Surjectivity lifts old
paths, and uniqueness of successors preserves determinism.

A surjection onto a nonempty set has a nonempty domain. A function into
an empty set has an empty domain.

The syntactic translation on arbitrary structures specializes to the
finite semantics, providing the effective reverse direction of Theorem 2.

Enumerate the successor set of each vertex to give its outgoing edges

MSO sentence has a finite reachable model.

Regularization is a subalgebra followed by a quotient, so it cannot
increase a sort. Bounded entries have rank at most n times the fibre
bound. Initial and root profiles give two subsets of the explicitly
bounded entry type; their quotient surjects onto the contextual classes.

Track the finite carrier sizes in the recognition induction. Atomic path
summaries have at most 2^(4(k+1)) values in sort k. Disjunction multiplies
bounds, existential quantification takes a powerset, and inverse relabelling
preserves the bound. The bound is computed directly from the input syntax.

The linked-pair Buchi automaton records three monoid elements and two
flags. Apply the explicit determinization bound and then multiply by
the finite-word evaluator state count. Neither bound depends on the
values of the algebra's multiplication or accepting tables.

Use equality, reverse a bisimulation, and compose two bisimulations by
existential quantification over the intermediate vertex.

A ranked system morphism is locally surjective and decodes to a
bisimulation. A common ranked unfolding therefore gives bisimilar
decodings. Isomorphisms and equivalence closure preserve bisimilarity.

At a target vertex, enumerate each successor together with a copy index
bounded by the source size. For each source vertex, map these copies onto
all its successors lying over that target successor. The resulting two
rankings have identical direction sets along the given functional map.

Every class of the finite-presentation contextual quotient has a reachable
representative. Equality of such classes implies equality in the original
reachable contextual quotient, since every original context is a finite
context with the same final observation. This gives a surjection from the
finite repaired quotient onto the original syntactic quotient.
Keep the algebra and letter map, and complement the accepting subset.

The product algebra evaluates coordinatewise and accepts exactly when
both recognizing coordinates accept.
Compose the recognizing letter map with the given alphabet map.

Use the same product algebra, accepting when at least one coordinate
belongs to its accepting subset.

The new letter interpretation is the nonempty set of all interpretations
of its lifts. Membership in the accepting subset is existential.

A finite functional graph has an ultimately periodic orbit. The branch's
vertices and directions are functions of that orbit.

Present every ultimately periodic branch by its finite graph, then apply
the periodic branch test for the parity condition.

Retain the prefix and one period, then redirect the last edge to the
start of the period. Periodicity includes directions as well as vertices.

Substitute a fixed realizing system for each generated value. Unfold-equivalent
outer systems have unfold-equivalent flattenings over the original alphabet.
Recognition and language invariance transfer membership of the accepting set.

Restrict the recognizing algebra to its generated values and quotient by
polynomial acceptance equivalence. Both steps preserve recognition and
finite sorts; closed unfolding invariance makes the quotient unfolding-invariant.

Successive renamings compose on variable targets and leave vertex targets
unchanged. Their existential edge witnesses compose in the same way.
The identity variable map leaves every transition target unchanged.

Keep the same vertex map. To lift a renamed edge, choose its original
edge witness, lift that edge, and then rename its variable target.

Renaming changes transition targets and relabelling changes vertex labels;
the two constructions commute definitionally.

The composed variable map is the original map, so the same vertex
morphism witnesses the resolution after factoring the renaming.

Choose the indicated outer successors and trim to reachable vertices.
Renaming composition preserves the local resolution morphisms; the old
outer resolution preserves the selected transitions and exits.

Choose an internal continuation or a variable exit for every resolution edge.
The resulting local deterministic resolutions form an outer deterministic
system. Its flattening maps to the given resolution and hence unfolds to it.

Choose one witnessing resolution for each bounded profile entry. The
entry type is finite, and summing the fibre bounds controls its arity.

Keep the source vertices and internal edges. For each variable edge,
restore the variable selected by the unique successor in the original
unrenamed target. The two deterministic edge conditions ensure uniqueness.

Apply yield inclusion to the renamed system, then lift the resulting
unfolding through its variable renaming (Section 2.9).

Forget whether a vertex belongs to a starting or an ordinary copy.
Internal edges stay in that copy; substituted outer edges enter an ordinary
copy. Inner and outer roots have the two specified initial preimages.

Every target vertex has its ordinary-copy preimage, whether reachable or
unreachable. Thus the root-expansion cover is a folding (Lemma 38).

Restrict the inner presentations using their canonical covers. Restrict
the outer pattern using the root-free outer-cover lemma, then compose
these covers and restrict the flattened presentations to reachable vertices.

Initial restriction preserves every resolution with its variable map and
observed value, hence preserves the whole initial profile.

A deterministic resolution has no roots. Its morphism therefore factors
through the presentation with root marks removed and, by reachability,
through its initial restriction. The reverse direction uses inclusion.

Initial marks and edges lift through the outer cover. Roots of a flattened
presentation can only come from outer roots when every inner root set is
empty, so no global surjectivity on outer vertices is needed.

Remove root marks and restrict the inner components to their initial parts.
Their initial profiles are unchanged. Transfer the resulting root-free
observation and then restore the original marks.

Expand every possible root entry into a separate starting copy. Its inner
profile is the root profile, while ordinary copies use initial profiles.
Restrict these root-free components, transfer their bounded observations,
and forget the starting-copy flags through the expansion cover.

Pass to the root-entry expansion, restrict its root-free labels, and
factor an initial resolution. Its finite support records the entry flag
at each used label. The same support admits the replacement expansion.

Project each regular branch of the unary run presentation into the
input run. Word correctness and branch evaluation give acceptance of
every regular branch; choice splitting gives acceptance of the graph.
Apply the acceptance implication for arbitrary type assignments.
Combine the two directions of the run evaluation criterion.

Specialize the common finite/infinite algebraic condition to the unary
and nullary sorts of the yield-syntactic algebra.

Finite branch observations have accepted values. For a regular infinite
branch restrict to its reachable orbit, apply graph evaluation, and use
the periodic branch test to obtain acceptance on all infinite branches.

Every inserted vertex is initial in its piece. Lift input paths to the
flattening; all input directions have corresponding unary copies.
Apply the presentation morphism observation principle to the branch path.
The direct branch graph is the finite path graph of its decoded letters.

The vertex at a branch step is the parallel component selected by that
step's direction. The terminal vertex is the atomic leaf component.
Regular branch observations inherit acceptance by their presentation map.

Each vertex selects one outgoing component. Its successor is mapped to
the component selected at the next input vertex, including around cycles.

All unary labels are selected. Finite choice splitting therefore applies
to the run presentation, including its cycles and retained vertices.

The unary labels in the flattened presentation are precisely the edge
types of legal transitions; nullary pieces cannot contribute unary labels.

Decoding commutes with the fold of encoded unary actions. The direct
path evaluation theorem identifies the resulting accepting value.
The product word condition retains the supplied parity test.

Normalize an arbitrary closed testing context. Extremality turns the
meet of continuation data into conjunction. Monotonicity supplies one
inequality; separation by all contexts supplies the converse.

First choose a parallel witness. Refine each unary component in its
composed testing context. Monotonicity retains the transition bound.

Adjoin an identity to use monoid factorization. Its nonempty blocks lie
in the original semigroup. Thin the cuts to a recurrent vertex; stability
and idempotence are preserved when consecutive blocks are grouped.
The atomic system of a letter of rank at most one is a witnessing system.

The associative, commutative, idempotent operation defines its usual
semilattice order.

Every yield has evaluation above the original system, by the morphism
and unfolding axioms. Apply continuity to the included family of yields.
A set included in every set is included in the empty set.
A nonempty set with no proper nonempty subset consists of one vertex.

Inclusion and universal proposition predicates exclude a bad vertex.
Existential edge predicates are recognized by the two-state path algebra.
The initial-label algebra reads the chosen mark at the initial vertex.

Boolean operations use product algebras. Quantification forgets the new
mark and uses the nonempty powerset algebra.

Induction on the first-order and set-variable syntax. Singleton sets give
exactly the choices for an existential vertex quantifier.
Flatten the binary pattern and evaluate its two labels first.

Expand each label as the binary sum of the old and new value. This sum
evaluates to the old value, while the new-labelled graph maps into the
expanded presentation by selecting its second copy at every vertex.
Use the source as a common unfolding, with its identity folding.

Disjoint-union associators and swaps preserve evaluation. The identity
morphism gives idempotence. No continuity axiom is used.

The order induced by an associative, commutative, idempotent binary
operation is a partial order, and that operation computes its meet.

The meet characterization and antisymmetry identify the contextual order
with the order induced by disjoint union.

The quotient substitution algebra is invariant under surjective covers
and reverses morphisms. The contextual meet gives its induced order.

Restrict the equal small profiles to the bound |B₁| + 1. The checked
contextual refinement theorem for that bound then applies to both the
initial and root observations.

Extremality gives the necessary comparisons for every boundary and unary
piece. Conversely, acceptance at the extremal datum and monotonicity give
acceptance at every larger datum.

The accepted normal data form the principal filter of the extremal datum.
Boundary unions and unary meets satisfy its bounds precisely when both
input data do.

Normalize each accepting algebra context. Boundary and unary comparisons
put the extremal datum below its normal form. Monotonicity and planting
invariance transfer acceptance back to the original value. Order separation
then gives the required contextual inequality.

An extra root or loop in an accepting test supplies a subsystem morphism
that permits adding that feature to the original extremal datum. Minimality
forces the feature to have been present already.

Merging the rooted copies maps the split witness to the original one.
Morphism monotonicity therefore preserves acceptance in its chosen context.

Duplicate one unary piece using a binary meet pattern and embed the result
into the accepting test of Delta. Extremality forces the original unary
value below the testing value.

The split outer pattern already is a parallel tuple. Associativity
identifies its unary evaluations with the flattened witness.

Factor the restricted outer template through one supported system.
Associativity evaluates its two labellings equally, while port restriction,
trimming, and output renaming identify the original flattened profiles.

Flatten a two-vertex pattern labelled by the two systems. Its flattening
covers their disjoint union; evaluating the labels gives the defining meet.

Associativity of evaluation identifies evaluation of a disjoint union
with meet of its evaluations. The disjoint-union associator and swap are
covers. Idempotence also follows directly from the identity morphism axiom.

Universal acceptance of the union of the two sets of yields is equivalent
to universal acceptance of each of them.

A deterministic resolution starts in one summand and all its reachable
vertices stay there. Apply this to initial and root resolutions. The
converse follows from the two inclusion morphisms.

Enumerate exactly the output indices occurring on an edge. Pull back
variable targets along this enumeration. The vertex graph is unchanged,
so reachability and deterministic successors are preserved.

Every old variable occurs, so the new output support is exactly the
image of the variable map.

The renamed atomic substitution is isomorphic to the renamed inner
system. Isomorphism invariance and associativity give the equality.

Expand every letter to its atomic system. Completion evaluation and the
inner unit identify the result with the original system class.

Compact both systems along their common output support. Reflect the
morphism through that injective renaming and apply supported unfolding
invariance to the compacted systems.

Select a deterministic common unfolding, then apply the two morphism
comparisons to identify the supported-evaluation profiles.

Choose representatives of the observation classes and flatten. A common
unfolding of the outer systems induces a common unfolding of these
flattenings, whose supported-evaluation profiles coincide.

A unary system has either no used output or one used output. Its class
is represented by an atomic closed value or an atomic unary value, so
the disjoint union of the two original sorts surjects onto the unary sort.

Compress the completed unary observations, whose cardinality is bounded
by |B₀| + |B₁|. Resize the hole to the quotient arity and select the
representative successor in every new direction. The port-substitution
isomorphism proves equality with the original closed evaluation (Lemma 81).

Select a system inside the common finite unfolding. Both composites
are morphisms between supported systems and hence are foldings.

The restored variable at an exit is determined by the original target.
The lifted morphism onto the fully supported target lifts each of its
outputs, so the restored presentation also has full support.

A morphism between deterministic systems lifts every vertex and every
outgoing edge of the target, hence every target output as well.

Uniqueness of the initial vertex and of successors implies local
surjectivity. Reachability of all target vertices implies surjectivity.

The reachable part of the fiber product is deterministic. Its projections
lift all outputs from either factor. Pairing any two compatible maps from
a system lands in this reachable part and is the unique factorization.

Choose one initial vertex and one edge in each permitted direction,
then restrict to the reachable part. The resulting map into the source
is injective. Its composite to the target is a folding, which also lifts
every output variable and proves full support.

Transfer the completed bounded initial and root observations in both
directions. The closed completion equivalence recovers the original
supported values, proving full profile equality (Lemma 83).

There are no target variables in rank zero, so every variable map
satisfies the small-fibre condition.

Move each output map across the resolution using inverse renaming, which
commutes with flattening. Transfer full initial and root observations in
the unfolding-invariant completion. Equal completed values restore full
support and the original supported values (Lemma 78).

Compact each legacy resolution along its used outputs. Equal supported
profiles supply a replacement with the same original value; restoring
the unused outputs gives the same completed value. Canonical trimming
covers transfer the root profiles.

Use an unfolding-invariant completion and its recognizing closed values.
Full supported profiles determine the completed bounded profiles, which
determine every unpruned closed contextual test.

The unary completion bound makes its legacy cutoff at most the original
small-map bound. Injective support restriction only reduces fibre sizes.
Apply the filtered profile transfer to initial and root observations.

A small map into n outputs has domain size at most n times the small
bound. Initial and root profiles therefore range over two finite
powersets of bounded entries.

Complete the supported algebra without increasing the unary cutoff
beyond |B₀| + |B₁| + 1. Equal supported small profiles therefore determine
every closed contextual test (Corollary 84).

A direct resolution is its own yield witness. Conversely a yield
witness has the same value as its target because supported evaluation
is invariant under unfoldings.
Complete the recognizer, complement its accepting set, and restrict back.
Products of the completed recognizers preserve finite sorts.
Compose the alphabet map with the map of the completed recognizer.

Relabel a common unfolding by the recognizing letter map. Equal
supported evaluations give equal membership in the accepting subset.

Apply finite powerset recognition after completion, then restrict to the
supported domain.

Complete the finite supported recognizer and apply the proved bounded
profile refinement for the unpruned contextual quotient.
Use the product recognizer with disjunctive acceptance.

Extend the original supported algebra to arbitrary output presentations.
Compress one oversized local map at a time, retaining a representative
for each continuation observation. Surjective local renaming preserves
full support, and the number of oversized vertices strictly decreases.
The completed unary sort has at most |B₀| + |B₁| elements. Associativity
and the closed-sort equivalence return the original evaluation (Lemma 82).

Choose supported direct witnesses for the local yields and flatten them.
Pair the outer and inner vertex maps to obtain the renamed resolution.
Pointwise unfolding invariance transfers its target to the original
supported flattening (Lemma 46).

Every outer edge can be traversed through a reachable variable of its
inner system. Induct on an outer path, then follow an inner path to the
desired vertex. No flattened vertex is removed.

The existing deterministic flattening supplies the unique successors.
Every outer variable edge is reached through its supported inner port,
and the reachable-part enumeration retains that edge.

Transfer the yield comparison to reachable presentations, apply finite
context monotonicity, then restore the original unpruned presentations
through their substitution covers.

Apply substitution monotonicity to both directions of the local yield
equivalences (Corollary 48, equivalence clause).

Apply the generic context/substitution equivalence to yield inclusion.
Context monotonicity and composition of yield inclusions supply its
hypotheses (Corollary 48, inclusion clause).

Rename a supported witness in the forward direction. In the reverse
direction restore the source variables through the unfolding and lift
full support from the supported target.

The canonical trimming cover preserves root entries and edges. Transfer
the initial-yield comparison across its rooted cover.

Yield inclusion reverses universal yield acceptance in every closed
context. Canonical substitution covers identify each unpruned
presentation with its reachable representative (Lemma 73).

Initial yields have finite support in the inserted presentation. Compact
the outputs of each component in a finite approximation, retaining its
variable map and whether it is an initial or a root yield.

Root yields have finite support in the inserted presentation. Compact
the outputs of each component in a finite approximation, retaining its
variable map and whether it is an initial or a root yield.

Compose a yield's renamed morphism for monotonicity. For reflection,
move the variable map across the morphism using the adjunction, pull
back the resulting locally surjective map, and select a supported system.

Unfold-equivalence preserves all yields. Conversely the identity yield
of one system, viewed as a yield of the other, supplies a common
supported unfolding because every morphism between systems is a folding.

Pull back a yield witness with a common system unfolding. Its projections
supply a new witness with exactly the original variable map. Apply the
same construction with the roots made initial for root yields.

The two foldings of a common unfolding preserve and reflect both yield
families. Compose their equivalences with the variable map fixed.

The identity on pairs of outer and inner vertices preserves internal
edges. Each renamed inner exit is connected through its matching
restricted outer direction, including exits to output variables.

Acceptance descends through the syntactic equivalence. The quotient map
sends disjoint union to meet, while acceptance of a disjoint union is the
conjunction of acceptance of its summands. These facts give the filter
properties. On deterministic systems acceptance is language membership.

The context labelled by atomic ordinary letters and the supplied hole
system is deterministic. Associativity evaluates its flattening by first
evaluating its labels; the unit law restores the ordinary letters.
Evaluate the two systems before applying the common variable renaming.

Flatten the renamed atomic outer system. Its flattening maps to the
renamed inner system, and a morphism between deterministic systems is a
local cover. Unfold invariance and associativity give the equality.

Relabel the flattened system and its inner components by the same alphabet
map. Relabelling commutes with flattening, so algebra associativity applies.

A morphism between systems is locally surjective. Relabel by the underlying
finite inner presentations and lift the outer cover through substitution.
Inner systems have no roots, which supplies the required root-free condition.

Choose a common cover for each pair of inner systems, substitute these
covers into the fixed outer pattern, and restrict the resulting covers to
reachable vertices.

Restrict the covering map to reachable vertices. Successors of reachable
vertices are reachable; initial and root vertices are reachable by empty paths.

Separate the first vertex by the flattening isomorphism. Associativity
reduces its suffix to a value, and induction gives the word evaluation.

The chain evaluation is its right-associated unary product. Associativity
identifies this with the nonempty interval product.

Both bracketings flatten to the same three-vertex chain. Associativity
evaluates the two pieces in either partition before the entire chain.
The action law in sort one is the semigroup law.

In sort zero the second vertex has no exits, giving the terminating-word
application graph.

Equip the unary sort with its checked associative composition. Apply the
finite semigroup factorization while recording the graph vertex at each
cut.

Stable semigroup factorization yields an accepting linked pair from graph
evaluation. Conversely, thin an accepting factorization to a recurrent
vertex and fold its prefix and loop back to the graph.

Expand the prefix and loop values into their word chains. Their flattening
covers the original graph; reachability makes the covering map globally
surjective. Associativity evaluates the two chains before the lasso.

A terminating branch covers the entire unary system. An infinite branch
visits every vertex, and the unary graph evaluation theorem applies.
If there is a leaf, reachability supplies a terminating branch; otherwise
all vertices are unary and the successor function supplies an infinite one.

All vertices lie on a single path from the initial vertex. An exit vertex
has no internal successor, so any two exit vertices coincide; uniqueness
of the deterministic successor then identifies their variables.

Every deterministic resolution uses at most one variable, so it lifts to
that variable's copy. If it has no exit, choose any copy. Forgetting the
copy index gives the converse, for initial and root resolutions alike.

Both marked and unmarked lifts preserve sums. Duplicating the fixed
planted prefix is absorbed by idempotence of the contextual meet.

Remove root marks, transfer full initial profiles, and restore the marks.
The argument applies to arbitrary finite outer presentations and all ranks.

Factor the resolution and replace its local resolutions by equal-profile
witnesses, keeping every variable map. Associativity identifies the
flattened values in every output rank.

Separate root-starting and ordinary copies of every component, transfer
their full profiles, then forget the copy flags through the expansion cover.

Restrict a root-free outer presentation and its labels through their
canonical covers. Transfer the resolution, then restore the original
presentation, retaining observations in every output rank.

Take the product of vertices, chosen directions, and word-automaton states.
Its transition relation preserves system edges and updates the word state.
A periodic witness in this finite product projects to a periodic branch
with the same least recurring priority.

Keep all vertices at each stage. Reassociate the three vertex coordinates,
then account for the finite enumerations on the two intermediate graphs.
The associator preserves and reflects every mark and transition.

Relabelling changes neither vertex sets nor marks and transitions, so
both constructions use the same finite enumeration and labelling.

Each atomic inner component contributes exactly its outer vertex, with
the same marks and successors. Projection is an isomorphism.

Flattening a single outer atomic vertex leaves its label unchanged, up
to the finite enumeration of its vertices.

Enumerate the image of the pair consisting of the target and observation.
Choose a preimage for every enumerated pair. Within any fixed target fibre,
the observation is injective on the selected classes.
Only the selected label changes, and its rank is preserved.

At the selected vertex the original letter fills the hole; every other
vertex carries its unchanged ordinary letter.

Mark the selected outer vertex and apply context smallification to its
atomic label. Context evaluation and the unit law identify the original
system and the system with its locally renamed label value.

Color each increasing pair by its interval product and its left prefix
product. Ramsey homogeneity fixes both. Concatenating two homogeneous
intervals proves idempotence, and appending one to a prefix proves stability.

The parity condition is exactly evenness of the unique least recurring
priority of the word automaton's run.

An infinite color class supplies a recurring priority. Choose the least
such natural number; every smaller priority has a last occurrence.

Discard the finitely many occurrences of smaller priorities. Among the
infinitely many occurrences of the least recurring priority, some state
recurs infinitely often. Choose two occurrences after the given bound.

Shift witnesses forward, or choose a witness beyond the omitted prefix
and subtract its length.

Finite context approximation supplies a family of initial and planted
root resolutions. For the converse, choose an unfolding witness for
each proposed yield. Their disjoint family covers the proposed sum and
maps into the original system; yield congruence transfers both maps
through the context.

Transfer initial resolutions through variable-splitting resolutions.
For root yields, expand root entries into starting copies and use covers
to relate their initial resolutions to the original root resolutions.

View the context as an outer pattern. Its ordinary letters have unchanged
atomic labels, and its hole has the given yield inclusion. Apply monotonicity
of flattening, including both initial and root yields.

Compose resolutions for preservation. For a locally surjective map,
pull back a resolution and choose one successor in each direction.
Apply the same argument to roots to obtain preservation of root yields.

Common covers have identical yields. Conversely, a system is one of its
own initial yields, so yield equivalence supplies a common system cover.

Factor the resolution into a flatten-resolution. Transfer its local
resolutions without changing their variable maps, and flatten again.
A common unfolding gives a direct resolution above the original system.
